definition_zh: 人工制品；文物；考古出土器物；（仪器或方法造成的）伪影、人为产物
definition_en: an object made by a person, especially one of historical or cultural interest; also a false feature produced by an instrument or method rather than by the thing being studied
core_image: 一只手把石块敲出刃口，几千年后手早已消失，那块石头还躺在土层里等人编号
scene: 考古系的学生在实验室里给一件石制小刀贴标签，标签上写着它出自哪一层土。An archaeology student labels the artifact, a small stone blade, with the layer it came from.
sceneCN: 这里 artifact 指「由人制作、具有历史或文化价值的实物」（第 1 个义项：经人手加工并作为研究或收藏对象的器物）；句意为学生给这件石制小刀贴上标明出土层位的标签。可辨识物件：石刃、标签纸、卡尺、标本盒、记录本。

pos.zh: 人工制品；文物；出土器物
伪影；人为产物；由方法造成的假象

derivatives.zh: 人工制品（英式拼写，与 artifact 同义）
人工制品的；器物层面的

senses.title: A thing made by human skill
senses.titleCN: 人工制品：人手做出的实物
senses.definition: an object shaped or made by a person rather than formed by nature
senses.definitionCN: 由人加工制作、而非自然形成的实物
senses.example: The museum displays artifacts from the bronze age.
senses.exampleCN: 博物馆展出青铜时代的人工制品。
senses.why: Artifact joins ars, skill or craft, with factum, something made, so the literal reading is a thing made by skill; a natural stone becomes an artifact only after a hand has worked it.
senses.whyCN: artifact 由 ars「技艺、手艺」与 factum「做成之物」合成，字面就是「以手艺做成的东西」；天然石块要等人手加工之后才算 artifact。

senses.title: An excavated find
senses.titleCN: 出土器物：从遗址里取出的古物
senses.definition: a portable object recovered from an archaeological deposit and used to study past behaviour
senses.definitionCN: 从考古堆积中取出、用于研究过去行为的手持器物
senses.example: Fragments of pottery are the most common artifacts at the site.
senses.exampleCN: 陶片是该遗址最常见的出土器物。
senses.why: Archaeology narrows the word to what can be lifted, bagged and numbered; walls and ditches remain features, while movable things become artifacts.
senses.whyCN: 考古学把这个词收窄到能拿起、装袋、编号的物件；墙基与沟槽算遗迹，能移动的东西才叫 artifact。

senses.title: A false result from a method
senses.titleCN: 伪影：仪器或方法造成的假结果
senses.definition: a spurious feature in an observation that comes from the instrument, the sample preparation or the procedure rather than from the subject
senses.definitionCN: 观察中由仪器、样品制备或操作程序造成、并非研究对象本身的虚假特征
senses.example: The dark line on the scan is an artifact of the staining process.
senses.exampleCN: 扫描图上的那条暗线是染色过程造成的伪影。
senses.why: Once making is separated from the object, the word can also name what the procedure made: a mark the method added rather than found.
senses.whyCN: 一旦把「造」与「对象」分开，这个词也能指流程造出来的东西：图像里由方法添上、而非对象本身存在的部分。

senses.title: A digital glitch
senses.titleCN: 数字伪影：压缩或显示产生的杂点
senses.definition: a visible or audible fault introduced by compression, sampling or display rather than present in the original signal
senses.definitionCN: 由压缩、采样或显示引入、原信号中并不存在的可见或可听瑕疵
senses.example: Heavy compression left blocky artifacts around the edges.
senses.exampleCN: 过度压缩在边缘留下了方块状伪影。
senses.why: The scientific sense moved into computing unchanged: the tool chain itself leaves marks that look like part of the picture.
senses.whyCN: 科学的伪影义原样进入计算机领域：工具链自己留下的痕迹，看上去却像画面的一部分。

senses.title: A trace made by the medium
senses.titleCN: 照片上并非实物的影像
senses.definition: a mark on a photograph or film produced by the lens, the sensor or the processing rather than by the scene
senses.definitionCN: 由镜头、传感器或冲洗过程产生、并非场景中实物的影像痕迹
senses.example: The pale spot on the old print is a photographic artifact.
senses.exampleCN: 这张老照片上的浅色斑点是一处摄影伪影。
senses.why: Film and lenses have their own chemistry and geometry; dust, flare and scratches are made by the medium, so the same label fits.
senses.whyCN: 胶片与镜头有自己的化学与几何：灰尘、眩光和划痕是介质造出来的，因此用同一个标签。

senses.title: A byproduct of a system
senses.titleCN: 系统的产物：制度或设计造成的现象
senses.definition: a result that arises from the way a system is built or measured rather than from the thing it claims to describe
senses.definitionCN: 由系统的构造或测量方式产生、而非其所声称描述的对象本身的结果
senses.example: The apparent rise in cases was an artifact of the new reporting rule.
senses.exampleCN: 病例数看似上升，其实是新报告规则造成的产物。
senses.why: Abstracted from instruments, an artifact is any outcome manufactured by the frame: change the frame and the effect disappears.
senses.whyCN: 从仪器义抽象出来后，artifact 指由框架制造的任何结果：换掉框架，效应就消失。

senses.title: Cultural property in a collection
senses.titleCN: 藏品：作为文化财产被收藏的器物
senses.definition: an item held, catalogued and protected as cultural property, often subject to ownership and repatriation rules
senses.definitionCN: 作为文化财产被收藏、编目并保护、常涉及归属与归还规则的器物
senses.example: The government asked for the return of artifacts taken during the war.
senses.exampleCN: 政府要求归还战争期间被取走的文物。
senses.why: The museum and legal sense adds a claim: the object is not only made by humans but is valued as part of a heritage that can be owned.
senses.whyCN: 博物馆与法律义增加了一层主张：这件物品不仅由人制作，还被当作可被拥有的遗产来珍视。

senses.title: The made opposed to the natural
senses.titleCN: 人为之物：与自然物相对的技术造物
senses.definition: anything whose form is produced by human technique, used when contrasting the made with the grown
senses.definitionCN: 形态由人的技术产生之物，用于与自然生成之物对照
senses.example: Philosophers ask whether a city is an artifact or a natural growth.
senses.exampleCN: 哲学家追问城市是人为之物还是自然生长之物。
senses.why: This is the oldest and widest reading: the moment skill shapes material, the result belongs to the class of made things, whatever its size.
senses.whyCN: 这是最古老也最宽的读法：技艺一旦作用于材料，产物就归入「人造之物」，不论其规模大小。

intro.en: Artifact is a Latin phrase turned into one English word: arte, by skill, plus factum, a thing made. It entered English in the seventeenth century as a learned term and only later became the ordinary word for an excavated object. Dates are approximate.
intro.cn: artifact 是把一个拉丁短语压成一个英语词：arte「以技艺」加 factum「做成之物」。它在十七世纪作为学术用语进入英语，后来才成为指称出土器物的常用词。年代均为约数。

items.en: Latin ars, genitive artis, meant skill, craft or technique; the ablative arte means by skill, and it is the form that appears inside artifact.
items.cn: 拉丁 ars（属格 artis）意为技艺、手艺或技术；夺格 arte 意为「以技艺」，正是出现在 artifact 里的形式。

items.en: Facere meant to make or do; its supine factum supplied both the noun thing made and the ending that builds factory, manufacture and factitious.
items.cn: facere 意为制作、做；其目的动名词 factum 既提供名词「做成之物」，也提供构成 factory、manufacture、factitious 的词尾。

items.en: The earliest English records use the word in anatomy and medicine for structures produced by disease or by technique, a sense close to the modern false-result reading.
items.cn: 最早的英语记录把它用在解剖学与医学中，指由疾病或技术造成的结构，这一用法接近现代「假结果」的读法。

items.en: From the nineteenth century the word was applied to the objects of ancient craft, and that museum sense now dominates everyday use.
items.cn: 十九世纪起，这个词被用于古代工艺的制品，这一博物馆义如今在日常使用中占主导。

items.en: American usage settled on artifact, British usage on artefact; both spellings continue the same Latin source and mean the same thing.
items.cn: 美式用法定为 artifact，英式用法定为 artefact；两种拼写都延续同一拉丁来源，意思相同。

items.en: Source uncertain: no attested Latin noun artifactus exists, so the English word is a later combination rather than a direct borrowing, and dictionaries do not name the first author who used it.
items.cn: 来源不确定：拉丁语中并无已证实的名词 artifactus，因此这个英语词属后世组合，而非直接借词；辞书也没有指出最早使用它的作者。

note.en: The first group holds words built on the same Latin stock of skill and making; the second group holds words for objects close in meaning but not made by human hands in the same sense.
note.cn: 第一组是同出拉丁「技艺与制作」词干的词；第二组是意思相近、但并非同样意义上由人手制作的物件。

entries.definition: The same word in British spelling; it is a variant, not a separate term with its own history.
entries.definitionCN: 同一个词的英式拼写，只是变体，并非另有来历的独立术语。

entries.definition: From ars plus facere as well, but it names a clever device or a trick, not the object produced.
entries.definitionCN: 同样由 ars 加 facere 构成，但它指巧妙的装置或诡计，而不是做出来的物件。

entries.definition: The adjective describing something made by skill rather than occurring naturally; it does not name a thing.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，描述由技艺而非自然生成的事物；它并不指称物件本身。

entries.definition: An object that survives from an earlier time, often valued for its age or holiness; the stress is on survival, not on being made.
entries.definitionCN: 从更早时代留存下来的物件，常因年代或神圣性受珍视；重点是「留存」，而非「被制作」。

entries.definition: An item kept as a sample of its kind for study; a specimen may be natural, while an artifact must be made.
entries.definitionCN: 作为同类样本保存以供研究的物件；样本可以是天然的，而人工制品必须由人制作。

entries.definition: Any thing that can be handled; it makes no claim about who made it or why it matters.
entries.definitionCN: 任何可拿取的物；它不主张由谁制作，也不说明为何重要。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: the two real Latin pieces, the archaeology rule, the scientific reversal and the spelling split.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：两个真实的拉丁成分、考古学的区分规则、科学义的反转，以及拼写分歧。

normal.en: ars, skill, plus factum, made: an artifact is literally a thing made by skill.
normal.cn: ars「技艺」加 factum「做成之物」：artifact 字面就是「以技艺做成的东西」。

normal.en: The same ars stock gives art, artifice, artificial and artifact; the same facere stock gives factory, manufacture and factitious.
normal.cn: 同出 ars 的有 art、artifice、artificial、artifact；同出 facere 的有 factory、manufacture、factitious。

normal.en: Field rule: if it can be bagged and numbered, it is an artifact; if it stays in the ground, it is a feature.
normal.cn: 田野规则：能装袋编号的叫器物；留在地里不动的叫遗迹。

normal.en: The scientific sense reverses the maker: there the instrument makes the mark, not the hand.
normal.cn: 科学义把制作者换了人：那里留下痕迹的是仪器，不是手。

normal.en: American artifact, British artefact; the meaning does not change with the spelling.
normal.cn: 美式 artifact，英式 artefact；意思不随拼写改变。

abstract.en: Abstractly, an artifact is anything a system adds to its own picture, including the distortion in the lens.
abstract.cn: 抽象地看，artifact 是任何系统添进自身图景的东西，包括镜头里的畸变。

abstract.en: Every made thing carries a signature of its maker, which is why artifacts can be read as evidence.
abstract.cn: 每一件人造之物都带着制作者的签名，正因如此器物才能被当作证据来读。

abstract.en: The word keeps asking one question: was this shaped, or did it grow?
abstract.cn: 这个词始终在追问一件事：它是被塑造的，还是自己长成的？

examples.en: Radiocarbon dating placed the artifact at about three thousand years old.
examples.cn: 放射性碳测年把这件器物的年代定在约三千年前。

examples.en: The ring around the star in the image is an optical artifact, not a real structure.
examples.cn: 图像中恒星周围的光环是光学伪影，并非真实结构。

examples.en: Researchers must separate the artifact of the measuring device from the signal they want.
examples.cn: 研究者必须把测量仪器造成的伪影与真正想要的信号区分开。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「艺术（art）+ 事实（fact）」——用艺术手艺做出来的实体 → 人工制品、文物

root: 拉丁 ars/artis「技艺」的夺格 arte「以技艺」+ factum「做成之物」（facere「制作」的目的动名词）；字面为「以技艺做成之物」。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses follow one gesture: a hand works material into a thing, and that thing is then dug up, faked by an instrument, produced by a system and finally owned as heritage.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项沿同一个动作展开：人手把材料做成物件，这件物件随后被挖出、被仪器伪造、被系统产出，最后被当作遗产拥有。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a hand shaping stone, and the shaped stone outliving the hand.
core.cn: 核心意象：一只手把石头打出形状，而被塑形的石头比手活得更久。

branches.en: MAKING ITSELF: craft applied to stuff is the root sense, and the broad contrast with nature is only its widest form.
branches.cn: 制作本身：技艺作用于材料是根义，与自然相对只是它最宽的形态。

branches.en: THE KEPT OBJECT: once lifted and numbered, a made thing becomes evidence, and once owned it becomes heritage.
branches.cn: 被保存的物件：被取出编号后成为证据，被拥有后成为遗产。

branches.en: THE INSTRUMENT MAKES TOO: the method adds a mark of its own, and the same logic explains digital faults.
branches.cn: 仪器也在制作：方法自己添上一道痕迹，同一逻辑解释了数字瑕疵。

branches.en: THE MEDIUM LEAVES TRACES: lens, film and sensor write on the image as surely as a hand writes on clay.
branches.cn: 介质留下痕迹：镜头、胶片与传感器在影像上书写，如同手在陶土上书写。

branches.en: THE FRAME INVENTS: abstracted once more, any system can manufacture an effect that vanishes when its frame is changed.
branches.cn: 框架会发明：再抽象一层，任何系统都能制造出换掉框架就消失的效应。

intro.en: Artifact is built from two Latin pieces that also build a large English family, so the word can be read morpheme by morpheme: skill plus making.
intro.cn: artifact 由两个拉丁成分构成，这两个成分还构成一大批英语词，因此可以逐语素读出：技艺加制作。

latinIntro.en: Latin ars, genitive artis, gives art, artist, artifice and artificial; Latin facere gives fact, factory, manufacture and factitious. The artifact family sits exactly where the two meet.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁 ars（属格 artis）衍生 art、artist、artifice、artificial；拉丁 facere 衍生 fact、factory、manufacture、factitious。artifact 一族正处在这两条线的交点上。

items.example: Ars in Latin covered both craft and cunning.
items.exampleCN: 拉丁语 ars 兼指手艺与机巧。

items.structure: art (English, from Latin ars through Old French)
items.meaning: the practice of skill, especially in making or expressing
items.meaningCN: 技艺的实践，尤指制作或表达上的
items.example: The art of stone working changed human history.
items.exampleCN: 石作技艺改变了人类历史。

items.structure: artifice (Latin ars + facere, a thing made by skill)
items.meaning: a clever device or a trick
items.example: The lock was an artifice of great subtlety.
items.exampleCN: 这把锁是一件极为精巧的装置。

items.meaning: made by human skill rather than occurring naturally
items.meaningCN: 由人的技艺制成而非自然生成
items.example: Artificial light changed the working day.
items.exampleCN: 人造光改变了工作日。

items.structure: facere (Latin verb, to make, to do)
items.example: Facere is the source of many English -fect and -fact words.
items.exampleCN: facere 是许多英语 -fect 与 -fact 词的来源。

items.structure: factum (Latin supine of facere, a thing made)
items.example: Factum gave English fact its earliest sense of a deed.
items.exampleCN: factum 给英语 fact 最早的「行为、事迹」义。

items.structure: fact (English, from Latin factum, a thing done)
items.meaning: something that is the case, originally a deed
items.example: The fact was recorded before any theory was proposed.
items.exampleCN: 事实在提出任何理论之前就已被记录。

items.structure: factory (Latin factorium, a place of making)
items.meaning: a building where goods are made
items.example: The factory produced pottery for the whole province.
items.exampleCN: 这家工厂为全省生产陶器。

items.meaning: to make goods, originally by hand
items.meaningCN: 制造货物，原指用手制作
items.example: They manufacture the blades from local flint.
items.exampleCN: 他们用当地燧石制造石刃。

items.meaning: artificially produced, often in a false way
items.meaningCN: 人为制造的，常带虚假意味
items.example: A factitious glow came from the treated surface.
items.exampleCN: 处理过的表面发出一种人为的光。

latinEntries.structure: facere (Latin verb, to make, to do)

definition_zh: 人工制品（英式拼写，等于 artifact）；文物；出土器物；伪影
definition_en: the British spelling of artifact: an object made by a person, especially one of historical interest, or a false feature produced by an instrument
core_image: 同一块打制石片出现在两本图录里，一本按英式拼写，一本按美式拼写，指的都是它
scene: 英式考古报告的前言里，编辑把全文的「人工制品」一词统一成英式拼写，并在注释里说明它与美式写法指同一事物。The British editor standardises artefact throughout the report and notes that it equals the American spelling.
sceneCN: 这里 artefact 指「人工制品」这一概念本身，只是采用英式拼写（第 1 个义项：由人制作、供研究或收藏的实物）；句意为编辑把报告里的人工制品一词统一为英式写法并注明与美式同义。可辨识物件：清样稿、红笔、拼写表、注释框、校样夹。

pos.zh: 人工制品；文物；出土器物（英式拼写）
伪影；人为产物（英式拼写）

senses.title: British spelling of a made object
senses.titleCN: 人工制品：英式拼写下的同一概念
senses.definition: an object made by human skill, written with the British spelling
senses.definitionCN: 由人的技艺制作的实物，采用英式拼写
senses.example: The catalogue lists every artefact by period and material.
senses.exampleCN: 图录按年代与材质列出每一件人工制品。
senses.why: The word is the same Latin combination as artifact, arte plus factum; British orthography kept the -e- of arte, while American usage dropped it.
senses.whyCN: 这个词与 artifact 是同一个拉丁组合 arte 加 factum；英式正字保留了 arte 中的 -e-，美式则将其省略。

senses.title: An excavated find in British reports
senses.titleCN: 出土器物：英式报告中的考古发现
senses.definition: a portable object recovered from an archaeological deposit, as recorded in British field reports
senses.definitionCN: 从考古堆积中取出的手持器物，见于英式田野报告
senses.example: Each artefact was bagged with its context number.
senses.exampleCN: 每件出土器物都连同其层位编号一起装袋。
senses.why: British archaeology writes artefact where American archaeology writes artifact; the field procedure behind the word is identical.
senses.whyCN: 英式考古写作 artefact，美式考古写作 artifact；这个词背后的田野程序完全相同。

senses.title: A handling mark in a specimen
senses.titleCN: 标本上由操作留下的痕迹
senses.definition: a distortion in a prepared specimen caused by cutting, staining or handling rather than by the tissue itself
senses.definitionCN: 制备标本时由切片、染色或操作造成、而非组织本身的畸变
senses.example: The fold in the section is a preparation artefact.
senses.exampleCN: 切片上的褶皱是制备过程造成的伪影。
senses.why: In microscopy the word marks whatever the preparative steps added, and British histology reports spell that artefact.
senses.whyCN: 在显微观察中，这个词标记制备步骤添上的东西，英式组织学报告把它拼作 artefact。

senses.title: A scanning fault in medical imaging
senses.titleCN: 医学影像中的扫描伪影
senses.definition: a false signal in a scan produced by the scanner, motion or reconstruction rather than by the body
senses.definitionCN: 扫描中由机器、运动或重建产生、而非身体本身的虚假信号
senses.example: Motion during the scan produced a bright artefact.
senses.exampleCN: 扫描时的移动产生了一处明亮伪影。
senses.why: The same false-result reading appears in British radiology writing, where artefact is the standard spelling.
senses.whyCN: 同一「假结果」读法出现在英式放射学写作中，那里 artefact 是标准拼写。

senses.title: A compression fault in audio
senses.titleCN: 音频压缩产生的杂音
senses.definition: an audible impurity introduced by compression or sampling rather than present in the recording
senses.definitionCN: 由压缩或采样引入、录音中并不存在的可听杂质
senses.example: The whistle at the end is a codec artefact.
senses.exampleCN: 结尾处的啸声是编解码器造成的伪影。
senses.why: Digital signal processing borrowed the word, and British technical writing kept the artefact spelling.
senses.whyCN: 数字信号处理借用了这个词，英式技术写作保留了 artefact 拼写。

senses.title: A bias introduced by procedure
senses.titleCN: 实验流程引入的偏差
senses.definition: a result in an experiment that comes from the way the study was set up rather than from the effect being tested
senses.definitionCN: 实验中由研究设计方式产生、而非所测效应本身的结果
senses.example: The apparent effect was an artefact of the sampling method.
senses.exampleCN: 看似存在的效应其实是抽样方法造成的偏差。
senses.why: Here the word names what the procedure manufactured; the British spelling carries the abstract sense just as artifact does.
senses.whyCN: 这里这个词指流程制造出来的东西；英式拼写与 artifact 一样承载这一抽象义。

senses.title: A cultural object in a museum record
senses.titleCN: 博物馆记录中的文化器物
senses.definition: an item catalogued as cultural property, often with a recorded provenance
senses.definitionCN: 作为文化财产编目的物品，通常附有来源记录
senses.example: The museum returned the artefact to its country of origin.
senses.exampleCN: 博物馆把这件文物归还给原产国。
senses.why: British institutions use artefact in provenance and repatriation files, where the object is treated as heritage rather than as evidence.
senses.whyCN: 英式机构在来源与归还档案中使用 artefact，那里物件被当作遗产而非证据。

senses.title: The made opposed to the natural
senses.titleCN: 人为之物：与自然物相对
senses.definition: anything whose form comes from human technique, used in contrast with what grows by itself
senses.definitionCN: 形态来自人的技术之物，用于与自行生长之物对照
senses.example: A hedgerow may be an artefact of centuries of grazing.
senses.exampleCN: 一条树篱可能是数百年放牧造成的人为产物。
senses.why: The widest reading survives in British writing too: skill shapes material, and the shaped result is an artefact whatever its size.
senses.whyCN: 最宽的读法在英式写作中同样存在：技艺塑造材料，被塑造的结果不论大小都是 artefact。

intro.en: Artefact is not a separate word but the British spelling of artifact, built from Latin arte, by skill, and factum, a thing made. Dates are approximate.
intro.cn: artefact 不是另一个词，而是 artifact 的英式拼写，由拉丁 arte「以技艺」与 factum「做成之物」构成。年代均为约数。

items.en: The ablative arte, from ars, artis, means by skill or by craft; it is the form that survived inside the British spelling.
items.cn: 夺格 arte 出自 ars（属格 artis），意为「以技艺、以手艺」；它正是英式拼写中保留下来的形式。

items.en: Factum, the supine of facere, means a thing made or done and supplies the second half of both spellings.
items.cn: factum 是 facere 的目的动名词，意为做成之物或做成之事，提供两种拼写的后半部分。

items.en: British dictionaries fixed artefact while American ones fixed artifact; the difference is spelling policy, not a difference in origin.
items.cn: 英国辞书定为 artefact，美国辞书定为 artifact；差别是正字政策，而非来源不同。

items.en: British scientific writing extended artefact to false results in imaging and experiments, exactly as American writing did with artifact.
items.cn: 英式科学写作把 artefact 扩展到成像与实验中的假结果，与美式写作对 artifact 的扩展完全平行。

items.en: Source uncertain: the exact date at which the -e- spelling became standard in Britain is not fixed by any single authority, and early printed texts show both forms.
items.cn: 来源不确定：-e- 拼写在英国成为标准的确切年代并无单一权威定论，早期印刷文本中两种形式都出现过。

note.en: The first group holds spelling variants and words from the same Latin stock; the second group holds nearby nouns for objects.
note.cn: 第一组是拼写变体与同出拉丁词干的词；第二组是邻近的物件名词。

entries.definition: The identical word in American spelling; no difference in meaning or history.
entries.definitionCN: 同一个词的美式拼写；意义与来历均无差别。

entries.definition: Built from the same Latin pieces but naming cleverness itself, not the object made.
entries.definitionCN: 同出拉丁成分，但指机巧本身，而不是做成的物件。

entries.definition: The British adjective meaning of or relating to an artefact; it cannot stand as the noun.
entries.definitionCN: 英式形容词，意为人工制品的或与器物有关的；不能充当名词。

entries.definition: Something that has survived from an earlier age; survival, not manufacture, is what the word stresses.
entries.definitionCN: 从更早时代留存下来的东西；这个词强调的是留存，而非制作。

entries.definition: A sample kept for examination; it need not be made by humans.
entries.definitionCN: 留作检验的样本；不一定由人制作。

entries.definition: An object as discovered in the ground, before it is cleaned and catalogued as an artefact.
entries.definitionCN: 刚在地里发现、尚未清理编目为器物的物件。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: the British -e-, the shared Latin pieces, and the parallel scientific senses.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：英式拼写里的 -e-、共有的拉丁成分，以及平行的科学义。

normal.en: British artefact keeps the -e- of Latin arte, by skill; American artifact drops it.
normal.cn: 英式 artefact 保留拉丁 arte「以技艺」中的 -e-；美式 artifact 则省略。

normal.en: Both spellings are the same combination: skill plus a thing made.
normal.cn: 两种拼写都是同一个组合：技艺加做成之物。

normal.en: British field reports bag and number artefacts; American reports bag and number artifacts.
normal.cn: 英式田野报告给 artefact 装袋编号；美式报告给 artifact 装袋编号。

normal.en: The imaging sense is identical on both sides of the Atlantic: the scanner writes the artefact.
normal.cn: 大西洋两岸的成像义完全相同：伪影是扫描仪写下的。

normal.en: If a text mixes artefact and artifact, check its publisher before assuming two different things.
normal.cn: 如果一篇文章同时出现 artefact 与 artifact，先查出版方，不要以为它们指两样东西。

abstract.en: Abstractly, the two spellings show that a word can split in form while staying one in meaning.
abstract.cn: 抽象地看，两种拼写说明一个词可以在形式上分家，而在意义上仍是同一个。

abstract.en: An artefact is still evidence of a hand, whatever letters we use to name it.
abstract.cn: 无论用哪套字母称呼它，人工制品仍然是手存在过的证据。

abstract.en: The false-result sense reminds us that the observer is also a maker.
abstract.cn: 假结果义提醒我们：观察者本身也是制造者。

examples.en: The report describes each artefact in the order it was recovered.
examples.cn: 报告按器物取出的顺序逐一描述。

examples.en: Reviewers asked the authors to distinguish artefact from genuine structure in the images.
examples.cn: 审稿人要求作者区分图像中的伪影与真实结构。

examples.en: British law treats an artefact of national importance as protected heritage.
examples.cn: 英国法律把具有国家重要性的文物视为受保护的遗产。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「art（艺术）+ e + fact（事实）」——英式多留一个 e，本质还是「用技艺做成的实物」→ 人工制品

root: 拉丁 arte「以技艺」（ars/artis 的夺格）+ factum「做成之物」；与 artifact 同源同义，仅拼写体系不同。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses repeat the artifact pattern in British spelling: the made object, the excavated find, the instrument's false mark, the system's byproduct and the owned heritage.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项以英式拼写重演 artifact 的模式：人造之物、出土发现、仪器假痕、系统产物与被拥有的遗产。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: one shaped stone appearing in two catalogues under two spellings.
core.cn: 核心意象：同一块被塑形的石头，以两种拼写出现在两本图录里。

branches.en: THE SAME CORE: the British spelling covers the root sense and the widest contrast with nature without changing meaning.
branches.cn: 同一核心：英式拼写覆盖根义与最宽的自然对照义，意义不变。

branches.en: FROM GROUND TO MUSEUM: a find becomes evidence in the field and heritage in the catalogue.
branches.cn: 从泥土到博物馆：发现物在田野成为证据，在图录里成为遗产。

branches.en: THE TOOL WRITES BACK: preparation and scanning add marks that the body did not produce.
branches.cn: 工具反写：制备与扫描添上身体并未产生的痕迹。

branches.en: THE CODEC'S WHISTLE: compression leaves a sound that was never recorded.
branches.cn: 编解码器的啸声：压缩留下从未被录下的声音。

branches.en: THE DESIGN'S EFFECT: a study can manufacture the very effect it claims to measure.
branches.cn: 设计的效应：研究可能制造出它声称要测量的那个效应。

intro.en: Artefact shares artifact's Latin pieces exactly, and the British spelling preserves the ablative arte more visibly.
intro.cn: artefact 与 artifact 的拉丁成分完全相同，而英式拼写更明显地保留了夺格 arte。

latinIntro.en: Latin ars, artis gives the arte- half; Latin facere, factum gives the -fact half. The same two roots build art, artifice, artificial, fact, factory and manufacture.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁 ars（属格 artis）提供 arte- 部分；拉丁 facere、factum 提供 -fact 部分。同两个词根构成 art、artifice、artificial、fact、factory、manufacture。

items.example: Ars covered both making and cunning in Latin.
items.exampleCN: 拉丁语 ars 兼指制作与机巧。

items.example: The phrase arte factum means made by skill.
items.exampleCN: 短语 arte factum 意为以技艺做成。

items.structure: art (English, from Latin ars via Old French)
items.example: Stone working was a high art long before writing.
items.exampleCN: 远在文字出现之前，石作已是高超技艺。

items.example: The mechanism was an artifice of great precision.
items.exampleCN: 这个机构是一件极为精密的装置。

items.meaningCN: 非自然的、由技艺制成的
items.example: Artificial materials now mimic stone.
items.exampleCN: 人造材料如今可以仿制石头。

items.example: Facere stands behind many English verbs in -fy.
items.exampleCN: facere 是许多英语 -fy 动词的来源。

items.example: Factum is the source of English fact.
items.exampleCN: factum 是英语 fact 的来源。

items.meaningCN: 做过的事，后指真实之事
items.example: The fact was established by measurement.
items.exampleCN: 这一事实由测量确立。

items.meaning: a place where things are made
items.example: The factory fired clay at high temperature.
items.exampleCN: 这家工厂高温烧制陶土。

items.example: They manufacture replicas for museums.
items.exampleCN: 他们为博物馆制造复制品。

definition_zh: 遗物；遗迹；圣髑；遗风；残存物
definition_en: an object or custom that has survived from an earlier time, especially one kept for its age, holiness or historical value
core_image: 一座废弃教堂的墙角还立着半截石柱，周围是新盖的楼，只有它停在旧年代里
scene: 山间小教堂的祭坛上放着一只旧木匣，匣里是一块据说是古代圣徒的遗骨。On the altar of the mountain chapel lies an old wooden casket holding a relic said to be the bone of an ancient saint.
sceneCN: 这里 relic 指「因年代久远或神圣性而被保存下来的遗物」（第 3 个义项：宗教传统中被尊崇的圣髑）；句意为小教堂祭坛上的木匣里存放着一块据称属于古代圣徒的遗骨。可辨识物件：木匣、祭坛布、烛台、石墙、铁锁。

pos.zh: 遗物；遗迹；圣髑；遗风；残存物
（复数 relics）遗骸；残存遗迹

collocations.zh: 过去的遗物；旧时代的残留

senses.title: An object surviving from the past
senses.titleCN: 遗物：从过去留存下来的物件
senses.definition: a thing that has survived from an earlier period and is valued for that survival
senses.definitionCN: 从更早时期留存下来、并因留存本身而受珍视的东西
senses.example: The sword is the last relic of the old castle.
senses.exampleCN: 这把剑是那座古堡最后的遗物。
senses.why: Relic comes from Latin reliquiae, the things left behind, from relinquere, to leave behind; the word begins with a departure.
senses.whyCN: relic 出自拉丁 reliquiae「留下之物」，源于 relinquere「留在身后」；这个词的起点就是一场离去。

senses.title: A ruin of an old structure
senses.titleCN: 遗迹：旧建筑的残存部分
senses.definition: a remaining part of a building or place from an earlier age
senses.definitionCN: 更早时代的建筑或场所残存下来的部分
senses.example: A single arch is the only relic of the abbey.
senses.exampleCN: 一座孤拱是这座修道院仅存的遗迹。
senses.why: A building leaves fragments behind when it falls; those fragments are literally what remains, so the same noun covers stone as well as portable objects.
senses.whyCN: 建筑倒塌时会留下碎片；这些碎片字面上就是「留下的东西」，因此同一个名词既指石块，也指可携带的物件。

senses.title: A sacred bodily remnant
senses.titleCN: 圣髑：宗教中被尊崇的遗骨或遗物
senses.definition: a part of a saint's body or a object connected with a holy person, kept for veneration
senses.definitionCN: 圣徒身体的一部分或与其相关的物品，保存以供敬礼
senses.example: Pilgrims travelled for weeks to see the relic.
senses.exampleCN: 朝圣者走了数周，只为看一眼这件圣髑。
senses.why: In religious use the left-behind object is specifically what death left: bone, cloth or a possession, and the value comes from contact with the holy person.
senses.whyCN: 在宗教用法中，留下的东西具体指死亡留下的部分：骨骸、衣物或随身物；价值来自与圣人的接触。

senses.title: A surviving custom or idea
senses.titleCN: 遗风：旧习俗或旧观念的残存
senses.definition: a practice or belief that continues from an earlier era although its original setting has gone
senses.definitionCN: 从更早时代延续下来、而原初环境已消失的做法或观念
senses.example: The rule is a relic of a time when horses set the speed of travel.
senses.exampleCN: 这条规定是马车决定出行速度那个时代的遗风。
senses.why: Once the word means what is left after something ends, it can name customs as easily as stones: the institution ended, the habit stayed.
senses.whyCN: 一旦这个词指某事物结束后的残留，它就能像指石头一样指习俗：制度终结了，习惯还留着。

senses.title: A personal keepsake
senses.titleCN: 纪念物：与逝者或往事相关的私人物品
senses.definition: an object kept for its connection with a person or period, often of little material value
senses.definitionCN: 因与某人或某段时期有关而保存的物品，常无多少物质价值
senses.example: She kept the old ticket as a relic of their first meeting.
senses.exampleCN: 她把那张旧车票留作他们初次见面的纪念物。
senses.why: The religious sense strips its holiness and leaves the structure: an object that carries contact with an absent person.
senses.whyCN: 去掉神圣性之后，宗教义的结构仍然在：一件承载着与不在场者之接触的物品。

senses.title: An antique or curiosity
senses.titleCN: 古董：因年代而被收藏的旧物
senses.definition: an old object collected or traded for its age and rarity
senses.definitionCN: 因年代与稀有而被收藏或交易的旧物
senses.example: The shop sells relics of the steam age.
senses.exampleCN: 这家店出售蒸汽时代的旧物。
senses.why: Market value attaches to age, so a relic becomes a category of goods; the word now labels a trade as well as a devotion.
senses.whyCN: 市场把价值附着在年代上，于是 relic 成为一种货品类别；这个词既标记虔敬，也标记买卖。

senses.title: Remains of a dead person
senses.titleCN: 遗骸：逝者留下的身体部分
senses.definition: the bodily remains of a dead person, usually in the plural relics or remains
senses.definitionCN: 逝者留下的身体部分，通常用复数 relics 或 remains
senses.example: The relics were buried again after the excavation.
senses.exampleCN: 发掘结束后，遗骸被重新安葬。
senses.why: This is the plainest reading of what is left behind: the body itself, which is why the plural form often appears in burial accounts.
senses.whyCN: 这是「留下之物」最朴素的读法：身体本身，因此复数形式常出现在安葬记述中。

senses.title: Something hopelessly outdated
senses.titleCN: 过时之物：被时代甩下的东西
senses.definition: a person, rule or device regarded as absurdly out of date
senses.definitionCN: 被视为荒唐过时的人、规定或装置
senses.example: The fax machine is a relic in most offices.
senses.exampleCN: 在多数办公室里，传真机已是过时之物。
senses.why: Survival can also be an accusation: if only the obsolete survives, the survivor becomes evidence of decay rather than of value.
senses.whyCN: 留存也可以成为一种指控：若只有被淘汰者留下，留存者就成了衰败的证据，而非价值的证据。

intro.en: Relic reached English through Old French from Latin reliquiae, the things left behind, a plural noun from relinquere, to leave behind. The religious sense came first in English use. Dates are approximate.
intro.cn: relic 经古法语来自拉丁 reliquiae「留下之物」，这是由 relinquere「留在身后」派生的复数名词。英语中最早出现的是宗教义。年代均为约数。

items.en: Relinquere means to leave behind or abandon, built from re-, back, and linquere, to leave; its participle reliquus means left over.
items.cn: relinquere 意为留在身后或舍弃，由 re-「向后」与 linquere「离开」构成；其分词 reliquus 意为剩下的。

items.en: The plural reliquiae named what remains after a person or thing is gone, and in church Latin it specialised to the bodily remains of a saint.
items.cn: 复数 reliquiae 指人或物消失后留下的东西，在教会拉丁语中专门指圣徒的遗骸。

items.en: Old French relique carried the devotional sense into English after the Norman period, and the plural relics covered bones, cloth and associated objects.
items.cn: 古法语 relique 在诺曼时期之后把敬礼义带入英语，复数 relics 涵盖骨骸、衣物与相关物品。

items.en: From the sixteenth century the word widened to ruins, surviving customs and old objects in general, while the sacred sense stayed alive.
items.cn: 十六世纪起，这个词扩展到废墟、残存习俗与一般旧物，同时神圣义仍然存活。

items.en: Source uncertain: the deeper origin of linquere is not established beyond the Latin family, and the competing link to a Greek verb meaning to leave is a hypothesis rather than a demonstrated relation.
items.cn: 来源不确定：linquere 在拉丁语族之外的更深来源未有定论；把它与某个意为「离开」的希腊动词相联系的另一种说法只是假说，并非已证实的关联。

note.en: The first group holds words that look or sound close and share the leaving-behind idea; the second group holds nouns for old surviving things.
note.cn: 第一组是形音相近、并共享「留下」观念的单词；第二组是指旧日留存物的名词。

entries.definition: A technical term for a species or feature surviving from an earlier environment; relic is the everyday word for the object.
entries.definitionCN: 指从更早环境残存下来的物种或地貌的技术术语；relic 是日常指物件的词。

entries.definition: The verb built on the same linquere, meaning to give up or let go; a relic is what was relinquished.
entries.definitionCN: 同出 linquere 的动词，意为放弃或放手；遗物就是被放手的东西。

entries.definition: From de- plus relinquere, meaning wholly abandoned; it describes the state, not the surviving object.
entries.definitionCN: 由 de- 加 relinquere 构成，意为被彻底弃置；它描述状态，而非留存物。

entries.definition: The general plural for whatever is left of a body, building or meal; relic usually adds age or reverence.
entries.definitionCN: 泛指身体、建筑或饭菜剩下的部分；relic 通常额外带有年代或敬意。

entries.definition: An object kept to remember a person or event; it stresses the memory, not the survival.
entries.definitionCN: 为记住某人或某事而保存的物品；它强调记忆，而非留存。

entries.definition: An old object valued in the market for its age; the word implies commerce, while relic implies devotion or history.
entries.definitionCN: 因年代在市场上受重视的旧物；该词含买卖意味，而 relic 含虔敬或历史意味。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: the leaving-behind verb, the church sense, the ruins and the modern insult.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：表示「留下」的动词、教会义、废墟义，以及现代的贬义。

normal.en: relinquere, to leave behind, gives reliquiae, the things left behind: a relic is a left-behind thing.
normal.cn: relinquere「留在身后」派生 reliquiae「留下之物」：relic 就是被留下的东西。

normal.en: The first English sense was devotional: bones, cloth and possessions of a saint.
normal.cn: 英语最早的义项是宗教性的：圣徒的骨骸、衣物与随身物。

normal.en: The plural relics covers both holy objects and human remains.
normal.cn: 复数 relics 既指神圣物件，也指人的遗骸。

normal.en: A ruin is a relic of a building; a custom can be a relic of an institution.
normal.cn: 废墟是建筑的遗物；习俗可以是某个制度的遗风。

normal.en: Calling a device a relic is an insult about its age, not praise for its survival.
normal.cn: 把某装置称作 relic，是在讥其老旧，而不是赞美它留存下来。

abstract.en: Abstractly, a relic is proof that a departure happened: the object marks an absence.
abstract.cn: 抽象地看，遗物是「离去曾发生」的证明：物件标记着一处缺席。

abstract.en: Value attaches to the link, not the material: a bone and a stone differ only in who touched them.
abstract.cn: 价值附着在联系上，而不在材料上：一块骨与一块石，差别只在谁曾触碰过。

abstract.en: Every survival carries a question: is this kept because it still works, or only because it is old?
abstract.cn: 每一种留存都带来一个问题：它被留着是因为仍然有用，还是只因它够老？

examples.en: The mosaics are the finest relic of the settlement's wealthy period.
examples.cn: 这些镶嵌画是该聚落富庶时期最精美的遗物。

examples.en: The procession carries the relic through the streets once a year.
examples.cn: 每年一次，游行队伍抬着这件圣髑穿过街道。

examples.en: Many archaeologists treat such rules as relics of an older recording system.
examples.cn: 许多考古学者把这类规定视为旧记录体系的残留。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「re（回）+ lic（留下）」——人走了，东西留在原地 → 遗物、遗迹

root: 拉丁 relinquere「留在身后」的派生名词 reliquiae「留下之物」，经古法语 relique 进入英语；词根 linquere 意为「离开」。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses follow one departure: what is left behind may be an object, a ruin, a saint's bone, a custom, a keepsake, a curiosity, a body or an absurdly outdated thing.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项沿一场离去展开：留下的可以是物件、废墟、圣人骨骸、习俗、纪念物、古董、遗体，或一件荒唐过时的东西。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a departure, and one object still standing where the person used to be.
core.cn: 核心意象：一场离去，以及原来有人之处仍立着的一件物件。

branches.en: THE LEFT-BEHIND THING: portable objects and standing ruins are both simply what the past did not take away.
branches.cn: 留下之物：可携带的物件与仍立的废墟，都只是过去没有带走的东西。

branches.en: CONTACT WITH THE ABSENT: a saint's bone and a body both keep the person present through matter.
branches.cn: 与缺席者的接触：圣徒的骨与遗体都借物质让人继续在场。

branches.en: THE HABIT OUTLASTS THE INSTITUTION: customs remain after the world that made them is gone.
branches.cn: 习惯比制度活得久：造出习俗的世界消失后，习俗仍在。

branches.en: KEEPING AND TRADING: the same old object can be a private memory or a priced curiosity.
branches.cn: 保存与买卖：同一件旧物既可以是私人记忆，也可以是被标价的古董。

branches.en: SURVIVAL AS INSULT: what outlives its use turns from treasure into evidence of decay.
branches.cn: 留存成为讥讽：活得超过用途的东西，从珍宝变成衰败的证据。

intro.en: Relic is a single Latin-derived noun whose stem also builds a small family of English words about leaving things behind.
intro.cn: relic 是一个拉丁来源的名词，其词干还构成一小族表示「留下」的英语词。

latinIntro.en: Latin relinquere, to leave behind, yields reliquiae and its English descendants relic and relics, plus relinquish and derelict, which keep the verbal force of leaving.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁 relinquere「留在身后」派生 reliquiae，其英语后裔有 relic、relics，以及保留「离开」动词力量的 relinquish 与 derelict。

items.example: The prefix marks motion away and back in many Latin verbs.
items.exampleCN: 这个前缀在许多拉丁动词中标记离开与返回的运动。

items.example: Linquere is the root of relinquish and derelict.
items.exampleCN: linquere 是 relinquish 与 derelict 的词根。

items.example: The army relinquished the fort at dawn.
items.exampleCN: 军队在黎明时弃守了堡垒。

items.example: Reliquiae covered bones, ruins and leftovers alike.
items.exampleCN: reliquiae 兼指骨骸、废墟与剩余物。

items.example: The relic was catalogued as twelfth-century work.
items.exampleCN: 这件遗物被编目为十二世纪的作品。

items.example: The relics were reburied with ceremony.
items.exampleCN: 遗骸被以仪式重新安葬。

items.meaning: a species or feature surviving from an earlier age
items.meaningCN: 从更早时代残存的物种或地貌
items.example: The lake holds relict species from the ice age.
items.exampleCN: 这座湖中有冰期残遗物种。

items.meaning: to give up or let go
items.example: She relinquished her claim to the land.
items.exampleCN: 她放弃了对这块土地的主张。

items.example: The derelict warehouse became a studio.
items.exampleCN: 那座废弃仓库变成了工作室。

items.meaning: a container for a sacred relic
items.example: The reliquary is kept in the cathedral treasury.
items.exampleCN: 这只圣髑匣保存在主教座堂的宝库里。

definition_zh: 遗骸；遗迹；剩余物；残羹剩饭；遗存
definition_en: the parts of a person, building, meal or material that are left after the rest has gone or been used
core_image: 火烧过的屋子里只剩半面墙和一层灰，别的都已经被带走或烧尽
scene: 清理火灾现场的人蹲在墙角，把烧焦的梁木和灰烬一起装进袋里登记。Investigators bag the remains of the burnt beam and the ash that lay beneath it.
sceneCN: 这里 remains 指「某物被毁或消失后剩下的部分」（第 2 个义项：建筑或物体残存下来的碎块）；句意为调查人员把烧焦的梁木残段与下面的灰烬一起装袋登记。可辨识物件：焦木、灰堆、证物袋、手套、记录板。

pos.zh: 遗骸；遗迹；剩余物；残羹剩饭（复数名词）
（remains of）……的残迹、遗存

forms.label: 单数形式（罕用，指一件残存物）

senses.title: A dead body
senses.titleCN: 遗骸：逝者留下的身体
senses.definition: the body or bones of a dead person or animal
senses.definitionCN: 死者或死去的动物留下的身体或骨骸
senses.example: The remains were identified by dental records.
senses.exampleCN: 遗骸通过牙科记录得到确认。
senses.why: Remain means to stay behind; when a person dies, what stays behind is the body, so the plural noun became the respectful word for it.
senses.whyCN: remain 意为「留下」；人死后留下的就是身体，因此复数名词成为指称遗体的敬语。

senses.title: What is left of a structure
senses.titleCN: 残迹：建筑或物体剩下的部分
senses.definition: the surviving pieces of a building, object or place after damage or decay
senses.definitionCN: 建筑、物体或场所在损毁或衰败后仍存留的部分
senses.example: Only the foundations remain as the remains of the temple.
senses.exampleCN: 这座神庙的残迹只剩地基。
senses.why: A structure that falls does not vanish; part of it stays, and the plural gathers those pieces into one noun.
senses.whyCN: 倒塌的建筑不会凭空消失；总有一部分留着，复数形式把这些碎片收拢成一个名词。

senses.title: The leftover part
senses.titleCN: 剩余部分：用掉或分掉之后剩下的量
senses.definition: the part of something that is left over after the rest has been used, taken or divided
senses.definitionCN: 某物在其余部分被使用、取走或分配之后剩余的部分
senses.example: The remains of the fund were transferred to a new project.
senses.exampleCN: 基金的剩余部分被转到新项目。
senses.why: The core verb simply states that something stays; applied to quantities, that means subtraction, and the noun names the result.
senses.whyCN: 核心动词只表示「某物留下」；用于数量时，这就意味着减法，名词便指减法的结果。

senses.title: Food left on the table
senses.titleCN: 残羹剩饭：用餐后剩下的食物
senses.definition: food that is left uneaten after a meal
senses.definitionCN: 一餐之后未被吃完的食物
senses.example: The dogs finished the remains of the roast.
senses.exampleCN: 狗把烤肉的残渣吃光了。
senses.why: The same subtraction applied to a meal: what the eaters did not take stays on the plate, and the word turns it into a noun.
senses.whyCN: 同一减法用于一餐：食客没有取走的部分留在盘里，这个词把它变成名词。

senses.title: Archaeological deposits
senses.titleCN: 考古遗存：遗址中留存下来的物质
senses.definition: the material traces of past human activity preserved in the ground
senses.definitionCN: 保存在地下、过去人类活动的物质痕迹
senses.example: The valley contains the remains of a whole village.
senses.exampleCN: 这个山谷保存着一座完整村落的遗存。
senses.why: Archaeology uses the word for whatever the past left in place: walls, pits, bones and ash, whether or not they can be lifted.
senses.whyCN: 考古学用这个词指过去原地留下的东西：墙、坑、骨与灰，无论能否被拿起来。

senses.title: Traces of an event
senses.titleCN: 残迹：某件事发生过的痕迹
senses.definition: the visible traces that an event, such as a fire or a flood, has left behind
senses.definitionCN: 火灾、洪水等事件过后留下的可见痕迹
senses.example: The remains of the flood were visible along the bank.
senses.exampleCN: 洪水留下的痕迹沿岸清晰可见。
senses.why: An event passes, but it alters matter; those alterations stay, and the plural noun names them as a group.
senses.whyCN: 事件过去了，却改变了物质；这些改变留了下来，复数名词把它们作为一组来指称。

senses.title: Residue after burning
senses.titleCN: 燃烧残渣：物质反应后剩下的部分
senses.definition: the ash or residue left after something has burned or reacted
senses.definitionCN: 某物燃烧或反应之后留下的灰或残渣
senses.example: The lab analysed the remains of the fuel.
senses.exampleCN: 实验室分析了燃料的残余物。
senses.why: Chemistry keeps the literal reading: matter is conserved, so a reaction leaves something behind, and that something is named with the same plural.
senses.whyCN: 化学保留字面义：物质守恒，反应必有所留，这个留下的东西仍用同一个复数名词。

senses.title: What survives of a body of work
senses.titleCN: 遗存：作品、文献或制度的留存部分
senses.definition: the part of a written, artistic or institutional legacy that survives
senses.definitionCN: 文字、艺术或制度遗产中留存下来的部分
senses.example: The remains of her library were sold at auction.
senses.exampleCN: 她藏书中的留存部分在拍卖会上售出。
senses.why: Extending the same idea to works rather than matter, the word names the fraction of a legacy that outlasted its maker.
senses.whyCN: 把同一观念从事物扩展到作品，这个词便指一份遗产中比其创造者活得更久的那一部分。

intro.en: Remains is the plural noun from the verb remain, which came through Old French from Latin remanere, to stay behind, built on re- and manere, to stay. Dates are approximate.
intro.cn: remains 是动词 remain 的复数名词形式；remain 经古法语来自拉丁 remanere「留在后面」，由 re- 与 manere「停留」构成。年代均为约数。

items.en: Manere meant to stay, dwell or remain; it also gives mansion, manor and permanent, all built on the idea of staying in place.
items.cn: manere 意为停留、居住、留下；它还衍生 mansion、manor、permanent，都建立在「留在原地」的观念上。

items.en: Remanere adds re-, back, to manere: to stay back when others go, the exact picture behind the English plural noun.
items.cn: remanere 在 manere 上加 re-「向后」：别人走了而自己留在后面，这正是英语复数名词背后的图景。

items.en: Old French remaindre passed the verb into English, and the plural noun remains appeared alongside it in the sense of what is left.
items.cn: 古法语 remaindre 把动词传入英语，复数名词 remains 随之出现，义为「剩下的东西」。

items.en: The respectful use for a dead body and the technical use for deposits both grow from the same reading, and both became fixed in the nineteenth century.
items.cn: 指遗体的敬语与指堆积的技术用语都从同一读法生长出来，并在十九世纪固定下来。

items.en: Source uncertain: the deeper origin of manere outside Latin is not established; suggested links to a root meaning to think are hypotheses, not proven derivations.
items.cn: 来源不确定：manere 在拉丁语之外的更深来源未有定论；把它与某个意为「思考」的词根相联系的说法只是假说，并非已证实的派生。

note.en: The first group holds forms of the same verb and its close relatives; the second group holds nouns for what is left behind.
note.cn: 第一组是同一动词的形式及其近亲；第二组是指残留物的名词。

entries.definition: The verb meaning to stay or be left; remains as a noun is its plural, not a separate verb form.
entries.definitionCN: 意为留下或仍然是；名词 remains 是它的复数，并非另一个动词形式。

entries.definition: A countable leftover or the unused part of a set; it is singular and often numerical.
entries.definitionCN: 可数的剩余部分或未用部分；是单数，且常带数量意味。

entries.definition: From the same Latin stock, but it stresses a small surviving piece, as of cloth or of a species.
entries.definitionCN: 同出拉丁词干，但强调一小块留存物，如布头或物种残存。

entries.definition: A surviving object valued for age or holiness; remains makes no such claim.
entries.definitionCN: 因年代或神圣性受珍视的留存物；remains 没有这种附加意味。

entries.definition: What is left after a process, especially a chemical one; narrower and more technical than remains.
entries.definitionCN: 过程之后留下的东西，尤指化学过程；比 remains 更窄、更技术化。

entries.definition: The broken remains of buildings; it names only structures, never bodies or food.
entries.definitionCN: 建筑物倒塌后的残迹；只指结构，不指遗体或食物。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: the re- plus manere structure, the burial use, the archaeology use and the everyday leftovers.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：re- 加 manere 的结构、殡葬义、考古义，以及日常的剩余义。

normal.en: manere, to stay, plus re-, back: remains are what stayed when the rest went.
normal.cn: manere「停留」加 re-「向后」：remains 是其余都走了之后留下的东西。

normal.en: The same manere stock gives mansion, manor and permanent, all about staying in place.
normal.cn: 同出 manere 的有 mansion、manor、permanent，都与「留在原地」有关。

normal.en: Human remains is the respectful phrase; ruins is for buildings only.
normal.cn: human remains 是敬语；ruins 只用于建筑。

normal.en: Archaeology says remains for walls, pits, bones and ash that stay in the ground.
normal.cn: 考古学用 remains 指留在地里的墙、坑、骨与灰。

normal.en: At dinner the same word covers what nobody finished.
normal.cn: 餐桌上同一个词指谁也没吃完的部分。

abstract.en: Abstractly, remains are the answer to a subtraction: something was taken, used or destroyed, and this is the part the subtraction did not reach.
abstract.cn: 抽象地看，remains 是一道减法的答案：某物被取走、用掉或毁掉，而这是减法没有触到的部分。

abstract.en: Matter is conserved, so every ending leaves a remainder somewhere.
abstract.cn: 物质守恒，所以每一种终结都在某处留下余数。

abstract.en: The word quietly insists that disappearance is never total.
abstract.cn: 这个词悄然坚持：消失从来都不彻底。

examples.en: The remains of the wall mark where the old city ended.
examples.cn: 城墙的残迹标出了旧城的边界。

examples.en: Forensic teams recovered the remains from the collapsed building.
examples.cn: 法医小组从倒塌的建筑中找到了遗骸。

examples.en: The remains of the reaction were sealed and stored.
examples.cn: 反应后的残渣被密封保存。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「re（回）+ mains（留）」——回头一看，还留在原地的那些 → 遗骸、残迹

root: 拉丁 remanere「留在后面」= re-（向后）+ manere「停留、居住」；英语动词 remain，其复数名词为 remains。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses follow one subtraction: after a person, a building, a meal, a fund, an event or a reaction is gone, the part that stayed is named by the same plural noun.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项沿同一道减法展开：人、建筑、一餐、资金、事件或反应消失之后，留下的那部分都用同一个复数名词指称。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a subtraction performed on the world, with one residue left on the page.
core.cn: 核心意象：对世界做一道减法，纸面上还剩下一笔余数。

branches.en: THE LARGE REMAINDERS: a body and a building are both what a departure could not remove.
branches.cn: 大的剩余物：遗体与建筑都是离去未能带走的部分。

branches.en: THE EVERYDAY SUBTRACTION: money and food show the same arithmetic at a smaller scale.
branches.cn: 日常减法：金钱与食物在更小的尺度上显示同一算术。

branches.en: THE GROUND'S MEMORY: deposits are remains that never moved and so became evidence.
branches.cn: 土地的记性：堆积是从未移动的残留，因此成了证据。

branches.en: THE EVENT'S RESIDUE: fire and chemical reaction leave traces of energy that passed through.
branches.cn: 事件的残余：火与化学反应留下能量经过的痕迹。

branches.en: THE LEGACY'S FRACTION: of a body of work, only a part outlives its maker.
branches.cn: 遗产的份额：一批作品之中，只有一部分比作者活得更久。

intro.en: Remains is built from a Latin prefix and a Latin verb, and the same verb builds a family of English words about staying and about what is left.
intro.cn: remains 由一个拉丁前缀与一个拉丁动词构成，这个动词还构成一族关于「停留」与「剩余」的英语词。

latinIntro.en: Latin manere, to stay, gives remain, remainder, remnant, mansion, manor and permanent; re- adds the direction back, so what remains is what stayed behind.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁 manere「停留」衍生 remain、remainder、remnant、mansion、manor、permanent；re- 加上「向后」的方向，因此 remains 就是留在后面的东西。

items.example: The prefix reverses or repeats the action of the verb.
items.exampleCN: 这个前缀使动词动作反向或重复。

items.example: Manere is the source of mansion and manor.
items.exampleCN: manere 是 mansion 与 manor 的来源。

items.example: A few guests remanere after the rest had gone.
items.exampleCN: 其余客人走后，少数客人留了下来。

items.example: Only two columns remain standing.
items.exampleCN: 只有两根柱子仍然立着。

items.example: The remains were catalogued by the site team.
items.exampleCN: 遗存由遗址团队编目。

items.structure: remainder (Old French remainder, that which remains)
items.example: The remainder of the grant funded the survey.
items.exampleCN: 拨款的剩余部分资助了这次调查。

items.example: A remnant of the cloth survived in the tomb.
items.exampleCN: 墓中留存下一小块布。

items.example: The old mansion became a museum.
items.exampleCN: 那座老宅成了博物馆。

items.example: The manor owned most of the surrounding fields.
items.exampleCN: 庄园拥有周边大部分田地。

items.example: The excavation left a permanent mark on the field.
items.exampleCN: 发掘在这片田野上留下永久痕迹。

latinEntries.structure: re- + manere (Latin verb, to stay behind)

definition_zh: 化成化石的；以化石形态保存的；僵化的；固化的
definition_en: preserved in the form of a fossil, or, figuratively, fixed so long in one form that it can no longer change
core_image: 一片叶子落进湖底，矿物一点点填满它的细胞，千万年后只剩石头上的一道叶脉
scene: 博物馆库房的抽屉里，一片叶子的轮廓被压进灰色石板，叶脉清晰，却已没有一丝有机物残留。The fossilized leaf in the drawer keeps every vein although nothing organic survives.
sceneCN: 这里 fossilized 指「有机体被矿物质替换、以化石形态保存下来」（第 1 个义项：生物遗体或遗迹经矿化作用定形）；句意为抽屉里的这片叶子虽保留了全部叶脉，有机物却已完全被矿物取代。可辨识物件：石板、叶脉纹、抽屉、标本签、软毛刷。

pos.zh: 化成化石的；以化石形态保存的
僵化的；固化的；停滞不前的（比喻）
（fossilize 的过去式与过去分词）使化石化；使僵化

senses.title: Turned to stone by mineral replacement
senses.titleCN: 矿化成石：有机质被矿物替换
senses.definition: preserved as a fossil because minerals have slowly replaced the original organic material
senses.definitionCN: 因矿物缓慢替换原有有机质而以化石形式保存下来
senses.example: The fossilized wood still shows the grain of the original trunk.
senses.exampleCN: 这块石化木仍能看出原树干的纹理。
senses.why: Fossil comes from Latin fossilis, dug up, from fodere, to dig; the -ized ending says the thing has undergone that change and is now stone-like.
senses.whyCN: fossil 出自拉丁 fossilis「被挖出的」，源于 fodere「挖掘」；-ized 结尾表示该物已经历这一变化，如今状如石头。

senses.title: Preserved as a trace fossil
senses.titleCN: 以遗迹化石形态保存
senses.definition: kept as a footprint, burrow, egg or other trace rather than as the body itself
senses.definitionCN: 以脚印、洞穴、蛋等遗迹而非遗体本身的形式保存下来
senses.example: The fossilized footprints record a walk across wet ash.
senses.exampleCN: 这些化石脚印记录了一次走过湿灰地的行走。
senses.why: A trace is also fossilized when the sediment hardens around the impression; the body is gone but the shape it made has become stone.
senses.whyCN: 当沉积物在印痕周围硬化时，遗迹同样被化石化；身体不在了，它留下的形状却成了石头。

senses.title: Fixed in an outdated form
senses.titleCN: 僵化：制度或观念不再变化
senses.definition: of an institution, idea or practice, fixed so long in one shape that reform becomes impossible
senses.definitionCN: 指制度、观念或做法长期固定于一种形态，以致无法改革
senses.example: The committee had fossilized into a ritual of approval.
senses.exampleCN: 这个委员会已经僵化成一道审批仪式。
senses.why: The metaphor borrows the geological process: what should have decayed instead hardened, and hardening removes the ability to adapt.
senses.whyCN: 这个比喻借用了地质过程：本该腐朽的东西反而硬化了，而硬化剥夺了适应能力。

senses.title: Stuck in old habits
senses.titleCN: 停滞：人停留在旧习惯里
senses.definition: of a person or group, no longer able to change because habits have hardened
senses.definitionCN: 指人或群体因习惯硬化而不再能改变
senses.example: He had fossilized in his opinions by the age of forty.
senses.exampleCN: 他四十岁时观念就已僵化。
senses.why: The same image applied to a mind: repeated behaviour sets like cement, and the set shape resists new evidence.
senses.whyCN: 同一意象用于心智：重复的行为像水泥一样凝固，凝固的形状抗拒新证据。

senses.title: A form frozen in a language
senses.titleCN: 语言中固化的形式
senses.definition: of a word or phrase, kept in an earlier form inside a fixed expression
senses.definitionCN: 指词或短语在固定表达中以较早的形式保存下来
senses.example: The fossilized phrase still uses a verb form no one speaks.
senses.exampleCN: 这个固化短语仍使用无人再说的动词形式。
senses.why: Languages preserve dead forms inside idioms the way rock preserves shells: the surrounding expression stops the change.
senses.whyCN: 语言在习语中保存已死的形式，就像岩石保存贝壳：周围的表达阻止了变化。

senses.title: Dated and unable to update
senses.titleCN: 定型的：因年代久远而无法更新
senses.definition: of a system or style, preserved in an earlier state and unable to modernise
senses.definitionCN: 指体系或风格停留在较早状态、无法现代化
senses.example: The fossilized software could not read any file made after two thousand five.
senses.exampleCN: 这套固化的软件读不了那一年之后生成的任何文件。
senses.why: Systems also harden: once dependencies set, every later change costs more than the system can pay, so the old shape survives.
senses.whyCN: 系统也会硬化：依赖一旦固定，此后每次改动的代价都超出系统所能支付，旧形状便存活下来。

senses.title: Bone filled with mineral
senses.titleCN: 骨骼被矿物质充填
senses.definition: of bone, shell or tooth, with its pores filled by mineral so that the original shape is kept
senses.definitionCN: 指骨骼、贝壳或牙齿的孔隙被矿物充填，从而保留原形
senses.example: The fossilized tooth is heavy because mineral fills every pore.
senses.exampleCN: 这颗化石牙很重，因为矿物填满了每个孔隙。
senses.why: Hard parts fossilize best because they already contain mineral; groundwater adds more, and the object gains weight and permanence.
senses.whyCN: 硬质部分最易化石化，因为它们本就含矿物；地下水再添矿物，物件便增加重量与持久性。

senses.title: Frozen in a single moment
senses.titleCN: 冻结在某一刻
senses.definition: used figuratively for anything that seems arrested at one moment and never moves on
senses.definitionCN: 比喻任何仿佛停在一刻、再也不向前的事物
senses.example: The village felt fossilized in the decade the mine closed.
senses.exampleCN: 这座村庄仿佛冻结在矿场关闭的那个年代。
senses.why: The image reaches its limit here: not merely old, but arrested, as if time had stopped and left the object inside a single layer.
senses.whyCN: 这个意象在此达到极限：不只是旧，而是被定格，仿佛时间停止，把物件封在某一层里。

intro.en: Fossilized is the past participle of fossilize, built on fossil plus the suffix -ize. Fossil goes back to Latin fossilis, dug up, from fodere, to dig. Dates are approximate.
intro.cn: fossilized 是 fossilize 的过去分词，由 fossil 加后缀 -ize 构成。fossil 上溯拉丁 fossilis「被挖出的」，源于 fodere「挖掘」。年代均为约数。

items.en: Fodere meant to dig; its participle fossus, dug, produced fossilis, a thing dug out of the earth.
items.cn: fodere 意为挖掘；其分词 fossus「被挖的」产生 fossilis，即从地里挖出之物。

items.en: Fossilis named anything obtained by digging, including stones and buried remains; English adopted it in the seventeenth century.
items.cn: fossilis 指任何挖掘所得之物，包括石头与埋藏的遗存；英语在十七世纪引入这个词。

items.en: As geology took shape, fossil narrowed to the preserved traces of organisms, and fossilize was coined for the process that produces them.
items.cn: 随着地质学成形，fossil 收窄为生物遗存的保存形态，fossilize 则为产生这一形态的过程而造。

items.en: By the nineteenth century the participle was already used of institutions and opinions that had hardened beyond change.
items.cn: 到十九世纪，这一分词已用于形容硬化到无法改变的制度与观念。

items.en: Source uncertain: no single author is credited with coining fossilize, and the date of its first geological use is not fixed; the suffix -ize was freely added to nouns in that period.
items.cn: 来源不确定：没有辞书把 fossilize 的创造归给某一位作者，其首次地质学用法也无定年；当时 -ize 后缀可自由加在名词上。

note.en: The first group holds words from the same fossil stock; the second group holds words for things that have stopped changing.
note.cn: 第一组是同出 fossil 词干的词；第二组是表示「不再变化」的词。

entries.definition: The preserved remains itself; fossilized describes the state the remains reached.
entries.definitionCN: 指保存下来的遗存本身；fossilized 描述它达到的状态。

entries.definition: The process verb, to turn into a fossil or to become rigid; the participle names the result.
entries.definitionCN: 过程动词，指变成化石或变得僵硬；分词形式指结果。

entries.definition: From the same fodere, to dig, but it describes animals adapted for digging, not preserved remains.
entries.definitionCN: 同出 fodere「挖掘」，但形容适应掘土的动物，而非保存下来的遗存。

entries.definition: Literally turned to stone by mineral replacement; it is the closest physical synonym, while fossilized can also mean trace-preserved.
entries.definitionCN: 字面指被矿物替换成石头；它是最接近的物理同义词，而 fossilized 也可指遗迹保存。

entries.definition: Stiff and unwilling to bend; it describes the behaviour, while fossilized adds the image of geological hardening.
entries.definitionCN: 僵硬、不愿弯曲；它描述行为，而 fossilized 增加了地质硬化的意象。

entries.definition: Old-fashioned and out of use; it says nothing about hardening, only about surviving past its time.
entries.definitionCN: 古旧而不再使用；它不涉及硬化，只说明活过了它的时代。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: the digging root, the -ize suffix, the trace fossils, and the metaphor of hardening.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：表示挖掘的词根、-ize 后缀、遗迹化石，以及硬化的比喻。

normal.en: fodere, to dig, gives fossilis, dug up: a fossil is literally something dug out of the ground.
normal.cn: fodere「挖掘」派生 fossilis「被挖出的」：化石字面就是从地里挖出的东西。

normal.en: -ize turns the noun into a process, and -ed marks the result: the thing has been through the process.
normal.cn: -ize 把名词变成过程，-ed 标记结果：该物已经历这一过程。

normal.en: Body fossils keep the organism; trace fossils keep what it did, such as footprints and burrows.
normal.cn: 实体化石保存生物本身；遗迹化石保存它做过的事，如脚印与洞穴。

normal.en: Hard parts fossilize best because bone and shell already contain mineral.
normal.cn: 硬质部分最易化石化，因为骨与壳本就含矿物。

normal.en: Applied to people, the same word accuses them of having hardened instead of growing.
normal.cn: 用于人时，同一个词是在指责他们硬化了，而不是成长了。

abstract.en: Abstractly, fossilization is change that stops: the object keeps its shape by losing its capacity to respond.
abstract.cn: 抽象地看，化石化是停止的变化：物件靠失去回应能力来保住形状。

abstract.en: Preservation and death are the same process seen from two sides: what survives is what could not decay.
abstract.cn: 保存与死亡是同一过程的两面：活下来的，正是无法腐朽的部分。

abstract.en: Every institution should ask whether its stability is growth or fossilization.
abstract.cn: 每个机构都该问：它的稳定是成长，还是僵化。

examples.en: The fossilized reef shows that a warm sea once covered this desert.
examples.cn: 这片石化礁石说明温暖的海曾覆盖过这片沙漠。

examples.en: Fossilized pollen in the sediment records the plants of that era.
examples.cn: 沉积物中的化石花粉记录了那个时代的植物。

examples.en: The department had fossilized around a procedure no one could defend.
examples.cn: 这个部门围绕一道无人能辩护的程序僵化了。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「fossil（化石）+ ized（已经变成）」——已经变成化石的 → 化石化的、僵化的

root: 拉丁 fossilis「被挖出的」（源于 fodere「挖掘」）+ 动词后缀 -ize 的过去分词 -ized；字面为「已被挖出、已成化石的」。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses follow one hardening: organic matter becomes stone, a trace becomes stone, and then institutions, minds, phrases, systems and whole places become unable to change.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项沿同一次硬化展开：有机物变成石头，遗迹变成石头，随后制度、心智、短语、系统乃至整个地方都变得无法改变。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: soft tissue replaced grain by grain until only a stone copy remains.
core.cn: 核心意象：柔软组织被一粒粒矿物替换，最后只剩一份石质副本。

branches.en: THE BODY IN STONE: replacement and pore-filling are two routes to the same heavy copy.
branches.cn: 石中的身体：替换与充填是通往同一份沉重副本的两条路。

branches.en: THE SHAPE LEFT BEHIND: a footprint hardens into evidence even when no body is there.
branches.cn: 留下的形状：即使没有身体，脚印也会硬化成证据。

branches.en: HARDENED INSTITUTIONS AND MINDS: what should have adapted instead set like cement.
branches.cn: 硬化的制度与心智：本该适应的东西却像水泥一样凝固。

branches.en: THE IDIOM AS AMBER: a fixed phrase preserves a dead form exactly as resin preserves an insect.
branches.cn: 习语如琥珀：固定短语保存已死的形式，正如树脂保存昆虫。

branches.en: ARRESTED TIME: systems and places stop updating and seem sealed inside one layer.
branches.cn: 被定格的时间：系统与地方停止更新，仿佛被封在某一层里。

intro.en: Fossilized is transparent: a Latin-derived noun, a productive verb suffix and a past-participle ending.
intro.cn: fossilized 的构造很透明：一个拉丁来源的名词、一个能产动词后缀与一个过去分词词尾。

latinIntro.en: Latin fodere, to dig, gives fossilis and then fossil; English adds -ize and -ed. The same fodere also gives fossorial, describing digging animals.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁 fodere「挖掘」衍生 fossilis，再进入英语为 fossil；英语加上 -ize 与 -ed。同一 fodere 还衍生 fossorial，形容掘土动物。

items.example: Fodere is the source of fossil and fossorial.
items.exampleCN: fodere 是 fossil 与 fossorial 的来源。

items.example: Fossilis described stones taken from deep ground.
items.exampleCN: fossilis 形容从深土中取出的石头。

items.example: The fossil was found in marine limestone.
items.exampleCN: 这块化石发现于海相石灰岩中。

items.example: Fossil plus -ize means to become a fossil.
items.exampleCN: fossil 加 -ize 意为变成化石。

items.meaning: to turn into a fossil, or to become rigid
items.example: Wood can fossilize in mineral-rich water.
items.exampleCN: 木材在富含矿物质的水中可以化石化。

items.example: The -ed ending marks the completed process.
items.exampleCN: -ed 词尾标记已完成的过程。

items.meaning: the process of becoming a fossil
items.example: Fossilization needs rapid burial and mineral water.
items.exampleCN: 化石化需要迅速埋藏与含矿物质的水。

items.example: The fossiliferous layer is dark and hard.
items.exampleCN: 含化石的层位颜色深、质地硬。

items.example: Fossorial mammals have strong forelimbs.
items.exampleCN: 掘土哺乳动物前肢强壮。

items.example: The fosse around the fort is still visible.
items.exampleCN: 堡垒周围的壕沟仍可见。

definition_zh: 发掘现场；考古工地；出土地点
definition_en: a place where soil and deposits are being dug away to expose buried remains, especially in archaeology
core_image: 一片被切成方格的黄土，四壁笔直，坑底露出石墙，几个人蹲在角落里用小铲刮土
scene: 夏日的土坡被切成整齐的方格，坑底露出半截石墙，学生蹲在角落里用小铲慢慢刮土。On the excavation site, students scrape the floor of a trench where a low stone wall has appeared.
sceneCN: 这里 excavation site 指「正在开挖、以揭露地下遗存的现场」（第 1 个义项：考古发掘的工作地点）；句意为学生在探方底部慢慢刮土，那里已露出一段矮石墙。可辨识物件：探方壁、石墙、手铲、土筐、卷尺。

pos.zh: 发掘现场；考古工地；出土地点
（工程意义上的）开挖场地

senses.title: A place being dug for remains
senses.titleCN: 发掘现场：为揭露遗存而开挖的地点
senses.definition: a location where earth is removed layer by layer to expose buried archaeological remains
senses.definitionCN: 逐层去除泥土以揭露埋藏遗存的地点
senses.example: The excavation site was fenced off before digging began.
senses.exampleCN: 开挖之前，发掘现场已被围栏隔开。
senses.why: Excavation is Latin ex- plus cavus, hollow: the work hollows out the ground, and site names the place where that hollowing happens.
senses.whyCN: excavation 由拉丁 ex-「出」加 cavus「空、凹」构成：这项工作把地面挖空，site 则指挖空发生的地点。

senses.title: The precise find spot
senses.titleCN: 出土点：具体发现器物的位置
senses.definition: the exact spot within a dig where an object or feature was found
senses.definitionCN: 发掘范围内器物或遗迹被找到的确切位置
senses.example: The coin was recorded at the excavation site before it was lifted.
senses.exampleCN: 这枚钱币在被取出之前已在出土位置记录。
senses.why: Context is everything in archaeology, so the phrase also marks a point in three-dimensional space, not just a general area.
senses.whyCN: 在考古中情境就是一切，因此这个短语也标记三维空间中的一点，而不只是笼统的区域。

senses.title: The working archaeological dig
senses.titleCN: 考古工地：带工作棚与探方的作业区
senses.definition: the organised working area of a dig, with trenches, shelters and recording stations
senses.definitionCN: 发掘的有组织作业区，含探方、工作棚与记录点
senses.example: The excavation site had a shelter over the deepest trench.
senses.exampleCN: 发掘现场在最深的探方上方搭了棚。
senses.why: A dig is a workplace as well as a place of discovery; tools, labels and shelters make the site a small factory of evidence.
senses.whyCN: 发掘既是发现之地，也是工作场所；工具、标签与棚子使这个现场成为一座证据的小工厂。

senses.title: A rescue dig before construction
senses.titleCN: 抢救性发掘现场：工程动工前的紧急开挖
senses.definition: a site dug quickly because a road, dam or building will destroy it
senses.definitionCN: 因道路、水坝或建筑即将毁掉遗址而紧急开挖的地点
senses.example: The rescue excavation site closed within three months.
senses.exampleCN: 这处抢救性发掘现场在三个月内结束工作。
senses.why: When destruction is scheduled, the site is defined by a deadline rather than by research questions, and the phrase carries that urgency.
senses.whyCN: 当毁坏已有日程，现场就由期限而非研究问题来定义，这个短语也带着这种紧迫感。

senses.title: A fossil quarry
senses.titleCN: 化石挖掘点：为取化石而开挖的地点
senses.definition: a place dug specifically to recover fossil remains rather than human artefacts
senses.definitionCN: 专门为取出化石而非人类器物而开挖的地点
senses.example: The fossil excavation site lies in a dry gully.
senses.exampleCN: 这处化石挖掘点位于一条干涸的冲沟里。
senses.why: The phrase is not restricted to archaeology: any systematic dig for buried remains, including palaeontological ones, can carry the name.
senses.whyCN: 这个短语并不限于考古：任何为取出埋藏遗存而进行的有系统开挖，包括古生物发掘，都可以用这个名字。

senses.title: A construction cut
senses.titleCN: 工程挖方场地：施工中的开挖区
senses.definition: an area where soil or rock is removed for building, mining or engineering
senses.definitionCN: 为建筑、采矿或工程而移除土石的区域
senses.example: The excavation site for the new station covered two streets.
senses.exampleCN: 新车站的挖方场地占了两条街。
senses.why: Outside archaeology the same words describe any open cut; the difference is that engineers remove earth to place something, while archaeologists remove it to read something.
senses.whyCN: 在考古之外，同样的词描述任何露天开挖；区别在于工程师挖土是为了放东西，考古学者挖土是为了读东西。

senses.title: A gridded excavation area
senses.titleCN: 发掘区：按探方网格划分的区域
senses.definition: the part of a site laid out in a grid of squares and recorded as a single unit
senses.definitionCN: 按方格网划分、作为一个单位记录的遗址区域
senses.example: The eastern excavation site produced most of the pottery.
senses.exampleCN: 东侧发掘区出土了大部分陶器。
senses.why: Modern digs divide space into measured squares; the phrase can name one such block, giving a unit of record rather than a point.
senses.whyCN: 现代发掘把空间分成有测量的方格；这个短语可指其中一个方格，提供的是记录单位而非一个点。

senses.title: A dig open to visitors
senses.titleCN: 对外开放的发掘现场：可供参观的展示区
senses.definition: a working or reconstructed dig displayed to the public as heritage interpretation
senses.definitionCN: 作为遗产阐释向公众展示的在挖或复原的发掘区
senses.example: The excavation site receives school groups every spring.
senses.exampleCN: 这处发掘现场每年春天接待学生团体。
senses.why: Heritage tourism turns the workplace into a stage, and the phrase then names a place designed to be looked at as well as dug.
senses.whyCN: 遗产旅游把工作场所变成舞台，这个短语于是也指既供发掘又供观看的场所。

intro.en: Excavation site joins two Latin-derived words: excavate, from ex- plus cavus, hollow, and site, from Latin situs, a place. The phrase is a modern English combination. Dates are approximate.
intro.cn: excavation site 由两个拉丁来源的词组合而成：excavate 出自 ex- 加 cavus「空、凹」，site 出自拉丁 situs「地点」。这个短语是近代英语的组合。年代均为约数。

items.en: Cavus meant hollow or cave-like; it gives cave, cavity and excavate, all about empty space cut into something solid.
items.cn: cavus 意为空的、洞穴状的；它衍生 cave、cavity、excavate，都与在固体中挖出空腔有关。

items.en: Excavare combined ex-, out, with cavare, to hollow, and meant to hollow out; English took it as excavate in the seventeenth century.
items.cn: excavare 由 ex-「出」与 cavare「挖空」构成，意为挖空；英语在十七世纪引入为 excavate。

items.en: Situs meant a position or a place, from sinere, to allow or leave; English site keeps the sense of a located spot.
items.cn: situs 意为位置或地点，出自 sinere「容许、留下」；英语 site 保留「有定位的地点」这一义。

items.en: Archaeology in the nineteenth century needed a term for the place of a dig as distinct from the dig itself, and excavation site supplied it.
items.cn: 十九世纪的考古学需要一个词指开挖地点、以区别于开挖本身，excavation site 正好补上。

items.en: Source uncertain: the exact date of the phrase's first appearance in print is not recorded, and its spread into engineering use is undocumented in detail.
items.cn: 来源不确定：这个短语首次见于印刷物的确切年代没有记录，它向工程用语的扩展也缺乏详细的文献记载。

note.en: The first group holds phrases that name related parts of a dig; the second group holds words for places where things are found.
note.cn: 第一组是命名发掘中相关部分的短语；第二组是指发现之地的词。

entries.definition: The activity or the hole made by digging; the site is the location where that activity happens.
entries.definitionCN: 指发掘活动或挖出的坑；现场则是这一活动发生的地点。

entries.definition: Any place with archaeological value, whether or not it is currently being dug.
entries.definitionCN: 任何具有考古价值的地点，无论当前是否正在开挖。

entries.definition: The excavation as a project and its site together, used informally by field crews.
entries.definitionCN: 口语中指发掘项目及其现场的整体，田野人员常用。

entries.definition: A single long cut inside a site, not the whole place of work.
entries.definitionCN: 遗址内的一条长形开挖，而不是整个工作场地。

entries.definition: A place where stone or fossils are extracted for use or study; it lacks the archaeological emphasis on context.
entries.definitionCN: 为利用或研究而开采石材或化石的地点；缺乏考古对情境的强调。

entries.definition: The open land around a dig; it names the setting, not the organised place of excavation.
entries.definitionCN: 发掘周围的露天地面；它指环境，而不是有组织的发掘地点。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: the hollowing root, the located place, the grid and the deadline.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：表示挖空的词根、有定位的地点、探方网格与工期期限。

normal.en: ex-, out, plus cavus, hollow: excavation is the making of a hollow in the ground.
normal.cn: ex-「出」加 cavus「空」：excavation 就是在地面上造出一个空腔。

normal.en: site comes from situs, a place: the phrase pins the hollowing to one located spot.
normal.cn: site 出自 situs「地点」：这个短语把开挖固定在一个有定位的点上。

normal.en: A dig is a workplace: trenches, shelters, labels and buckets all belong to the site.
normal.cn: 发掘是工作场所：探方、棚子、标签与土筐都属于现场。

normal.en: Rescue digs are defined by a deadline, not by a research question.
normal.cn: 抢救性发掘由期限定义，而不是由研究问题定义。

normal.en: Archaeologists dig to read; engineers dig to place. The words are the same, the purpose is not.
normal.cn: 考古学者挖土是为了读，工程师挖土是为了放。词相同，目的不同。

abstract.en: Abstractly, a site is a place where absence is being turned into information.
abstract.cn: 抽象地看，现场是把「空缺」转成信息的地方。

abstract.en: The phrase holds two acts at once: destroying the ground and preserving its order.
abstract.cn: 这个短语同时包含两种行为：破坏地面，又保存它的秩序。

abstract.en: Every site is a one-time experiment: once removed, the deposit cannot be put back.
abstract.cn: 每个现场都是一次性实验：堆积一旦被移除，就无法放回。

examples.en: Heavy rain flooded the excavation site overnight.
examples.cn: 大雨一夜之间淹了发掘现场。

examples.en: The excavation site is closed to the public while the wall is exposed.
examples.cn: 墙体暴露期间，发掘现场对公众关闭。

examples.en: Each excavation site is recorded with photographs before any soil is moved.
examples.cn: 动土之前，每个发掘现场都要拍照记录。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「ex（出）+ cave（洞）+ site（地点）」——把土挖出成洞的地方 → 发掘现场

root: 拉丁 excavare「挖空」= ex-（出）+ cavare（挖空，出自 cavus「空」）+ 拉丁 situs「地点」；字面为「被挖空的地点」。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses follow one hollow: a place is opened in the ground, and the phrase then marks the exact find spot, the working dig, the rescue cut, the fossil quarry, the engineering cut, one grid square and a site open to visitors.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项沿同一个空腔展开：在地面上打开一处空间，这个短语随后标记确切出土点、作业工地、抢救性开挖、化石挖掘点、工程挖方、一个探方格，以及向公众开放的现场。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a square hole cut into yellow earth, its walls straight, a stone wall showing at the bottom.
core.cn: 核心意象：黄土被切成方坑，四壁笔直，坑底露出一段石墙。

branches.en: THE CUT ITSELF: whether for research or construction, the first act is the same removal of earth.
branches.cn: 开挖本身：无论为研究还是施工，第一个动作都是同样的移土。

branches.en: LOCATION AND UNIT: a point in three dimensions and a measured square are two scales of the same record.
branches.cn: 位置与单位：三维中的一点与一个有测量的方格，是同一记录的两个尺度。

branches.en: THE WORKPLACE: shelter, tools and labels turn a hole into an instrument of knowledge.
branches.cn: 工作场所：棚子、工具与标签把一个坑变成求知的仪器。

branches.en: URGENCY AND ORIGIN: a deadline or a fossil bed can define a site as sharply as a research plan.
branches.cn: 紧迫与来源：期限或化石层可以像研究计划一样明确地定义一个现场。

branches.en: THE SITE ON SHOW: heritage display turns the workplace into a stage for visitors.
branches.cn: 展示中的现场：遗产展示把工作场所变成供访客观看的舞台。

intro.en: Excavation site is a two-word phrase whose members are both Latin-derived and still productive in English.
intro.cn: excavation site 是一个双词短语，两个成员都源自拉丁语，且在现代英语中仍有构词能力。

latinIntro.en: Latin cavus, hollow, gives cave, cavity, excavate and excavation; Latin situs, place, gives site and situate. The phrase simply joins the act to the location.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁 cavus「空」衍生 cave、cavity、excavate、excavation；拉丁 situs「地点」衍生 site、situate。这个短语只是把动作与地点连在一起。

items.example: Cavus is the source of cave and cavity.
items.exampleCN: cavus 是 cave 与 cavity 的来源。

items.example: Cavare gave English excavation its inner verb.
items.exampleCN: cavare 为英语 excavation 提供了内部动词。

items.example: The prefix marks removal from the inside.
items.exampleCN: 这个前缀标记从内部取出。

items.example: They excavated the floor of the trench by hand.
items.exampleCN: 他们用手工开挖探方底部。

items.meaning: the act or result of digging out
items.example: The excavation took two seasons.
items.exampleCN: 这次发掘用了两个季度。

items.meaning: one who digs, or a digging machine
items.example: The excavator removed the modern fill.
items.exampleCN: 挖掘机清除了现代填土。

items.example: The cave preserved bones for thousands of years.
items.exampleCN: 这处洞穴把骨骸保存了数千年。

items.example: The cavity in the tooth held mineral infill.
items.exampleCN: 牙中的空腔填有矿物质。

items.example: The site lies beside the old river bed.
items.exampleCN: 这处地点位于旧河床边。

items.example: The trench was situated on the eastern slope.
items.exampleCN: 探方位于东坡上。

latinEntries.structure: ex- + cavare (Latin verb, to hollow out)

definition_zh: 考古证据；考古学意义上的实物与情境依据
definition_en: material and contextual information from the past, such as objects, deposits and structures, used to support claims about how people lived
core_image: 桌上并排放着陶片、骨渣、一张地层剖面图和一页测年报告，四样东西互相指向同一个年代
scene: 研究室的桌上并排放着陶片、烧过的骨渣、一张地层剖面图和一份测年报告，四样东西互相印证同一个年代。In the laboratory, the archaeological evidence is laid out as pottery, burnt bone, a section drawing and a dating report.
sceneCN: 这里 archaeological evidence 指「用来支持关于过去生活之论断的实物与情境材料」（第 1 个义项：考古研究中作为依据的物质材料总体）；句意为桌上四类材料彼此印证同一个年代。可辨识物件：陶片、骨渣、剖面图、测年报告、标签。

pos.zh: 考古证据；实物依据（不可数）
（某一项）考古证据材料

senses.title: Material proof of past life
senses.titleCN: 实物证据：过去生活的物质依据
senses.definition: the body of physical material used to support claims about past human behaviour
senses.definitionCN: 用来支持关于过去人类行为之论断的物质材料总体
senses.example: Archaeological evidence shows that the valley was farmed early.
senses.exampleCN: 考古证据表明这个谷地很早就被耕作。
senses.why: Evidence comes from Latin evidentia, clearness, from ex- plus videre, to see: what counts is what can be shown, and archaeology shows it with things.
senses.whyCN: evidence 出自拉丁 evidentia「清楚」，源于 ex- 加 videre「看见」：算数的是能被展示的东西，而考古学用实物来展示。

senses.title: Evidence from artefacts
senses.titleCN: 器物证据：由出土器物提供的依据
senses.definition: proof drawn from the shape, material and wear of objects that people made
senses.definitionCN: 由人所制器物的形状、材质与使用痕迹提供的依据
senses.example: The pottery gives the strongest archaeological evidence for trade.
senses.exampleCN: 陶器为贸易提供了最有力的考古证据。
senses.why: Objects carry decisions in their form: a rim, a glaze or a repair records a choice, and choices can be compared across places.
senses.whyCN: 物件把决定带在形状里：一道口沿、一层釉或一处修补都记录了一次选择，而选择可以跨地点比较。

senses.title: Stratigraphic proof
senses.titleCN: 地层证据：由层位关系提供的依据
senses.definition: proof from the order and position of layers, which fixes what is earlier and what is later
senses.definitionCN: 由层的顺序与位置提供的依据，用来确定先后关系
senses.example: The stratigraphic evidence places the wall below the Roman floor.
senses.exampleCN: 地层证据把这堵墙定在罗马地面之下。
senses.why: Layers accumulate in order, so position itself is a claim about time; a find below another find is older by construction.
senses.whyCN: 层按顺序堆积，因此位置本身就是关于时间的论断：位于另一发现物之下的发现物，按形成规律更早。

senses.title: Evidence from structures
senses.titleCN: 遗迹证据：由建筑与构筑物提供的依据
senses.definition: proof from walls, ditches, floors and other built features that cannot be moved
senses.definitionCN: 由墙、沟、地面等不可移动的建筑与构筑特征提供的依据
senses.example: The ditch is archaeological evidence of a defended boundary.
senses.exampleCN: 这条沟是防御边界的考古证据。
senses.why: Features record organised labour: someone dug, cut and filled, and the shape of that effort survives after the people leave.
senses.whyCN: 遗迹记录有组织的劳动：有人挖过、切过、填过，这份劳作的形状在人离开后仍然留存。

senses.title: Dating evidence
senses.titleCN: 测年证据：确定年代的依据
senses.definition: measurements such as radiocarbon ages that place material on a calendar
senses.definitionCN: 把材料定位到日历上的测量结果，如放射性碳年龄
senses.example: The dating evidence puts the burial in the third century.
senses.exampleCN: 测年证据把这处墓葬定在三世纪。
senses.why: Decay runs at a known rate, so the amount left measures elapsed time; the measurement converts material into a date.
senses.whyCN: 衰变以已知速率进行，因此剩余的量可测量流逝的时间；这项测量把材料转换成日期。

senses.title: Chemical and biological evidence
senses.titleCN: 化学生物证据：由成分与同位素提供的依据
senses.definition: proof from the composition of bones, teeth or residues, revealing diet, origin or craft
senses.definitionCN: 由骨骼、牙齿或残留物的成分提供的依据，可揭示饮食、来源或工艺
senses.example: Isotope values are archaeological evidence of a migrant childhood.
senses.exampleCN: 同位素值是迁移童年经历的考古证据。
senses.why: Bodies record what they ate and drank; chemistry reads that record, so the body becomes a document.
senses.whyCN: 身体记录了吃过与喝过的东西；化学读取这份记录，于是身体变成一份文件。

senses.title: Circumstantial proof
senses.titleCN: 间接证据：需靠推断连接的依据
senses.definition: material that supports a conclusion only when combined with other lines of reasoning
senses.definitionCN: 只有与其他推理线索结合时才支持结论的材料
senses.example: The absence of weapons is circumstantial evidence of a peaceful site.
senses.exampleCN: 缺少武器是这处遗址平和的间接证据。
senses.why: Not every trace points directly at its cause; some only narrow the possibilities, and the word still covers them.
senses.whyCN: 并非每条痕迹都直接指向原因；有些只缩小可能性范围，这个词同样涵盖它们。

senses.title: Absence as proof
senses.titleCN: 缺失作为证据：没有发现本身也说明问题
senses.definition: the evidential value of what is missing, when preservation or sampling makes absence meaningful
senses.definitionCN: 当保存条件或抽样使「没有」具有意义时，缺失本身的证据价值
senses.example: The missing grain stores are archaeological evidence of a failed harvest.
senses.exampleCN: 粮仓的缺失是歉收的考古证据。
senses.why: A negative finding can be informative if the search was thorough; nothing found where something should have been is itself a datum.
senses.whyCN: 如果搜寻足够彻底，否定的发现也能提供信息：本该有东西的地方什么都没有，这本身就是一条资料。

intro.en: Archaeological evidence joins Greek archaeology to Latin evidence: arkhaiologia, the study of what is old, and evidentia, clearness. The phrase is a modern English combination. Dates are approximate.
intro.cn: archaeological evidence 把希腊来源的 archaeology 与拉丁来源的 evidence 连在一起：arkhaiologia 指对古老之物的研究，evidentia 指清楚。这个短语是近代英语的组合。年代均为约数。

items.en: Arkhē meant beginning or first principle, and arkhaios meant ancient; arkhaiologia was talk or study of ancient things.
items.cn: arkhē 意为开端或第一原理，arkhaios 意为古老的；arkhaiologia 指关于古代事物的谈论或研究。

items.en: Logos meant word, account or reason, and -logia became the suffix for a field of study; archaeology is the account of ancient remains.
items.cn: logos 意为言词、叙述或理性，-logia 成为学科后缀；archaeology 就是关于古代遗存的叙述。

items.en: Evidentia meant clearness or distinctness, from evidens, plainly seen, built on ex- plus videre, to see.
items.cn: evidentia 意为清楚、分明，出自 evidens「清楚可见」，由 ex- 加 videre「看见」构成。

items.en: As archaeology became a discipline in the nineteenth century, evidence was attached to it to name the material grounds of argument rather than the arguments themselves.
items.cn: 十九世纪考古学成为学科时，evidence 被附着其上，用来指论证的物质依据，而非论证本身。

items.en: Source uncertain: the first printed use of the exact phrase is not recorded, and Greek arkhaiologia itself is attested only in a few ancient authors.
items.cn: 来源不确定：这一确切短语的首次印刷使用没有记录，希腊语 arkhaiologia 本身也只在少数古代作者笔下出现。

note.en: The first group holds phrases built on evidence in other fields; the second group holds words for grounds of argument.
note.cn: 第一组是其他领域中以 evidence 构成的短语；第二组是论证依据类的词。

entries.definition: Proof from documents and testimony rather than from material remains; the two often need each other.
entries.definitionCN: 来自文献与证言而非物质遗存的依据；两者常需互相配合。

entries.definition: Material proof gathered for a legal case; archaeology may supply it, but the purpose is a court.
entries.definitionCN: 为法律案件收集的物质依据；考古可以提供，但目的在法庭。

entries.definition: The entire surviving body of material; evidence is the part of it used to support a particular claim.
entries.definitionCN: 全部留存下来的物质总体；证据是其中用于支持某一具体论断的部分。

entries.definition: A conclusion that leaves no reasonable doubt; archaeological evidence is usually suggestive rather than decisive.
entries.definitionCN: 不留合理怀疑的结论；考古证据通常只是提示性的，而非决定性的。

entries.definition: Recorded observations before interpretation; evidence is data already selected to support a claim.
entries.definitionCN: 解释之前的记录观察；证据是已被挑选来支持论断的资料。

entries.definition: A sign that points toward a conclusion without establishing it.
entries.definitionCN: 指向某一结论、但并未确立该结论的迹象。
