normalIntro.en: Normal associations: the seeing root, the Greek study of the old, the four kinds of material and the value of absence.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：表示「看见」的词根、希腊语「研究古老之物」、四类材料，以及缺失的价值。

normal.en: videre, to see, gives evidence: evidence is what can be shown to the eye.
normal.cn: videre「看见」派生 evidence：证据就是能展示给眼睛看的东西。

normal.en: arkhaios, ancient, plus logos, account: archaeology is the account of ancient remains.
normal.cn: arkhaios「古老」加 logos「叙述」：archaeology 是关于古代遗存的叙述。

normal.en: Four common kinds are artefacts, layers, structures and measurements.
normal.cn: 常见的四类是器物、地层、遗迹与测量结果。

normal.en: Objects, layers, walls and dates must agree; one kind alone rarely settles a question.
normal.cn: 器物、地层、墙体与年代必须彼此吻合；单靠一类很少能定论。

normal.en: Absence can be evidence, but only if the search was thorough enough to have found something.
normal.cn: 缺失可以是证据，但前提是搜寻足够彻底，本该能找到东西。

abstract.en: Abstractly, evidence is material promoted to the status of an argument.
abstract.cn: 抽象地看，证据是被提升到论证地位的材料。

abstract.en: The past does not speak; it leaves a distribution, and evidence is the pattern we choose to read.
abstract.cn: 过去不会说话；它留下一种分布，而证据是我们选择去读的图案。

abstract.en: Every claim should be only as strong as the material that carries it.
abstract.cn: 每一个论断的强度，都不应超过承载它的材料。

examples.en: There is little archaeological evidence for the earliest years of the settlement.
examples.cn: 关于这处聚落最早年代的考古证据很少。

examples.en: The team combined archaeological evidence with satellite images of the valley.
examples.cn: 团队把考古证据与该谷地的卫星影像结合起来。

examples.en: Absence of bone is weak archaeological evidence, since bone rarely survives in this soil.
examples.cn: 没有骨是薄弱的考古证据，因为骨在这种土壤里很难保存。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「考古（archaeology）+ 证据（evidence）」——从土里挖出来、能摆上桌的证据 → 考古证据

root: 希腊 arkhaios「古老的」+ logos「叙述、研究」构成 archaeology；拉丁 evidens（ex- + videre「看见」）构成 evidence；字面为「由古代遗存显示出来的依据」。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses follow one showing: material from the past is displayed as proof, and the kinds of material, the measurements, the weak links and even the gaps all count as evidence.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项沿同一次「显示」展开：过去的材料被摆出来作为依据，材料的类别、测量、薄弱环节，乃至空缺，都可计入证据。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: four kinds of material laid side by side until they point at one date.
core.cn: 核心意象：四类材料并排放置，直到它们共同指向同一个年代。

branches.en: THE THINGS THEMSELVES: objects are the first and most direct form of archaeological proof.
branches.cn: 物本身：器物是最先也最直接的考古依据。

branches.en: POSITION AS PROOF: a layer and a wall argue through order and shape rather than through content.
branches.cn: 位置即证据：地层与墙体通过顺序和形状而非内容来论证。

branches.en: THE BODY AS DOCUMENT: dates and isotopes turn material into readable measurements.
branches.cn: 身体即文件：年代与同位素把材料变成可读的测量。

branches.en: THE WEAK LINK: circumstantial material narrows possibilities without settling them.
branches.cn: 薄弱环节：间接材料缩小可能性，却不作定论。

branches.en: THE INFORMATIVE GAP: a thorough search that finds nothing has itself produced a datum.
branches.cn: 有信息量的空缺：彻底搜寻却一无所获，本身也产生了一条资料。

intro.en: Archaeological evidence joins two learned words, one Greek and one Latin, both of which still build English terms.
intro.cn: archaeological evidence 把两个学术词连在一起，一个来自希腊语，一个来自拉丁语，两者至今仍在构成英语术语。

latinIntro.en: Greek arkhaios and logos build archaeology and archaeologist; Latin evidens and evidentia build evidence and evidential. The phrase marks the material side of the Greek discipline with a Latin word for clearness.
latinIntro.cn: 希腊 arkhaios 与 logos 构成 archaeology、archaeologist；拉丁 evidens、evidentia 构成 evidence、evidential。这个短语用拉丁的「清楚」来标记希腊学科的物质侧面。

items.example: Arkhē names the starting point of a thing.
items.exampleCN: arkhē 指一物的起点。

items.example: Arkhaios describes what belongs to an early time.
items.exampleCN: arkhaios 形容属于早期的东西。

items.example: Logos supplies the -logy of many disciplines.
items.exampleCN: logos 为许多学科提供 -logy 后缀。

items.example: Archaeology reads the past through things.
items.exampleCN: 考古学通过实物读过去。

items.example: The map shows archaeological zones.
items.exampleCN: 这张图标出考古区域。

items.example: Evidens joins ex-, out, with videre, to see.
items.exampleCN: evidens 由 ex-「出」与 videre「看见」构成。

items.example: Evidentia became English evidence.
items.exampleCN: evidentia 成为英语 evidence。

items.example: The evidence was photographed in place.
items.exampleCN: 证据在原地被拍照记录。

items.example: The find has evidential value only in context.
items.exampleCN: 这项发现只有放在情境中才有证据价值。

items.example: The wear marks evince long use.
items.exampleCN: 使用痕迹表明长期使用。

definition_zh: 考古记录；物质遗存总体；发掘与登记档案
definition_en: the surviving body of material remains and the documentation of excavations, taken together as the record of the human past
core_image: 一面墙的架子上排满纸盒，每盒贴一个编号，旁边是一排写满层位与坐标的登记册
scene: 库房的架子上排满纸盒，每盒贴一个编号，旁边一摞登记册写满层位与坐标。The archaeological record fills the shelves with numbered boxes and matching registers.
sceneCN: 这里 archaeological record 指「留存下来的物质遗存与发掘记录合在一起构成的总体」（第 1 个义项：作为人类过去之记录的物质与文献总和）；句意为架上的编号纸盒与对应登记册共同构成这份记录。可辨识物件：纸盒、编号签、登记册、铅笔、层位表。

pos.zh: 考古记录；物质遗存总体（不可数）
（某一地区或某次发掘的）记录材料

senses.title: The surviving material record
senses.titleCN: 物质遗存总体：留存下来的全部物质材料
senses.definition: everything that survives from past human activity and can be studied as a body of material
senses.definitionCN: 过去人类活动中留存下来、可作为材料总体研究的一切
senses.example: Forests and cities both leave different traces in the archaeological record.
senses.exampleCN: 森林与城市在考古记录中留下不同的痕迹。
senses.why: Record comes from Latin recordari, to remember, built on cor, heart: the word treats matter as a memory that the earth kept.
senses.whyCN: record 出自拉丁 recordari「记住」，其词根是 cor「心」：这个词把物质当作大地保存下来的记忆。

senses.title: The field documentation
senses.titleCN: 田野记录：发掘现场的表格与笔记
senses.definition: the notes, plans, sections and photographs made while a site is being dug
senses.definitionCN: 发掘过程中所做的笔记、平面图、剖面图与照片
senses.example: The archaeological record for the trench fills four notebooks.
senses.exampleCN: 这个探方的田野记录写满了四个笔记本。
senses.why: Digging destroys the deposit, so the written record must replace what the spade removes; documentation is the site's second life.
senses.whyCN: 发掘会毁掉堆积，因此文字记录必须替代铁锹移走的东西；档案就是遗址的第二次生命。

senses.title: The published literature
senses.titleCN: 已发表记录：正式出版的研究材料
senses.definition: the published reports and articles through which a dig becomes available to other researchers
senses.definitionCN: 使一次发掘可为其他研究者使用的正式报告与论文
senses.example: Much of the archaeological record is known only through old reports.
senses.exampleCN: 考古记录的很大部分只能通过旧报告得知。
senses.why: An unpublished dig is nearly invisible; publication is what turns private notes into a public record.
senses.whyCN: 未发表的发掘几乎不可见；出版才把私人笔记变成公共记录。

senses.title: The register and database
senses.titleCN: 登记册与数据库：编目化的记录
senses.definition: the catalogued list of sites, finds and contexts held in a register or database
senses.definitionCN: 以登记册或数据库形式保存的地点、发现物与情境目录
senses.example: The national archaeological record lists every known burial mound.
senses.exampleCN: 全国考古记录列出了每一处已知的墓葬土丘。
senses.why: Once entries are numbered and indexed, the record becomes searchable, and a searchable past is a different kind of evidence.
senses.whyCN: 一旦条目被编号并建立索引，记录就变得可检索，而可检索的过去是另一种证据。

senses.title: The regional sequence
senses.titleCN: 区域序列：某地区遗存的年代序列
senses.definition: the ordered succession of material from one region, used to place finds in time
senses.definitionCN: 某地区材料的先后序列，用于把发现物定位到时间中
senses.example: The island's archaeological record runs from early farming to the bronze age.
senses.exampleCN: 这座岛的考古记录从早期农耕延续到青铜时代。
senses.why: Materials from one area accumulate into a sequence, and that sequence becomes the local ruler against which new finds are measured.
senses.whyCN: 同一地区的材料累积成序列，这个序列就成为衡量新发现的地方标尺。

senses.title: Bias and incompleteness
senses.titleCN: 偏差与不完整：记录本身的偏向
senses.definition: the distortion in the record caused by what survives, what is found and what is published
senses.definitionCN: 因何物留存、何物被发现、何物被发表而造成的记录偏差
senses.example: Stone survives better, so the archaeological record overstates stone tools.
senses.exampleCN: 石头更易保存，因此考古记录夸大了石器的比重。
senses.why: The record is a sample, not a census: decay, discovery and publication each filter it, and every filter leaves a bias.
senses.whyCN: 记录是样本而非普查：腐朽、发现与发表各是一道筛子，每道筛子都留下偏差。

senses.title: Curation of the archive
senses.titleCN: 档案保存：记录被长期维护的状态
senses.definition: the state of being kept, conserved and made accessible in a museum or archive
senses.definitionCN: 在博物馆或档案馆中被保存、修复并可查阅的状态
senses.example: Poor curation has already damaged part of the archaeological record.
senses.exampleCN: 保存不善已经损坏了部分考古记录。
senses.why: Documentation and objects decay too, so the record needs care; curation is what keeps a past record from becoming a future loss.
senses.whyCN: 档案与物件也会衰败，因此记录需要照料；保存工作防止过去的记录变成未来的损失。

senses.title: The record as a research archive
senses.titleCN: 作为研究资料库的记录
senses.definition: the accumulated body of material and data reused for new questions long after the original dig
senses.definitionCN: 原始发掘结束很久之后，仍被用于新问题的材料与数据总体
senses.example: Old samples in the archaeological record answered a new question about diet.
senses.exampleCN: 考古记录中的旧样本回答了一个关于饮食的新问题。
senses.why: Good records outlive their questions; the archive becomes a mine that later researchers can reopen with new tools.
senses.whyCN: 好的记录比它最初的问题活得更久；资料库成为后来者可用新工具重开的矿。

intro.en: Archaeological record joins Greek archaeology, the study of ancient things, with record, from Latin recordari, to remember. The phrase treats material and documents as one memory of the past. Dates are approximate.
intro.cn: archaeological record 把希腊来源的 archaeology（研究古代事物）与 record 连在一起；record 出自拉丁 recordari「记住」。这个短语把物质与文献当成同一份关于过去的记忆。年代均为约数。

items.en: Cor, genitive cordis, meant heart, and the Romans placed memory in the heart; recordari meant to remember, literally to bring back to the heart.
items.cn: cor（属格 cordis）意为心，罗马人把记忆安置在心里；recordari 意为记住，字面是「重新带回心里」。

items.en: Recordari, built on re-, back, plus cor, produced recorder in Old French and record in English, first as a verb and then as a noun.
items.cn: recordari 由 re-「回」加 cor 构成，经古法语 recorder 产生英语 record，先作动词，后作名词。

items.en: Arkhaios, ancient, plus logos, account, gave the name of the discipline that studies material remains.
items.cn: arkhaios「古老」加 logos「叙述」，构成研究物质遗存之学科的名称。

items.en: Nineteenth-century archaeologists began to speak of a record because the surviving material could be read like an archive, with entries, gaps and losses.
items.cn: 十九世纪考古学者开始谈「记录」，因为留存材料可以像档案一样阅读，有条目、空缺与散失。

items.en: Source uncertain: the date at which the phrase became standard is not documented, and the metaphor of material as a record has been criticised as misleading by later scholars.
items.cn: 来源不确定：这个短语成为标准说法的年代没有文献记载，而把物质比作记录的做法后来也受到学者批评，认为会误导。

note.en: The first group holds phrases that name parts or views of the same archive; the second group holds words for bodies of stored information.
note.cn: 第一组是命名同一档案之部分或视角的短语；第二组是表示储存信息总体的词。

entries.definition: The portion of the record used to support one specific claim; the record is the whole.
entries.definitionCN: 记录中用于支持某一具体论断的部分；记录是整体。

entries.definition: The systematic search that adds new entries to the record rather than the record itself.
entries.definitionCN: 为记录增添新条目的系统搜寻，而非记录本身。

entries.definition: The documentation for a single site, a small unit inside the larger record.
entries.definitionCN: 单个遗址的档案，是更大记录中的一个小编单位。

entries.definition: An organised store of documents; the archaeological record includes objects as well as documents.
entries.definitionCN: 有组织的文献储存；考古记录除文献外还包括实物。

entries.definition: A structured set of searchable entries; it is one modern form of the record, not its whole content.
entries.definitionCN: 可检索条目的结构化集合；它是记录的现代形式之一，而非全部内容。

entries.definition: Evidence given by a witness; it is human speech, while the archaeological record is mostly mute matter.
entries.definitionCN: 证人提供的证据；它出自人的言说，而考古记录多半是无声的物质。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: the heart-rooted memory word, the Greek discipline, the filters of decay and the archive that outlives its dig.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：以「心」为根的记忆词、希腊学科、腐朽造成的筛子，以及比发掘活得更久的档案。

normal.en: recordari, to remember, from cor, heart: the record is the earth's memory.
normal.cn: recordari「记住」出自 cor「心」：记录就是大地的记忆。

normal.en: Archaeology is the Greek account of ancient things, and the record is what that account is built on.
normal.cn: archaeology 是希腊语「关于古代事物的叙述」，记录正是这项叙述的立足处。

normal.en: Digging destroys, so the written record must stand in for what the spade removed.
normal.cn: 发掘会毁坏，因此文字记录必须代替铁锹移走的部分。

normal.en: Three filters shape it: what survives, what is found, what is published.
normal.cn: 三道筛子塑造它：什么留存下来、什么被发现、什么被发表。

normal.en: A good archive outlives its original question and can be reopened later.
normal.cn: 好的档案比它最初的问题活得更久，日后还能被重新打开。

abstract.en: Abstractly, a record is a sample pretending to be a census, and its gaps are as informative as its entries.
abstract.cn: 抽象地看，记录是伪装成普查的样本，它的空缺与条目同样有信息量。

abstract.en: The word fuses matter and memory: what is kept is at once an object and a statement.
abstract.cn: 这个词把物质与记忆熔在一起：被保存的东西既是物件，也是陈述。

abstract.en: Every archive decides what the future will be able to ask.
abstract.cn: 每座档案库都在决定未来能提出什么问题。

examples.en: Coastal sites are poorly represented in the archaeological record.
examples.cn: 海岸遗址在考古记录中所占比例很低。

examples.en: The excavation was never published, so it barely enters the archaeological record.
examples.cn: 这次发掘从未发表，因此几乎未进入考古记录。

examples.en: New dating methods let researchers re-read the same archaeological record.
examples.cn: 新的测年方法让研究者重读同一份考古记录。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「考古（archaeology）+ 记录（record）」——埋在地下、又被写进册子的全部痕迹 → 考古记录

root: 希腊 arkhaios「古老的」+ logos「叙述」构成 archaeology；拉丁 recordari「记住」（re- + cor「心」）构成 record；字面为「关于古代遗存的记忆总体」。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses follow one archive: matter survives, diggers write it down, reports publish it, registers index it, regions order it, filters bias it, curators keep it and later researchers reopen it.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项沿同一座档案库展开：物质留存，发掘者记下，报告发表，登记册编目，区域排序，筛子造成偏差，保管者维护，后来者重开。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: numbered boxes on a shelf beside registers that describe them.
core.cn: 核心意象：架上的编号纸盒，旁边是描述它们的登记册。

branches.en: MATTER AND ORDER: the surviving body gains meaning only when arranged into a regional sequence.
branches.cn: 物质与秩序：留存总体只有排成区域序列才获得意义。

branches.en: WRITING REPLACES DIGGING: notes and reports preserve what the spade destroyed.
branches.cn: 书写替代挖掘：笔记与报告保存了铁锹毁掉的东西。

branches.en: THE INDEX: numbering turns a heap into a searchable record.
branches.cn: 索引：编号把一堆东西变成可检索的记录。

branches.en: THE FILTERS: decay, discovery and publication bias the sample, and care is needed to keep what remains.
branches.cn: 筛子：腐朽、发现与发表使样本带偏，而留存部分需要照料。

branches.en: THE REOPENED MINE: an archive outlives its questions and serves new ones.
branches.cn: 重开的矿：档案比它的问题活得更久，并服务于新问题。

intro.en: Archaeological record is a Greek-Latin hybrid phrase: the discipline from Greek and the memory word from Latin.
intro.cn: archaeological record 是一个希腊—拉丁混合短语：学科名来自希腊语，记忆之词来自拉丁语。

latinIntro.en: Greek arkhaios and logos build archaeology; Latin re- and cor build record, recordari and recorder. English record then extends to recording, recorded and recordation.
latinIntro.cn: 希腊 arkhaios 与 logos 构成 archaeology；拉丁 re- 与 cor 构成 record、recordari、recorder。英语 record 再扩展出 recording、recorded、recordation。

items.example: Arkhaios marks what belongs to an early age.
items.exampleCN: arkhaios 标记属于早期时代之物。

items.example: Logos gives the -logy of archaeology.
items.exampleCN: logos 为 archaeology 提供 -logy。

items.example: Archaeology depends on careful recording.
items.exampleCN: 考古学依赖细致的记录。

items.example: Cor is the root of record and cordial.
items.exampleCN: cor 是 record 与 cordial 的词根。

items.meaning: to remember, to call back to mind
items.example: Recordari is the source of English record.
items.exampleCN: recordari 是英语 record 的来源。

items.meaning: to set down, or a written account
items.example: Every find is recorded with coordinates.
items.exampleCN: 每件发现物都连坐标一起记录。

items.meaning: the act or product of setting down
items.example: Good recording saves a site from oblivion.
items.exampleCN: 良好的记录使遗址免于湮没。

items.meaning: set down in writing or data
items.example: The wall is recorded in plan and section.
items.exampleCN: 这堵墙被记录在平面图与剖面图中。

items.example: The recorder noted the depth of each layer.
items.exampleCN: 记录员记下每一层的深度。

items.example: Recordation of the find took a full day.
items.exampleCN: 这件发现物的登记记录花了一整天。

definition_zh: 考古调查；遗址踏查；区域系统调查
definition_en: the systematic search for and recording of archaeological sites and features, usually without large-scale excavation
core_image: 两个人沿着犁过的田埂慢慢走，每隔十步停一下，把地上的陶片位置记进平板
scene: 犁过的田里，两个人沿着田埂慢慢走，每隔十步停一下，把地上的陶片位置记进平板。In the ploughed field, the archaeological survey advances step by step as each pottery fragment is plotted.
sceneCN: 这里 archaeological survey 指「为发现并记录遗址与遗迹而进行的系统搜寻」（第 1 个义项：以踏查、观测与记录为主、通常不大规模开挖的调查）；句意为两人沿田埂逐段行走，把每片陶片的位置标入平板。可辨识物件：田埂、陶片、平板、测距轮、记录笔。

pos.zh: 考古调查；遗址踏查（可数或不可数）
（调查形成的）调查报告

senses.title: A systematic search without digging
senses.titleCN: 系统调查：不开挖的搜寻与记录
senses.definition: the organised search for sites and features across a landscape, relying on observation and recording rather than excavation
senses.definitionCN: 在较大区域内依靠观察与记录、而非开挖来寻找遗址与遗迹的有组织搜寻
senses.example: The archaeological survey covered the whole valley in one summer.
senses.exampleCN: 这次考古调查在一个夏季内覆盖了整个谷地。
senses.why: Survey comes from Old French surveoir, to oversee, from sur- plus veoir, to see: the work is organised looking before any ground is opened.
senses.whyCN: survey 出自古法语 surveoir「俯视、察看」，由 sur- 加 veoir「看」构成：这项工作是在动土之前的有组织观看。

senses.title: A walkover field check
senses.titleCN: 地面踏查：沿地表步行查看
senses.definition: a survey carried out on foot, recording objects visible on the surface of ploughed or eroded ground
senses.definitionCN: 以步行的方式调查，记录耕地或侵蚀地面上可见的物件
senses.example: Fieldwalking survey found pottery along the ridge.
senses.exampleCN: 地面踏查在山脊沿线发现了陶片。
senses.why: Ploughing brings buried material to the surface, so walking a field is a cheap way to sample what lies below.
senses.whyCN: 耕作把埋藏材料翻到地表，因此在田里行走是取样地下内容的一种低成本方式。

senses.title: Aerial reconnaissance
senses.titleCN: 航空调查：从空中识别遗迹
senses.definition: a survey that reads crop marks, shadows and soil differences from aircraft or drones
senses.definitionCN: 从飞机或无人机上判读作物痕迹、阴影与土壤差异的调查
senses.example: Aerial survey revealed a buried road across the plain.
senses.exampleCN: 航空调查揭示出一条横穿平原的埋藏道路。
senses.why: Buried walls change how crops grow and how soil dries, so a pattern visible from above can be a plan of what is below.
senses.whyCN: 埋藏的墙会改变作物生长与土壤干湿，因此从上方可见的图案可能就是地下布局的平面图。

senses.title: Remote sensing survey
senses.titleCN: 遥感调查：用传感器扫描地表
senses.definition: a survey using satellite or airborne sensors such as radar and multispectral imaging
senses.definitionCN: 使用卫星或机载传感器（如雷达与多光谱成像）进行的调查
senses.example: The remote sensing survey mapped moisture across the desert.
senses.exampleCN: 遥感调查绘制了沙漠中的湿度分布。
senses.why: Sensors see beyond visible light, and differences in moisture or temperature can expose structures that no eye would catch.
senses.whyCN: 传感器能看到可见光之外的信息，湿度或温度的差异可以让肉眼无法察觉的结构显露出来。

senses.title: Geophysical prospection
senses.titleCN: 地球物理勘探：用仪器探测地下
senses.definition: a survey that measures magnetism, resistance or radar reflection to detect buried features before digging
senses.definitionCN: 通过测量磁性、电阻或雷达反射，在开挖前探测地下遗迹的调查
senses.example: The geophysical survey outlined a ditched enclosure.
senses.exampleCN: 地球物理勘探勾勒出一处带沟的围栏。
senses.why: Different materials respond differently to fields and currents, so an instrument can feel the shape of a wall through the soil.
senses.whyCN: 不同材料对场与电流的响应不同，因此仪器可以隔着土壤摸到墙的形状。

senses.title: A sample-based survey
senses.titleCN: 抽样调查：按样本推断整体
senses.definition: a survey designed around sampled transects or squares so that results can be generalised statistically
senses.definitionCN: 围绕抽样样带或方格设计、使结果可作统计推广的调查
senses.example: The sample survey estimated site density per square kilometre.
senses.exampleCN: 抽样调查估算了每平方公里的遗址密度。
senses.why: Whole landscapes are too large to walk completely, so a designed sample lets a small walked fraction stand for the whole.
senses.whyCN: 整片景观太大，无法全部走完，因此经过设计的样本让一小部分踏查结果代表整体。

senses.title: A site inventory survey
senses.titleCN: 遗址登记调查：为名录收集信息
senses.definition: a survey whose purpose is to list, describe and assess sites for protection or planning
senses.definitionCN: 以列入名录、描述与评估遗址以供保护或规划为目的的调查
senses.example: The inventory survey recorded forty new sites.
senses.exampleCN: 这次遗址登记调查记录了四十处新遗址。
senses.why: Protection begins with a list; the survey becomes an administrative instrument as much as a research one.
senses.whyCN: 保护从一份名录开始；这项调查因此既是研究工具，也是行政工具。

senses.title: The written survey report
senses.titleCN: 调查报告：调查形成的书面成果
senses.definition: the published or archived report presenting the methods, results and interpretation of a survey
senses.definitionCN: 呈现调查方法、结果与解释的已发表或归档报告
senses.example: The archaeological survey is held in the county archive.
senses.exampleCN: 这份考古调查报告保存在郡档案馆。
senses.why: Survey as a countable noun can name the document; the same word covers both the looking and its paper trace.
senses.whyCN: survey 作可数名词时可指文件；同一个词既涵盖观看，也涵盖它留下的纸面痕迹。

intro.en: Archaeological survey joins Greek archaeology with survey, which came through Old French from Latin supervidere, to look over. The phrase names organised looking before digging. Dates are approximate.
intro.cn: archaeological survey 把希腊来源的 archaeology 与 survey 连在一起；survey 经古法语来自拉丁 supervidere「俯视、察看」。这个短语指动土之前的有组织观看。年代均为约数。

items.en: Videre meant to see, and it builds vision, visible, video and survey alike; the survey sense is literally a way of seeing.
items.cn: videre 意为看见，它构成 vision、visible、video 与 survey；survey 义字面上就是一种看的方式。

items.en: Super, over, plus videre, to see, gave supervidere, to look over or inspect; Old French made it surveoir.
items.cn: super「在上」加 videre「看」构成 supervidere「俯视、检查」；古法语把它变成 surveoir。

items.en: English survey first meant to oversee or inspect, then to measure land, and finally to gather systematic information of any kind.
items.cn: 英语 survey 最初意为监督、检查，继而指测量土地，最后指系统收集任何类型的信息。

items.en: As archaeology professionalised, survey was set against excavation: one reads the surface, the other reads the depth.
items.cn: 随着考古学专业化，survey 与 excavation 形成对照：一个读地表，一个读深处。

items.en: Source uncertain: the exact date when survey acquired its archaeological sense is not fixed, and early uses overlap with simple land measurement.
items.cn: 来源不确定：survey 获得考古义的确切年代没有定论，早期用法与单纯的土地测量相互重叠。

note.en: The first group holds terms for survey methods; the second group holds words for search and examination.
note.cn: 第一组是调查方法的术语；第二组是搜寻与检查类的词。

entries.definition: Digging to expose deposits; survey reads the surface before any digging starts.
entries.definitionCN: 开挖以揭露堆积；调查则在动土之前先读地表。

entries.definition: The archaeological term for searching a landscape for sites, especially by geophysical means.
entries.definitionCN: 考古学中指在景观中寻找遗址的术语，尤指用地球物理手段。

entries.definition: A preliminary look to decide where to work; a survey may be systematic rather than merely preliminary.
entries.definitionCN: 为决定在哪里工作而做的初步察看；调查可以是系统的，而不只是初步的。

entries.definition: The resulting catalogue of sites; the survey is the activity, the inventory is the record.
entries.definitionCN: 调查产生的遗址名录；survey 是活动，inventory 是记录。

entries.definition: The production of maps from observations; a survey may end in a map but is not only cartography.
entries.definitionCN: 由观察制作地图；调查可能以地图收尾，但不等同于制图。

entries.definition: A close look to check condition or quality; it lacks the systematic coverage that defines a survey.
entries.definitionCN: 为检查状况或质量而细看；缺少调查所要求的系统覆盖。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: the seeing root, the surface-before-depth contrast, the sample and the report.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：表示「看」的词根、先地表后深处的对照、抽样，以及报告。

normal.en: videre, to see, gives survey: it is organised looking.
normal.cn: videre「看见」派生 survey：它是有组织的观看。

normal.en: Survey reads the surface; excavation reads the depth.
normal.cn: 调查读地表；发掘读深处。

normal.en: Ploughing lifts buried material, so a walked field is a sample of what lies below.
normal.cn: 耕作把埋藏材料翻上来，因此走过一块田就是对地下的取样。

normal.en: Geophysics lets an instrument feel a wall through the soil.
normal.cn: 地球物理让仪器隔着土壤摸到墙。

normal.en: Survey also names the report, so the word covers both the looking and its paper trace.
normal.cn: survey 也指报告，因此这个词既包括观看，也包括它的纸面痕迹。

abstract.en: Abstractly, a survey is a decision about where to look, made before anything is touched.
abstract.cn: 抽象地看，调查是在触碰任何东西之前，关于「往哪里看」的决定。

abstract.en: Sampling turns an impossible whole into a defensible fraction.
abstract.cn: 抽样把一个不可能走完的整体变成一个可辩护的分数。

abstract.en: Every survey chooses what counts as a site, and that choice is already interpretation.
abstract.cn: 每项调查都在选择什么算作遗址，而这个选择已经是解释。

examples.en: The survey found no evidence of settlement on the upper slopes.
examples.cn: 调查在上部坡地没有发现聚落证据。

examples.en: A geophysical survey was run before the trench was opened.
examples.cn: 在开挖探方之前先做了一次地球物理勘探。

examples.en: The survey report lists every field walked and every find plotted.
examples.cn: 调查报告列出走过的每块田与标出的每件发现物。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「考古（archaeology）+ 察看（survey）」——不动土，先用眼睛把地面看一遍 → 考古调查

root: 希腊 arkhaios「古老的」+ logos「研究」构成 archaeology；拉丁 super「在上」+ videre「看」经古法语形成 survey；字面为「对古代遗存的有组织察看」。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses follow one look: the search is organised, then carried out on foot, from the air, by sensor, by instrument, by sample, for a register, and finally written down.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项沿同一次观看展开：搜寻先被组织，再依次以步行、空中、传感器、仪器、抽样方式进行，为名录服务，最后写成文字。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: two walkers crossing a ploughed field, stopping to plot each fragment.
core.cn: 核心意象：两人穿过犁过的田，每见一片陶片就停下来标点。

branches.en: THE WALKED SURFACE: the first survey is a pair of eyes moving across open ground.
branches.cn: 走过的地表：最初的调查就是一双眼睛在开阔地面上移动。

branches.en: SEEING FROM ABOVE: aircraft and satellites extend the same look to a scale the walker cannot reach.
branches.cn: 从上方看：飞机与卫星把同一种观看扩展到步行者达不到的尺度。

branches.en: FEELING THROUGH SOIL: instruments substitute for eyes where the ground is opaque.
branches.cn: 隔着土摸：在地面不透明处，仪器代替了眼睛。

branches.en: THE FRACTION: sampling makes an unwalkable whole answerable.
branches.cn: 分数：抽样使走不完的整体变得可回答。

branches.en: THE LIST AND THE BOOK: results become an inventory, then a report that others can read.
branches.cn: 名录与书：结果先成为名录，再成为他人可读的报告。

intro.en: Archaeological survey is a Greek-Latin hybrid: a Greek discipline name plus a Latin verb of seeing.
intro.cn: archaeological survey 是希腊—拉丁混合短语：一个希腊学科名，加一个拉丁「看」的动词。

latinIntro.en: Latin videre, to see, builds vision, visible, video, supervise and survey; Greek arkhaios and logos build archaeology. Survey adds sur-, over, to the act of seeing.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁 videre「看见」构成 vision、visible、video、supervise、survey；希腊 arkhaios 与 logos 构成 archaeology。survey 在「看」的动作上加 sur-「在上」。

items.example: Videre is the root of vision and survey.
items.exampleCN: videre 是 vision 与 survey 的词根。

items.example: The prefix gives the sense of looking down from above.
items.exampleCN: 这个前缀带来从上方俯视的意思。

items.example: Supervidere passed into Old French as surveoir.
items.exampleCN: supervidere 传入古法语成为 surveoir。

items.example: They surveyed the field on foot.
items.exampleCN: 他们步行调查了这块田。

items.example: The surveyor marked each transect.
items.exampleCN: 调查员标出了每条样带。

items.example: Surveying continued through the dry season.
items.exampleCN: 调查在旱季持续进行。

items.example: A senior archaeologist supervised the survey.
items.exampleCN: 一位资深考古学家监督这次调查。

items.meaning: the act or power of seeing
items.example: Vision and survey share the same Latin verb.
items.exampleCN: vision 与 survey 共用同一个拉丁动词。

items.example: Surface finds are visible after ploughing.
items.exampleCN: 耕作之后地表发现物可见。

items.example: Archaeology and survey grew up together.
items.exampleCN: 考古学与调查方法一同成长。

latinEntries.structure: super- + videre (Latin verb, to look over)

definition_zh: 地层学；层序学；考古地层；分层结构
definition_en: the study of the order, position and age of layered deposits, used in geology and archaeology to establish sequences
core_image: 一面陡壁被刮平，深浅不同的土带一层压一层，最下面的一层最老，最上面的一层最新
scene: 探方一侧的土壁被刮得平整，深浅不同的土带一层压着一层，最底下的土色最深。The exposed wall shows stratigraphy as bands of soil stacked oldest at the bottom and youngest at the top.
sceneCN: 这里 stratigraphy 指「堆积层按上下顺序排列所构成的层序及其研究」（第 2 个义项：地层序列本身）；句意为刮平的土壁上，不同颜色的土层依次叠压，最下面的最老、最上面的最新。可辨识物件：土壁、土层带、刮刀、比例尺、层位线。

pos.zh: 地层学；层序学
地层序列；层位关系（不可数）

senses.title: The study of layered order
senses.titleCN: 地层学：研究层序的学科
senses.definition: the branch of geology and archaeology that studies how layers form, succeed and correlate
senses.definitionCN: 研究层如何形成、先后相接与对比的地质学与考古学分支
senses.example: Stratigraphy tells us which deposit formed first.
senses.exampleCN: 地层学告诉我们哪一层堆积先形成。
senses.why: Stratum is Latin for a layer spread out, from sternere, to spread; -graphy is Greek for writing, so the word means writing about layers.
senses.whyCN: stratum 是拉丁语「铺开的一层」，出自 sternere「铺展」；-graphy 是希腊语「书写」，因此这个词意为「对层的书写」。

senses.title: The layering itself
senses.titleCN: 层序：土层的实际排列
senses.definition: the actual arrangement of layers at a place, read from a section or a core
senses.definitionCN: 某地点通过剖面或岩芯读出的层的实际排列
senses.example: The stratigraphy at the trench edge is unusually clear.
senses.exampleCN: 探方边缘的层序异常清楚。
senses.why: The same word names both the discipline and its object, just as geology names both a science and a rock face.
senses.whyCN: 同一个词既指学科，也指其对象，正如 geology 既指地质学也指一处岩面。

senses.title: Archaeological stratigraphy
senses.titleCN: 考古地层：人类活动形成的堆积层序
senses.definition: the sequence of deposits made by human activity, such as floors, fills and dumps, and their cut relationships
senses.definitionCN: 由人类活动形成的堆积顺序，如居住面、填土与废弃物，及其切压关系
senses.example: Archaeological stratigraphy records a floor cut by a later pit.
senses.exampleCN: 考古地层记录了一个被后期灰坑打破的居住面。
senses.why: People also make layers, and they cut into older ones; the discipline reads both accumulation and intrusion.
senses.whyCN: 人也会制造层，并切穿更早的层；这门学科既读堆积，也读侵入。

senses.title: Correlation between sections
senses.titleCN: 地层对比：把分离的剖面接起来
senses.definition: the matching of layers across different places so that separate sequences can be joined
senses.definitionCN: 把不同地点的层相互对应，使分离的序列得以连接
senses.example: Stratigraphy links the two sides of the valley.
senses.exampleCN: 地层对比把谷地两侧连接起来。
senses.why: A layer exposed in one place is not the same layer everywhere; correlation uses colour, texture and contained finds to match them.
senses.whyCN: 在一处露出的层并不等于各处的同一层；对比依靠颜色、质地与所含发现物把它们配对。

senses.title: Rock-layer geology
senses.titleCN: 岩层学：地质上的成层研究
senses.definition: the geological study of sedimentary rock layers and their ages
senses.definitionCN: 对沉积岩层及其年代的地质学研究
senses.example: Stratigraphy placed the limestone below the sandstone.
senses.exampleCN: 地层学把石灰岩定在砂岩之下。
senses.why: The discipline began with rock, not with graves; sedimentary layers accumulate in order and carry the oldest at the bottom.
senses.whyCN: 这门学科起初研究岩石，而非墓葬；沉积层按顺序堆积，最老的位于底部。

senses.title: The law of superposition
senses.titleCN: 叠加律：上覆者晚于下伏者
senses.definition: the principle that in an undisturbed sequence the upper layer is younger than the layer below it
senses.definitionCN: 在未受扰动的序列中，上层晚于其下层的原理
senses.example: Stratigraphy assumed the rule held until a burrow was found.
senses.exampleCN: 地层学一直假定这条规律成立，直到发现一处动物洞穴。
senses.why: The rule is the whole basis of relative dating, and its exceptions, such as pits and burrows, are what fieldworkers watch for.
senses.whyCN: 这条规律是相对测年的全部基础，而灰坑与洞穴等例外正是田野工作者要留意的。

senses.title: Reading a section
senses.titleCN: 判读剖面：清理剖面并绘出层界
senses.definition: the practical skill of interpreting a cleaned section and drawing its layer boundaries
senses.definitionCN: 判读清理过的剖面并绘出层界线的实践技能
senses.example: Her stratigraphy of the section was checked by a second recorder.
senses.exampleCN: 她对剖面的层序判读由第二位记录员复核。
senses.why: Layers are not labelled in the ground; the reader must decide where one ends and the next begins, and that decision is an interpretation.
senses.whyCN: 层在地下并没有标签；判读者必须决定一层在哪里结束、下一层在哪里开始，而这个决定本身就是解释。

senses.title: Layered structure as metaphor
senses.titleCN: 分层结构：比喻意义上的层次
senses.definition: any system read as stacked levels, such as a text, a society or a set of rules
senses.definitionCN: 任何被当作叠置层次来读的系统，如文本、社会或一套规则
senses.example: The historian applied stratigraphy to the layers of the law.
senses.exampleCN: 这位历史学者把分层结构用于法律的各个层次。
senses.why: Once layers mean order, the image travels: anything built up over time can be read from bottom to top.
senses.whyCN: 一旦层意味着顺序，这个意象就会迁移：任何随时间累积的东西都可以从下往上读。

intro.en: Stratigraphy joins Latin stratum, a layer, with Greek -graphia, writing. The term was coined for geology in the nineteenth century and later borrowed by archaeology. Dates are approximate.
intro.cn: stratigraphy 把拉丁 stratum「层」与希腊 -graphia「书写」连在一起。这个词十九世纪为地质学而造，后来被考古学借用。年代均为约数。

items.en: Sternere meant to spread out or lay flat; its participle stratus gave stratum, a layer spread over a surface.
items.cn: sternere 意为铺开、摊平；其分词 stratus 产生 stratum，即铺在表面上的一层。

items.en: Stratum named a bed or layer, and the plural strata became the standard word for rock and soil layers.
items.cn: stratum 指一层或一层床，复数 strata 成为岩石与土壤层的标准词。

items.en: Greek graphein, to write, gave -graphia, a writing or description; geography, biography and stratigraphy all use it.
items.cn: 希腊 graphein「书写」产生 -graphia，即书写或描述；geography、biography、stratigraphy 都用它。

items.en: Geologists needed a word for the description of layered rock, and stratigraphy supplied it; the principles of superposition and correlation came with it.
items.cn: 地质学家需要一个词来描述成层岩石，stratigraphy 正好补上；叠加与对比原理随之而来。

items.en: Archaeologists borrowed the term for human deposits, adding cuts and fills to the geological vocabulary of layers.
items.cn: 考古学者把这个词借用于人类堆积，在层的地质词汇中加入切与填。

items.en: Source uncertain: the coinage is generally attributed to nineteenth-century geologists, but no single author and date are agreed, and the first use in archaeology is also undocumented.
items.cn: 来源不确定：这个词的创造一般归给十九世纪的地质学家，但没有公认的单一作者与年代，它在考古学中的首次使用同样缺乏记载。

note.en: The first group holds terms from the same layer stock; the second group holds words for ordering and for layers.
note.cn: 第一组是同出「层」词干的术语；第二组是表示排序与层的词。

entries.definition: A single layer; stratigraphy is the study of many layers and their order.
entries.definitionCN: 单独的一层；stratigraphy 是研究多层及其顺序的学科。

entries.definition: Relating to stratigraphy; it describes a relationship or a position, not the discipline.
entries.definitionCN: 与地层学有关的；它描述关系或位置，而非学科本身。

entries.definition: The atmospheric layer named from the same Latin word for layer, but it has nothing to do with deposits.
entries.definitionCN: 大气层名，借用了同一个拉丁「层」词，但与堆积无关。

entries.definition: The study of the earth as a whole; stratigraphy is one of its core methods.
entries.definitionCN: 研究整个地球的学科；地层学是其核心方法之一。

entries.definition: The order in which things follow one another; stratigraphy is the reading of that order in deposits.
entries.definitionCN: 事物相继出现的顺序；地层学是从堆积中读出这个顺序。

entries.definition: The layer and association in which an object lies; stratigraphy supplies the framework for context.
entries.definitionCN: 物件所在的层与共存关系；地层学为情境提供框架。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: the spreading root, the writing suffix, superposition and the two-section match.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：表示铺展的词根、书写后缀、叠加律，以及两个剖面的对比。

normal.en: sternere, to spread, gives stratum: a layer is something spread over a surface.
normal.cn: sternere「铺展」派生 stratum：层就是铺在表面上的东西。

normal.en: -graphy is writing: stratigraphy is writing about layers.
normal.cn: -graphy 是书写：stratigraphy 就是书写层。

normal.en: Superposition: in an undisturbed stack, the top is youngest and the bottom is oldest.
normal.cn: 叠加律：在未受扰动的叠层中，最上面最新，最下面最老。

normal.en: Pits and burrows cut older layers, and those cuts must be read as later events.
normal.cn: 灰坑与洞穴切穿更老的层，这些切口必须当作更晚的事件来读。

normal.en: Correlation matches colour, texture and finds to join separate sections.
normal.cn: 对比依靠颜色、质地与发现物，把分离的剖面接起来。

abstract.en: Abstractly, stratigraphy is time made visible as order: the vertical axis is history.
abstract.cn: 抽象地看，地层学是把时间变成可见的顺序：竖轴就是历史。

abstract.en: It is the art of reading interruption: what cuts what tells you what came later.
abstract.cn: 它是判读打断的技艺：谁切穿了谁，就告诉你谁更晚。

abstract.en: Any archive, text or institution built up over time can be read as a stack of layers.
abstract.cn: 任何随时间累积的档案、文本或制度，都可以当作一摞层来读。

examples.en: The pit cuts the floor, so by stratigraphy the pit is later.
examples.cn: 灰坑切穿了居住面，因此按地层关系灰坑更晚。

examples.en: Without stratigraphy, the finds would have no order at all.
examples.cn: 没有地层，这些发现物就完全没有顺序。

examples.en: The two sections were correlated by their stratigraphy.
examples.cn: 两个剖面通过地层对比被连接起来。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「strata（层）+ graphy（写）」——把一层层土写成一张剖面图 → 地层学

root: 拉丁 stratum「铺开的一层」（出自 sternere「铺展」）+ 希腊 -graphia「书写、描述」；字面为「对层的书写」。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses follow one stack: the discipline reads the layers, the layers themselves, human deposits, matched sections, rock strata, the rule of superposition, the act of reading and the metaphor of levels.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项沿同一叠层展开：学科读层，层本身，人类堆积，剖面对比，岩层，叠加律，判读行为，以及层次的比喻。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a cleaned wall of soil, bands stacking oldest to youngest.
core.cn: 核心意象：一面刮净的土壁，土带自老至新依次叠压。

branches.en: THE DISCIPLINE AND THE ROCK: the same reading applies to soil and to sedimentary stone.
branches.cn: 学科与岩石：同一套读法既用于土壤，也用于沉积岩。

branches.en: NATURAL AND HUMAN STACKS: people add floors, fills and cuts to the natural sequence.
branches.cn: 自然叠层与人类叠层：人在自然序列上添加居住面、填土与切口。

branches.en: JOINING SECTIONS: correlation turns separate walls into one regional sequence.
branches.cn: 连接剖面：对比把分离的土壁连成一个区域序列。

branches.en: THE RULE AND THE READING: superposition gives the logic, and the recorder applies it at the section.
branches.cn: 规律与判读：叠加律提供逻辑，记录员在剖面上应用它。

branches.en: LAYERS EVERYWHERE: once order is visible as a stack, any accumulated system can borrow the image.
branches.cn: 处处有层：一旦顺序可见为一摞，任何累积系统都能借用这个意象。

intro.en: Stratigraphy is a Latin-Greek compound, and both halves build many English technical words.
intro.cn: stratigraphy 是一个拉丁—希腊复合词，两半都构成大量英语技术词。

latinIntro.en: Latin sternere, to spread, gives stratum, stratus and stratify; Greek graphein, to write, gives -graphy, -graph and graphic. The compound names the description of layers.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁 sternere「铺展」衍生 stratum、stratus、stratify；希腊 graphein「书写」衍生 -graphy、-graph、graphic。这个复合词命名对层的描述。

items.structure: sternere (Latin verb, to spread out, lay flat)
items.example: Sternere gives stratum and prostration.
items.exampleCN: sternere 衍生 stratum 与 prostration。

items.structure: stratum (Latin noun, a layer spread out)
items.example: Each stratum held a different kind of soil.
items.exampleCN: 每一层土质都不同。

items.example: The strata dip toward the river.
items.exampleCN: 这些层向河流方向倾斜。

items.example: Water and wind stratify the sediment.
items.exampleCN: 水和风使沉积物分层。

items.example: The stratified sand records repeated floods.
items.exampleCN: 分层砂记录了一次次洪水。

items.example: Stratification takes centuries in still water.
items.exampleCN: 在静水中分层需要数百年。

items.example: Graphein supplies the -graphy of many fields.
items.exampleCN: graphein 为许多领域提供 -graphy。

items.meaning: writing or description of a field
items.meaningCN: 某一领域的书写或描述
items.example: Geography and stratigraphy share the suffix.
items.exampleCN: geography 与 stratigraphy 共用这个后缀。

items.meaning: relating to layers or their order
items.example: The stratigraphic boundary is marked in red.
items.exampleCN: 地层界线用红色标出。

items.example: The stratigrapher checked the section.
items.exampleCN: 地层专家检查了这个剖面。

definition_zh: 地层的；层序的；地层学的；按层位判定的
definition_en: relating to the order and position of layers, or determined by a layer's place in a sequence
core_image: 两条剖面隔着山谷相望，同样颜色的土带被一条虚线连起来，标出它们属于同一层
scene: 两条相隔很远的剖面被画在同一张图上，同样颜色的土带之间用虚线相连，表示它们属于同一层。The drawing links the two sections with dashed lines where the stratigraphic bands match.
sceneCN: 这里 stratigraphic 指「与层的顺序和位置有关的」（第 1 个义项：描述层序关系的形容词用法）；句意为图上用虚线把两条剖面中颜色相同的土带对应起来，说明它们属同一层。可辨识物件：剖面图、色带、虚线、标高线、图例。

pos.zh: 地层的；层序的；地层学的
按层位判定的；层位上的

senses.title: Relating to layer order
senses.titleCN: 地层的：与层的顺序有关的
senses.definition: relating to the order in which layers are arranged
senses.definitionCN: 与层排列的先后顺序有关的
senses.example: The stratigraphic order of the deposits is clear.
senses.exampleCN: 这些堆积的地层顺序很清楚。
senses.why: The adjective simply attaches the noun stratigraphy to whatever it describes, so anything about layer order can be called stratigraphic.
senses.whyCN: 这个形容词只是把名词 stratigraphy 附着到所修饰的对象上，因此任何关于层序的东西都可以称为 stratigraphic。

senses.title: Determined by position in a sequence
senses.titleCN: 按层位判定的：由所在层位决定
senses.definition: fixed or dated by where an object lies within a layer sequence
senses.definitionCN: 由物件在层序中的位置来确定或断代
senses.example: Its stratigraphic position makes it later than the wall.
senses.exampleCN: 它的层位说明它晚于那堵墙。
senses.why: Position is the argument: if the object lies above a layer, it must have arrived after that layer formed.
senses.whyCN: 位置就是论据：如果物件位于某一层之上，它必定在该层形成之后才到达。

senses.title: Belonging to the discipline
senses.titleCN: 地层学的：属于该学科的
senses.definition: belonging to the study of layers as a field of research
senses.definitionCN: 属于以层为研究对象的学科领域
senses.example: The paper is a stratigraphic study of the basin.
senses.exampleCN: 这篇论文是对该盆地的地层学研究。
senses.why: The same adjective can label a work, a method or a specialist as belonging to the discipline rather than to a single layer.
senses.whyCN: 同一个形容词可以标记一项工作、一种方法或一位专家属于该学科，而不是属于某一层。

senses.title: Descriptive of a boundary
senses.titleCN: 层界的：描述两层之间界线的
senses.definition: relating to the contact surface where one layer ends and the next begins
senses.definitionCN: 与一层结束、下一层开始之接触面有关的
senses.example: The stratigraphic boundary is sharp and undulating.
senses.exampleCN: 这条地层界线清晰而起伏。
senses.why: Boundaries are where the reading happens: a sharp line means a sudden change, a gradual one means slow accumulation.
senses.whyCN: 界线正是判读发生之处：界线清晰意味着突变，渐变意味着缓慢堆积。

senses.title: Used in correlation
senses.titleCN: 用于对比的：把分离的层对应起来
senses.definition: relating to the matching of layers between separate places
senses.definitionCN: 与把不同地点的层相互对应有关的
senses.example: Stratigraphic correlation connects the two valleys.
senses.exampleCN: 地层对比把两个谷地连接起来。
senses.why: Correlation is an adjective-level claim: two bands are said to be stratigraphically equivalent when they can be matched.
senses.whyCN: 对比是一种形容词层面的主张：两条土带可以配对时，就说它们在地层上相当。

senses.title: Archaeologically layered
senses.titleCN: 考古地层的：人类堆积的层位
senses.definition: relating to human-made deposits and their cut-and-fill relations
senses.definitionCN: 与人类造成的堆积及其切填关系有关的
senses.example: The stratigraphic record includes floors, pits and dumps.
senses.exampleCN: 考古地层记录包括居住面、灰坑与废弃物。
senses.why: In archaeology the adjective marks deposits that people made, where the sequence also records digging and filling.
senses.whyCN: 在考古学中，这个形容词标记人造成的堆积，那里的序列也记录挖掘与填充。

senses.title: Arranged in levels
senses.titleCN: 分层排列的：比喻意义上的层次
senses.definition: used figuratively for anything organised as a series of levels
senses.definitionCN: 比喻任何按一系列层次组织的事物
senses.example: The novel has a stratigraphic structure of voices.
senses.exampleCN: 这部小说有一层叠一层的声音结构。
senses.why: The adjective travels with the metaphor: once a system is imagined as layers, its parts can be called stratigraphic too.
senses.whyCN: 这个形容词随比喻迁移：一旦某系统被想象成层，其各部分也可称为 stratigraphic。

senses.title: Between two layers
senses.titleCN: 层间的：位于两层之间的
senses.definition: relating to what lies between layers, such as a thin seam or a gap
senses.definitionCN: 与位于层之间的东西（如薄夹层或缺失）有关的
senses.example: A thin stratigraphic seam separates the two phases.
senses.exampleCN: 一条薄薄的层间夹层把两个阶段分开。
senses.why: The space between layers is also part of the order, and a thin seam can mark a pause in deposition.
senses.whyCN: 层与层之间的空间同样属于顺序，一条薄夹层可以标记堆积中的一次停顿。

intro.en: Stratigraphic is the adjective from stratigraphy, built on Latin stratum, layer, and Greek -graphia, writing, with the English adjective ending -ic. Dates are approximate.
intro.cn: stratigraphic 是 stratigraphy 的形容词形式，由拉丁 stratum「层」与希腊 -graphia「书写」构成，再加英语形容词词尾 -ic。年代均为约数。

items.en: Stratum, a layer spread out, comes from sternere, to spread; the adjective keeps the noun stem strat- unchanged.
items.cn: stratum 指铺开的一层，出自 sternere「铺展」；形容词保留了名词词干 strat-。

items.en: The noun stratigraphy ends in -graphy from Greek graphein, to write; the adjective replaces -y with -ic.
items.cn: 名词 stratigraphy 以希腊 graphein「书写」而来的 -graphy 结尾；形容词把 -y 换成 -ic。

items.en: Both noun and adjective appeared with the rise of layered geology, and the adjective was needed as soon as people spoke of stratigraphic position and correlation.
items.cn: 名词与形容词随成层地质学的兴起而出现；一旦人们谈论层位与对比，形容词便成为必需。

items.en: Archaeology took the noun and the adjective together, applying them to human deposits without changing their form.
items.cn: 考古学把名词与形容词一并借来，用于人类堆积，形式未变。

items.en: Source uncertain: the first recorded use of the adjective is not fixed, and the variant stratigraphical competes with stratigraphic without a clear rule.
items.cn: 来源不确定：这个形容词的首次记录使用年代没有定论，异体 stratigraphical 与 stratigraphic 并存，并无明确规则。

note.en: The first group holds forms of the same word family; the second group holds adjectives for ordered or layered things.
note.cn: 第一组是同一词族的各种形式；第二组是表示有序或成层的形容词。

entries.definition: The discipline or the layer sequence itself; the adjective only describes something as related to it.
entries.definitionCN: 指学科或层序本身；形容词只描述某物与之相关。

entries.definition: The longer variant of the same adjective, common in older British writing.
entries.definitionCN: 同一形容词的较长变体，多见于较早的英式写作。

entries.definition: The single layer that the adjective refers to; stratigraphic never names the layer itself.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词所指的单个层；stratigraphic 本身从不指称那一层。

entries.definition: Simply having layers, with no claim about their order or age.
entries.definitionCN: 只是有层，并不主张其顺序或年代。

entries.definition: Following one after another; it states order without the geological image.
entries.definitionCN: 一个接一个；它陈述顺序，却不带地质意象。

entries.definition: Describing rock formed from deposited material; stratigraphic concerns the order, not the material.
entries.definitionCN: 描述由沉积物形成的岩石；stratigraphic 关心顺序，而非材料。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: the -ic adjective ending, the lateral -y to -ic shift, and the position argument.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：-ic 形容词词尾、-y 到 -ic 的转换，以及位置作为论据。

normal.en: stratigraphy minus -y plus -ic gives stratigraphic, the ordinary English adjective pattern.
normal.cn: stratigraphy 去 -y 加 -ic 得 stratigraphic，这是英语常见的形容词构成方式。

normal.en: Stratigraphic position is the argument: above a layer means after it.
normal.cn: 层位就是论据：在某层之上，意味着在它之后。

normal.en: A stratigraphic boundary is where one layer stops and the next starts.
normal.cn: 地层界线是一层结束、下一层开始的地方。

normal.en: Stratigraphic correlation matches bands between distant sections.
normal.cn: 地层对比把相隔很远的剖面中土带配对。

normal.en: The variant stratigraphical is longer but means exactly the same.
normal.cn: 异体 stratigraphical 更长，但意思完全相同。

abstract.en: Abstractly, the adjective converts a science into a property: anything with an order can be called stratigraphic.
abstract.cn: 抽象地看，这个形容词把一门学科转成一种属性：任何具有顺序的东西都能被称为 stratigraphic。

abstract.en: Saying something is stratigraphically later is a claim about reading, not about the object alone.
abstract.cn: 说某物在地层上更晚，是关于判读的主张，而不只关于物件本身。

abstract.en: The word reminds us that position can be a form of evidence.
abstract.cn: 这个词提醒我们：位置本身可以是证据的一种形式。

examples.en: The two finds are stratigraphically equivalent.
examples.cn: 这两件发现物在层位上相当。

examples.en: Stratigraphic evidence places the burial above the collapsed floor.
examples.cn: 地层证据把这处墓葬定在塌陷地面之上。

examples.en: A stratigraphic gap separates the two occupations.
examples.cn: 一段地层缺失把两次居住分开。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「strata（层）+ graphic（描绘的）」——把层画出来的 → 地层的、层位的

root: 拉丁 stratum「层」+ 希腊 -graphia「书写」构成 stratigraphy，再加形容词词尾 -ic；字面为「与层的书写、层序有关的」。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses follow one order: the adjective describes layer order, position as proof, the discipline, a boundary, correlation, human deposits, metaphor and the space between layers.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项沿同一个顺序展开：这个形容词描述层序、位置即证据、学科归属、界线、对比、人类堆积、比喻，以及层间空间。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: two separate sections joined by dashed lines where the bands match.
core.cn: 核心意象：两条分离的剖面在土带相配处以虚线相连。

branches.en: ORDER AS PROPERTY: the adjective turns the discipline into a quality that work, method or person can carry.
branches.cn: 顺序作为属性：这个形容词把学科转成工作、方法或人可携带的性质。

branches.en: POSITION AS PROOF: being above or below is the argument itself.
branches.cn: 位置即证据：在上或在下本身就是论据。

branches.en: THE CONTACT AND THE GAP: boundaries and thin seams carry as much information as the layers.
branches.cn: 接触面与空缺：界线与薄夹层携带的信息不亚于层本身。

branches.en: THE MATCH: correlation is the adjective applied across space.
branches.cn: 配对：对比是这个形容词跨空间的运用。

branches.en: HUMAN LAYERS AND METAPHOR: the term serves excavated deposits and then any stacked system.
branches.cn: 人类层与比喻：这个词先服务发掘堆积，再扩展到任何叠置系统。

intro.en: Stratigraphic is a transparent adjective: a Latin layer noun, a Greek writing suffix and an English adjective ending.
intro.cn: stratigraphic 是一个透明的形容词：拉丁「层」名词、希腊「书写」后缀与英语形容词词尾。

latinIntro.en: Latin sternere and stratum supply strat-; Greek graphein supplies -graph-; English -ic closes the word. The same pieces build stratigraphy, stratigrapher and stratigraphical.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁 sternere 与 stratum 提供 strat-；希腊 graphein 提供 -graph-；英语 -ic 收尾。相同成分构成 stratigraphy、stratigrapher、stratigraphical。

items.example: The lowest stratum is the oldest.
items.exampleCN: 最下面的一层最老。

items.example: Sediment is spread out by water and then buried.
items.exampleCN: 沉积物被水铺开后又被埋藏。

items.example: Graphein gives the -graph- of stratigraphic.
items.exampleCN: graphein 为 stratigraphic 提供 -graph-。

items.example: Stratigraphy is the description of layers.
items.exampleCN: stratigraphy 就是对层的描述。

items.example: The -ic ending makes an adjective from a noun.
items.exampleCN: -ic 词尾把名词变成形容词。

items.example: Stratigraphy supplies the framework for dating.
items.exampleCN: 地层学为断代提供框架。

items.meaning: relating to layers or their order
items.example: The stratigraphic sequence is complete.
items.exampleCN: 层序是完整的。

items.meaning: the same, in a longer form
items.example: Older reports prefer the stratigraphical form.
items.exampleCN: 较早的报告更爱用 stratigraphical 形式。

items.example: The stratigrapher logged the section.
items.exampleCN: 地层专家记录了这条剖面。

items.example: Floods stratify the gravel.
items.exampleCN: 洪水使砾石分层。

definition_zh: 埋葬；葬礼；墓穴；墓葬；掩埋
definition_en: the act or ceremony of placing a dead body in the ground, or the grave and its contents considered as one archaeological unit
core_image: 几个人在土坑边低头站立，坑底铺着石板，一具裹着布的身体被缓缓放下
scene: 黄昏的土坡上，几个人站在坑边低头不语，坑底铺着石板，一具裹布的身体被缓缓放下。At dusk, the burial begins as the wrapped body is lowered onto the stone floor of the grave.
sceneCN: 这里 burial 指「把死者安置入土的仪式与行为」（第 1 个义项：埋葬的行为与葬礼过程）；句意为黄昏时人们把裹布的身体缓缓放入铺石板的墓坑。可辨识物件：墓坑、石板、裹尸布、土堆、铁锹。

pos.zh: 埋葬；葬礼
墓穴；墓葬（考古单位）
掩埋；埋藏

senses.title: The act of placing a body in the ground
senses.titleCN: 埋葬：把遗体安置入土的行为
senses.definition: the act of putting a dead body into the ground
senses.definitionCN: 把死者身体放入地下的行为
senses.example: The burial took place at dawn beside the church.
senses.exampleCN: 埋葬在黎明时分于教堂旁进行。
senses.why: Burial comes from Old English byrgan, to bury, and its noun replaced the older byrgels; the core act is covering a body with earth.
senses.whyCN: burial 出自古英语 byrgan「埋葬」，其名词形式取代了更早的 byrgels；核心动作是用土覆盖身体。

senses.title: The funeral rite
senses.titleCN: 葬礼：围绕下葬的仪式
senses.definition: the ceremony and rites that accompany the placing of a body
senses.definitionCN: 伴随遗体安置而举行的仪式与礼节
senses.example: The burial included prayers and a procession.
senses.exampleCN: 葬礼包括祈祷与送葬行列。
senses.why: Once the act is ritualised, the noun shifts from the physical placing to the ceremony that surrounds it.
senses.whyCN: 一旦这一动作仪式化，名词就从身体的安置转向围绕它的仪式。

senses.title: The grave itself
senses.titleCN: 墓穴：容纳遗体的坑或构筑
senses.definition: the pit, chamber or structure made to receive a body
senses.definitionCN: 为容纳遗体而挖的坑、建造的墓室或构筑
senses.example: The burial was lined with flat stones.
senses.exampleCN: 这座墓穴内壁铺着石板。
senses.why: Metonymy turns the event into its container: what is dug for the burial comes to be called the burial.
senses.whyCN: 转喻把事件变成容器：为埋葬而挖的东西，后来也被称作 burial。

senses.title: An archaeological burial unit
senses.titleCN: 墓葬单位：考古记录中的一个整体
senses.definition: a grave and all its contents recorded together as a single archaeological context
senses.definitionCN: 把墓穴及其全部内容作为一个考古情境一起记录
senses.example: Each burial was drawn in plan and section.
senses.exampleCN: 每处墓葬都绘制了平面图与剖面图。
senses.why: Archaeology needs countable units, so the whole grave, body and goods become one burial with a number.
senses.whyCN: 考古学需要可计数的单位，于是整个墓、遗体与随葬品成为一个带编号的 burial。

senses.title: The manner of interment
senses.titleCN: 葬式：安置遗体的具体方式
senses.definition: the way a body is laid out, such as extended, crouched, cremated or in a coffin
senses.definitionCN: 遗体的放置方式，如仰身直肢、屈肢、火化或装棺
senses.example: The crouched burial suggests an early date.
senses.exampleCN: 屈肢葬式暗示年代较早。
senses.why: The position of the body is a choice made by the survivors, so burial also names the style of that choice.
senses.whyCN: 身体的姿势是生者做出的选择，因此 burial 也指这一选择的具体样式。

senses.title: Covering something with earth
senses.titleCN: 掩埋：用土石覆盖
senses.definition: the covering of an object or surface with soil, sand or debris
senses.definitionCN: 用土、沙或碎屑覆盖物件或表面
senses.example: Rapid burial preserved the footprints.
senses.exampleCN: 迅速掩埋保存了这些脚印。
senses.why: Outside funerals the word keeps the physical sense: whatever is covered and sealed away has undergone burial.
senses.whyCN: 在殡葬之外，这个词保留物理义：凡被覆盖封存的东西都经历了 burial。

senses.title: Disposal by burying waste
senses.titleCN: 废物掩埋：以埋藏方式处置
senses.definition: the disposal of waste or hazardous material by burying it
senses.definitionCN: 把废物或危险材料埋入地下的处置方式
senses.example: The burial of chemical waste is strictly regulated.
senses.exampleCN: 化学废物的掩埋受到严格管制。
senses.why: The same covering act serves disposal, where the aim is not memory but containment.
senses.whyCN: 同一覆盖动作也服务于处置，其目的不是纪念，而是封存。

senses.title: The burying of hopes or memory
senses.titleCN: 比喻：把希望或记忆埋起来
senses.definition: used figuratively for the ending or hiding of hopes, feelings or the past
senses.definitionCN: 比喻希望、情感或往事的终结与隐藏
senses.example: The report was a burial of the old plan.
senses.exampleCN: 这份报告等于把旧计划埋掉了。
senses.why: If burial seals something away for good, then any permanent ending can borrow the image.
senses.whyCN: 如果埋葬意味着永久封存，那么任何永久性的终结都可以借用这个意象。

intro.en: Burial comes from Old English byrgels, a burying place, from byrgan, to bury, a native Germanic verb. The modern noun reshaped the older word. Dates are approximate.
intro.cn: burial 出自古英语 byrgels「埋葬之处」，源于本族日耳曼动词 byrgan「埋葬」。现代名词是在更早的词形上重塑而成。年代均为约数。

items.en: Byrgan meant to bury or to hide in the earth; it continues Proto-Germanic *burzjan, related to a root for protecting and covering.
items.cn: byrgan 意为埋葬或藏入土中；它延续原始日耳曼语 *burzjan，与表示保护、覆盖的词根相关。

items.en: Byrgels named the grave or the act of burying, built with the noun suffix -els; it was the ordinary word before burial replaced it.
items.cn: byrgels 指坟墓或埋葬行为，由名词后缀 -els 构成；在 burial 取代它之前，这是常用词。

items.en: Middle English burial appears as a remodelled noun, probably influenced by the verb bury and by Latin-derived burial terms in church usage.
items.cn: 中古英语 burial 作为重塑名词出现，可能受动词 bury 以及教会用语中拉丁来源的殡葬词影响。

items.en: Field archaeology made burial a countable unit in the twentieth century, so a single grave became a burial with a number.
items.cn: 二十世纪的田野考古把 burial 变成可数单位，于是单个墓穴成为带编号的 burial。

items.en: Source uncertain: the exact process by which burial replaced byrgels is not documented, and the deeper Indo-European connections of *burzjan are reconstructed rather than attested.
items.cn: 来源不确定：burial 取代 byrgels 的具体过程没有文献记载，*burzjan 更深的印欧语联系属重构形式，而非有据可查。

note.en: The first group holds words from the same burying stock; the second group holds terms for graves and funerals.
note.cn: 第一组是同出「埋葬」词干的词；第二组是墓葬与丧葬类的词。

entries.definition: To place in the ground; burial is the noun naming the act or its result.
entries.definitionCN: 放入土中；burial 是名词，指行为或结果。

entries.definition: Having been placed under ground; it describes the object, not the event.
entries.definitionCN: 已被置于地下；它描述物件，而非事件。

entries.definition: A place set aside for graves; burial alone names an act, a grave or a unit.
entries.definitionCN: 专用于墓葬的地点；burial 本身指行为、墓穴或单位。

entries.definition: The excavation that receives a body; it names the hole rather than the event.
entries.definitionCN: 容纳遗体的开挖坑；它指那个坑，而非事件。

entries.definition: The formal or technical word for placing a body in a grave, often used in official records.
entries.definitionCN: 把遗体放入墓穴的正式或技术说法，常用于官方记录。

entries.definition: The ceremony for the dead as a whole; burial may be one part of it or may name the rite alone.
entries.definitionCN: 为死者举行的整体仪式；burial 可以是其中一环，也可单独指仪式。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: the Old English verb, the metonymy from act to grave, the countable unit and the waste sense.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：古英语动词、由行为到墓穴的转喻、可数单位，以及废物处置义。

normal.en: byrgan, to bury, is the native verb behind both bury and burial.
normal.cn: byrgan「埋葬」是 bury 与 burial 背后的本族动词。

normal.en: Metonymy: the act of burying becomes the grave that receives the body.
normal.cn: 转喻：埋葬行为变成容纳遗体的墓穴。

normal.en: In field archaeology a burial is a numbered unit containing a body and its goods.
normal.cn: 在田野考古中，burial 是一个带编号的单位，含遗体与随葬品。

normal.en: Burial also covers ordinary burying: ash buried a town, sand buried footprints.
normal.cn: burial 也指普通掩埋：火山灰埋了城镇，沙埋了脚印。

normal.en: Waste burial aims at containment, not remembrance.
normal.cn: 废物掩埋的目的在封存，而非纪念。

abstract.en: Abstractly, burial is the act of making something inaccessible in order to preserve or to forget it.
abstract.cn: 抽象地看，burial 是为保存或为遗忘而使某物不可接近的行为。

abstract.en: The same gesture serves memory and disposal, which is why the word can be tender or technical.
abstract.cn: 同一个动作既服务记忆也服务处置，因此这个词可以温柔，也可以技术化。

abstract.en: What is buried is both protected and removed; that double effect is the whole word.
abstract.cn: 被埋之物既受保护又被移除；这一双重效果就是这个词的全部。

examples.en: The burial was excavated in the second season.
examples.cn: 这处墓葬在第二个发掘季被清理。

examples.en: Burial in the churchyard was reserved for parish members.
examples.cn: 教堂墓地的埋葬权保留给本教区成员。

examples.en: Rapid burial under ash preserved the wooden roof.
examples.cn: 火山灰下的迅速掩埋保存了木屋顶。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「bury（埋）+ al（名词）」——把人或物埋进土里的这件事 → 埋葬、墓葬

root: 古英语 byrgan「埋葬」派生的名词 byrgels「埋葬之处」，中古英语重塑为 burial；更深来源属原始日耳曼语重构形式 *burzjan。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses follow one covering: a body is placed in the earth, the rite and the grave grow around it, and then the same act covers objects, waste and finally hopes.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项沿同一次覆盖展开：身体被放入土中，仪式与墓穴随之生长，随后同一动作覆盖物件、废物，最后覆盖希望。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a wrapped body lowered onto a stone floor at dusk.
core.cn: 核心意象：黄昏时分，一具裹布的身体被放入铺石板的坑底。

branches.en: THE ACT AND THE RITE: placing the body and the ceremony around it are two faces of one event.
branches.cn: 行为与仪式：安置遗体与围绕它的仪式是同一事件的两面。

branches.en: CONTAINER AND UNIT: metonymy gives the grave, and archaeology gives it a number.
branches.cn: 容器与单位：转喻给出墓穴，考古学再给它编号。

branches.en: THE CHOSEN POSTURE: how the body is laid out records a decision by the survivors.
branches.cn: 被选定的姿势：遗体如何摆放记录了生者的决定。

branches.en: COVERING ANYTHING: earth seals objects as well as bodies, and waste burial seeks containment.
branches.cn: 覆盖任何东西：土既封存身体也封存物件，废物掩埋追求的是封存。

branches.en: THE CLOSED CHAPTER: any permanent ending can be imagined as a burial.
branches.cn: 合上的一章：任何永久终结都可以被想象为一次埋葬。

intro.en: Burial is a native English noun from a Germanic verb, with a suffix that also appears in a few old nouns.
intro.cn: burial 是由日耳曼语动词派生的英语本族名词，其词尾也出现在少数古老名词中。

latinIntro.en: There is no Latin root behind burial; the word is native. Latin-based relatives such as interment and funeral belong to a different formation and are not cognates.
latinIntro.cn: burial 背后没有拉丁词根，这个词是本族词。interment、funeral 等拉丁来源的近义词属于不同构词，并非同源。

items.example: The burial was recorded as a single unit.

items.example: The buried floor lay beneath the ash.
items.exampleCN: 被埋的居住面位于火山灰之下。

items.meaning: the act of placing under earth
items.example: Burying the dead was a community duty.
items.exampleCN: 埋葬死者曾是社群的责任。

definition_zh: 墓地；坟场；古墓葬区；埋葬场地
definition_en: an area of land set aside for graves, whether used in the present or left from an earlier period
core_image: 一片缓坡上整齐排着低矮的土丘，草被修剪过，尽头是一道矮石墙和铁门
scene: 缓坡上整齐排着低矮的土丘，草被修剪过，尽头是一道矮石墙和一扇铁门。On the burial ground, the low mounds stand in rows behind an iron gate.
sceneCN: 这里 burial ground 指「专用于墓葬的一片土地」（第 1 个义项：作为埋葬场所的地块）；句意为坡地上的低矮坟丘成排排列，铁门之后是修剪过的草地。可辨识物件：坟丘、矮墙、铁门、草地、路径。

pos.zh: 墓地；坟场；埋葬场地
（考古）古墓葬区

senses.title: Land set aside for graves
senses.titleCN: 墓地：专用于墓葬的地块
senses.definition: a piece of land reserved for burying the dead
senses.definitionCN: 保留用于埋葬死者的土地
senses.example: The village burial ground lies beyond the last house.
senses.exampleCN: 村子的墓地在最后一排房屋之外。
senses.why: Ground here is Old English grund, bottom or foundation: the phrase names land understood as a base for graves.
senses.whyCN: ground 是古英语 grund「底部、基础」：这个短语把土地理解为承载墓葬的基底。

senses.title: An ancient cemetery area
senses.titleCN: 古墓葬区：成片的古代墓葬
senses.definition: a zone containing many graves of an earlier period, treated as one archaeological area
senses.definitionCN: 包含大量更早时期墓葬、作为一个考古区域处理的地区
senses.example: The ancient burial ground was mapped before the road was built.
senses.exampleCN: 修路之前，这片古墓葬区已被测绘。
senses.why: Archaeology treats a cluster of graves as a ground rather than as isolated burials, because the grouping itself carries information.
senses.whyCN: 考古学把成组的墓当作一个「场地」而非孤立墓葬，因为分组的格局本身就携带信息。

senses.title: The burial zone inside a site
senses.titleCN: 遗址内的埋葬区：聚落中的墓葬地带
senses.definition: the part of a settlement or site where the dead were buried
senses.definitionCN: 聚落或遗址中埋葬死者的地带
senses.example: The burial ground lies outside the domestic area.
senses.exampleCN: 埋葬区位于居住区之外。
senses.why: Separating the dead from the living is itself a spatial decision, and the phrase marks that decision on the map.
senses.whyCN: 把死者与生者分开本身就是一种空间决定，这个短语把这一决定标在地图上。

senses.title: A military cemetery
senses.titleCN: 军人墓地：安葬阵亡者的场地
senses.definition: a burial ground maintained for soldiers or war dead
senses.definitionCN: 为士兵或战争死难者维护的墓地
senses.example: The military burial ground is kept by a national commission.
senses.exampleCN: 这处军人墓地由国家委员会维护。
senses.why: The phrase acquires an institutional sense when a state or army takes responsibility for the ground and its graves.
senses.whyCN: 当国家或军队承担这块土地及其墓葬的责任时，这个短语便获得制度意义。

senses.title: A place where animals are buried
senses.titleCN: 动物埋骨地：集中掩埋动物遗骸之处
senses.definition: a site where animal carcasses or bones are deliberately buried, often in large numbers
senses.definitionCN: 有意集中掩埋动物尸体或骨骼的地点
senses.example: The pit was a burial ground for livestock after the epidemic.
senses.exampleCN: 疫病之后，这个坑成了牲畜的埋骨地。
senses.why: The phrase is not limited to human dead: any deliberate, repeated burial of bodies creates a ground.
senses.whyCN: 这个短语并不限于人类死者：任何有意的、反复的尸体掩埋都会造出一处场地。

senses.title: A mass or hurried burial place
senses.titleCN: 乱葬地：集体或仓促掩埋之处
senses.definition: a place where many bodies are buried quickly, without individual graves
senses.definitionCN: 许多遗体被仓促掩埋、没有单独墓穴的地方
senses.example: The field became a burial ground after the flood.
senses.exampleCN: 洪水之后，这片田野成了乱葬地。
senses.why: When normal rites cannot keep pace with deaths, land itself becomes the container, and the phrase marks that emergency.
senses.whyCN: 当正常仪式跟不上死亡速度时，土地本身成为容器，这个短语标记的正是这种紧急状态。

senses.title: A churchyard
senses.titleCN: 教堂墓地：教堂周围的安葬地
senses.definition: the ground beside a church, consecrated and used for parish burials
senses.definitionCN: 教堂旁经祝圣、供教区埋葬之用的土地
senses.example: Her parents lie in the church burial ground.
senses.exampleCN: 她的父母安葬在教堂墓地。
senses.why: Consecration turns ordinary land into a ground with rules; the phrase then carries legal and religious weight.
senses.whyCN: 祝圣把普通土地变成有规则的场地，这个短语于是带上法律与宗教分量。

senses.title: A dumping place for discarded things
senses.titleCN: 比喻：被弃置之物的归宿
senses.definition: used figuratively for a place or field where outdated ideas or objects end up
senses.definitionCN: 比喻过时观念或物件最终被丢下的地方或领域
senses.example: That journal became a burial ground for failed theories.
senses.exampleCN: 那份期刊成了失败理论的葬身之地。
senses.why: The image of ground receiving the dead transfers easily to any place where unwanted things are deposited for good.
senses.whyCN: 土地接纳死者的意象很容易迁移到任何永久堆放废弃之物的场所。

intro.en: Burial ground joins burial, from Old English byrgan, to bury, with ground, from Old English grund, bottom or foundation. Both words are native English. Dates are approximate.
intro.cn: burial ground 把 burial（出自古英语 byrgan「埋葬」）与 ground（出自古英语 grund「底部、基础」）连在一起。两个词都是英语本族词。年代均为约数。

items.en: Grund meant the bottom or foundation of something, and it extended to the surface of the earth; English ground keeps both the depth and the surface senses.
items.cn: grund 指某物的底部或基础，也扩展到地表；英语 ground 同时保留「深处」与「表面」两义。

items.en: Byrgan meant to bury or hide in earth, and its noun forms produced the modern burial.
items.cn: byrgan 意为埋葬或藏入土中，其名词形式产生现代 burial。

items.en: The two words combine early in English usage to name land reserved for graves, as distinct from a single grave or a funeral.
items.cn: 这两个词在英语用法中很早就结合，用来指保留给墓葬的土地，以区别于单个墓穴或葬礼。

items.en: Church law gave the phrase a technical sense: consecrated ground had rules about who could be buried and where.
items.cn: 教会法赋予这个短语技术义：祝圣过的土地对谁可以葬、葬在哪里都有规定。

items.en: Source uncertain: the first written use of the exact phrase is not recorded, and the age of the compound can only be estimated from its two native parts.
items.cn: 来源不确定：这一确切短语的首次书面使用没有记录，其形成年代只能从两个本族成分来估计。

note.en: The first group holds words for places of burial; the second group holds words that name a grave or a funeral.
note.cn: 第一组是埋葬场所的词；第二组是命名墓穴或葬礼的词。

entries.definition: A modern, often landscaped place for graves; burial ground is older and can be archaeological or emergency.
entries.definitionCN: 现代常经景观设计的墓葬地；burial ground 更古老，也可指考古或紧急掩埋地。

entries.definition: The consecrated land beside a church; it is one kind of burial ground, not the whole category.
entries.definitionCN: 教堂旁经祝圣的土地；它是一种墓地，而非整个类别。

entries.definition: An older or informal word for a place of graves, often beside a church.
entries.definitionCN: 指墓葬地的较早或口语说法，常指教堂旁。

entries.definition: A single excavation for one body; a burial ground holds many graves.
entries.definitionCN: 为单具遗体挖的坑；墓地容纳许多墓穴。

entries.definition: A grand building for tombs; it is architecture, while a burial ground is land.
entries.definitionCN: 用于墓葬的宏大建筑；它是建筑，而墓地是土地。

entries.definition: A large ancient cemetery, often with monumental tombs; it stresses scale and city-like layout.
entries.definitionCN: 大型古代墓地，常带纪念性墓葬；强调规模与城市式布局。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: two native words, the consecrated churchyard, the military cemetery and the metaphorical dumping ground.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：两个本族词、祝圣的教堂墓地、军人墓地，以及比喻意义上的弃置地。

normal.en: ground is Old English grund, the base of things: a burial ground is land treated as the base of graves.
normal.cn: ground 是古英语 grund「基底」：墓地就是把土地当作墓的基底。

normal.en: burial is from byrgan, to bury: the phrase says what the land is for.
normal.cn: burial 出自 byrgan「埋葬」：这个短语说明这块地是做什么用的。

normal.en: A churchyard is a consecrated burial ground with rules about who may lie there.
normal.cn: 教堂墓地是祝圣过的墓地，对谁可葬有规定。

normal.en: Military burial grounds are maintained by states and armies rather than by families.
normal.cn: 军人墓地由国家与军队维护，而非由家庭维护。

normal.en: In metaphor the ground receives whatever a field no longer wants.
normal.cn: 在比喻中，这块地接纳某个领域不再要的一切。

abstract.en: Abstractly, a burial ground is space organised around one certainty: that the dead must go somewhere.
abstract.cn: 抽象地看，墓地是围绕一个确定事实组织起来的空间：死者总得有地方去。

abstract.en: The phrase separates the living from the dead by a boundary drawn on land.
abstract.cn: 这个短语用画在土地上的界线把生者与死者分开。

abstract.en: Any field that receives finished things becomes, in speech, a burial ground.
abstract.cn: 任何接纳已终结之物的领域，在言语中都会变成一块墓地。

examples.en: The burial ground was fenced to keep livestock out.
examples.cn: 墓地围了栏，防止牲畜进入。

examples.en: Developers were required to leave the ancient burial ground untouched.
examples.cn: 开发商被要求不动这片古墓葬区。

examples.en: The island has a small burial ground for sailors lost at sea.
examples.cn: 岛上有一小片墓地，安葬在海上失踪的水手。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「burial（埋葬）+ ground（地）」——专门用来埋葬的那块地 → 墓地

root: 古英语 byrgan「埋葬」派生的 burial + 古英语 grund「底部、土地」；字面为「用于埋葬的土地」。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses follow one piece of land: it receives graves, ancient clusters, site zones, soldiers, animals, emergency dead, parish members, and finally discarded ideas.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项沿同一块土地展开：它接纳墓穴、古代墓葬群、遗址墓葬区、军人、动物、紧急死难者、教区成员，最后接纳被弃置的观念。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: low mounds in rows on a slope, behind an iron gate.
core.cn: 核心意象：坡地上成排的低矮坟丘，铁门之后。

branches.en: ORDINARY AND CONSECRATED: the same land can be a plain cemetery or a church ground with rules.
branches.cn: 普通与祝圣：同一块地可以是普通墓地，也可以是带规则的教堂墓地。

branches.en: GROUPING AS INFORMATION: a cluster of graves becomes a zone, and its position relative to the living matters.
branches.cn: 分组即信息：成组的墓成为一个区域，它与生者的相对位置有意义。

branches.en: THE STATE TAKES CHARGE: military grounds turn burial into national maintenance.
branches.cn: 国家接管：军人墓地使埋葬变成国家维护事务。

branches.en: THE OVERFLOW: animals and disaster victims show land receiving bodies faster than rites can follow.
branches.cn: 溢出：动物与灾民显示土地接收尸体的速度超过仪式所能跟进。

branches.en: THE LAST DEPOSIT: anything finally abandoned can be said to have a burial ground.
branches.cn: 最后的堆放：任何最终被弃置的东西，都可以说有一块墓地。

intro.en: Burial ground is a native two-word compound, and neither half is Latin, so the phrase is readable from Old English alone.
intro.cn: burial ground 是本族双词复合，两半都不是拉丁来源，因此仅凭古英语就能读出这个短语。

latinIntro.en: No Latin root stands behind either half. The Latin-derived cemetery and interment are near synonyms built on different roots, so they are not cognates of this phrase.
latinIntro.cn: 两半背后都没有拉丁词根。拉丁来源的 cemetery 与 interment 是近义词，但构词词根不同，因此不是这个短语的同源词。

items.meaning: the act or place of burying
