items.meaning: the enclosed ground beside a church
items.example: The churchyard holds the oldest graves.
items.exampleCN: 教堂墓地里有最老的墓。

items.example: The new cemetery lies outside the village.
items.exampleCN: 新墓地在村外。

definition_zh: 坟墓；陵墓；墓室；葬身之处
definition_en: a grave or a built structure that holds a dead body, especially one made of stone and intended to be permanent
core_image: 一座石砌墓室嵌在山坡里，门楣上刻着名字，门内一片黑暗，外面是明亮的沙地
scene: 山坡上凿出一座石砌墓室，门楣刻着名字，门内一片黑暗，外面是明亮的沙地。Cut into the hillside, the tomb keeps its carved name above a door that opens into darkness.
sceneCN: 这里 tomb 指「容纳遗体的石造墓室或坟墓」（第 1 个义项：以构筑物形式保存遗体的墓葬）；句意为山坡里凿出的墓室门楣上刻着名字，门内昏暗，门外是明亮沙地。可辨识物件：石墓门、门楣刻字、黑暗墓室、沙地、台阶。

pos.zh: 坟墓；陵墓；墓室
葬身之处（比喻）

senses.title: A grave, especially a built one
senses.titleCN: 坟墓：尤指有构筑的墓
senses.definition: a place where a dead body is laid, typically a stone structure rather than a simple pit
senses.definitionCN: 安放遗体的地方，通常是有石造构筑的墓而非简单土坑
senses.example: The tomb was cut directly into the rock.
senses.exampleCN: 这座墓直接凿进岩石中。
senses.why: Tomb goes back through Latin tumba to Greek tymbos, a burial mound; the word began as a heap over a grave and then named the structure itself.
senses.whyCN: tomb 经拉丁 tumba 上溯希腊 tymbos「坟丘」；这个词起初指盖在墓上的土堆，后来指构筑本身。

senses.title: A grand monumental tomb
senses.titleCN: 陵墓：宏大纪念性的墓葬建筑
senses.definition: a large, often royal or public monument built to hold and honour the dead
senses.definitionCN: 为容纳并纪念死者而建的大型、常为王室或公共的纪念建筑
senses.example: The royal tomb took thirty years to build.
senses.exampleCN: 这座王陵修了三十年。
senses.why: Scale turns a grave into a monument; the word then carries architecture, ceremony and public memory at once.
senses.whyCN: 规模把坟墓变成纪念物；这个词于是同时承载建筑、仪式与公共记忆。

senses.title: The chamber inside
senses.titleCN: 墓室：容纳遗体的内部空间
senses.definition: the inner room of a tomb where the body and goods are placed
senses.definitionCN: 墓中安放遗体与随葬品的内部空间
senses.example: The tomb chamber was painted with scenes of the harvest.
senses.exampleCN: 墓室内壁绘有收获场景。
senses.why: A tomb is both shell and room, and the word shifts between the outside structure and the inside space.
senses.whyCN: 墓既是外壳也是房间，这个词在外部构筑与内部空间之间转换。

senses.title: A stone container for the dead
senses.titleCN: 石椁：包住遗体的石制容器
senses.definition: a stone coffin or enclosure that holds a body or a coffin
senses.definitionCN: 容纳遗体或棺材的石制棺椁或围护
senses.example: The body lay inside a tomb of cut stone.
senses.exampleCN: 遗体安放在一座凿石椁中。
senses.why: The boundary between a room and a container is thin: once the structure is small and closed, tomb names the box.
senses.whyCN: 房间与容器的界线很薄：一旦构筑变小并封闭，tomb 就指那只石箱。

senses.title: An archaeological tomb unit
senses.titleCN: 考古墓葬单位：作为记录对象的墓
senses.definition: a tomb recorded as one structure with its contents and construction history
senses.definitionCN: 连同内容与建造过程作为一个整体记录的墓葬构筑
senses.example: The tomb was recorded as a single unit with its shaft.
senses.exampleCN: 这座墓连同竖井被作为一个单位记录。
senses.why: Excavators need stable units, so the whole built grave, shaft and chamber become one tomb on the plan.
senses.whyCN: 发掘者需要稳定的单位，于是整座构筑墓、竖井与墓室在平面图上成为一座 tomb。

senses.title: A holy tomb
senses.titleCN: 圣陵：宗教传统中的圣者之墓
senses.definition: the tomb of a saint or prophet, often a place of pilgrimage
senses.definitionCN: 圣徒或先知之墓，常为朝圣之地
senses.example: Pilgrims came to the holy tomb for healing.
senses.exampleCN: 朝圣者来到这座圣陵求医治。
senses.why: A holy person's tomb becomes a contact point between the living and the sacred, so the structure gains a devotional role.
senses.whyCN: 圣者之墓成为生者与神圣之间的接触点，这座构筑于是获得敬礼功能。

senses.title: A single chamber in a catacomb
senses.titleCN: 地下墓穴中的单室
senses.definition: one excavated room within a network of underground galleries used for burials
senses.definitionCN: 地下墓道网络中用于埋葬的一个开凿室
senses.example: Each family tomb in the catacomb has its own niche.
senses.exampleCN: 地下墓穴中每个家族墓室都有自己的壁龛。
senses.why: Underground burial multiplies small rooms, and each room is a tomb in the countable sense.
senses.whyCN: 地下埋葬造出许多小室，每个小室都是可数意义上的 tomb。

senses.title: A place of death, figuratively
senses.titleCN: 比喻：葬身之处或死亡之地
senses.definition: used figuratively for a place or situation that ends a life, a career or a hope
senses.definitionCN: 比喻终结生命、事业或希望的地方或处境
senses.example: The valley was a tomb for the expedition.
senses.exampleCN: 这个谷地成了探险队的葬身之处。
senses.why: If a tomb is where something is finally laid to rest, then any fatal or final place can borrow the name.
senses.whyCN: 如果墓是某物最终安息之处，那么任何致命或终结性的地方都能借用这个名字。

intro.en: Tomb came into English through Old French tombe from Latin tumba, itself borrowed from Greek tymbos, a burial mound. Dates are approximate.
intro.cn: tomb 经古法语 tombe 来自拉丁 tumba，而 tumba 又借自希腊 tymbos「坟丘」。年代均为约数。

items.en: Tymbos meant a burial mound or a grave, and it is related to a Greek verb meaning to swell, because a mound is heaped up.
items.cn: tymbos 意为坟丘或坟墓，与一个意为「鼓起」的希腊动词相关，因为坟丘是堆起来的。

items.en: Latin borrowed tymbos as tumba, keeping the sense of a grave and extending it to the built structure.
items.cn: 拉丁语借入 tymbos 为 tumba，保留坟墓义，并扩展到构筑物。

items.en: Old French tombe carried the word into English after the Norman conquest, first as a grave and then as a monument.
items.cn: 古法语 tombe 在诺曼征服后把词带入英语，最初指墓，后指纪念性墓葬。

items.en: From the sixteenth century the word increasingly named large built tombs, while grave remained the plain term for a dug pit.
items.cn: 十六世纪起，这个词越来越多指大型构筑墓，而 grave 仍是普通土坑的常用词。

items.en: Source uncertain: the link between tymbos and the swelling verb is generally accepted but not certain, and the exact route through Old French dialects is not fully documented.
items.cn: 来源不确定：tymbos 与「鼓起」动词的联系一般被接受，但并非确证；经古法语各方言的具体路径也缺乏完整记载。

note.en: The first group holds words that look or sound close to tomb; the second group holds words for graves and monuments.
note.cn: 第一组是形音上与 tomb 接近的词；第二组是坟墓与纪念性建筑的词。

entries.definition: The stone that marks a tomb; the tomb is the grave or structure beneath or behind it.
entries.definitionCN: 标记墓葬的石块；tomb 是它下方或后方的墓与构筑。

entries.definition: To place in a tomb or to serve as a tomb for something; it is the action, not the structure.
entries.definitionCN: 放入墓中，或作为某物的墓；它是动作，不是构筑。

entries.definition: A burial mound, from the same Latin stock; it names the heap rather than the chamber.
entries.definitionCN: 坟丘，同出拉丁词干；它指土堆，而非墓室。

entries.definition: A dug place for a body; tomb usually implies a built or marked structure.
entries.definitionCN: 为遗体挖的坑；tomb 通常暗示有构筑或标记。

entries.definition: A large monumental building containing tombs; it is the house, while a tomb can be a single chamber.
entries.definitionCN: 容纳墓葬的大型纪念建筑；它是房屋，而 tomb 可以是单个墓室。

entries.definition: An underground vault beneath a church used for burials; it is a room within a larger building.
entries.definitionCN: 教堂下用于埋葬的地下室；它是更大建筑中的一个房间。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: the Greek mound, the Latin borrowing, the royal monument and the chamber inside.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：希腊坟丘、拉丁借词、王陵纪念建筑，以及内部墓室。

normal.en: tymbos, a mound, became Latin tumba and English tomb: the word starts as a heap over a grave.
normal.cn: tymbos「坟丘」变成拉丁 tumba 与英语 tomb：这个词起初是盖在墓上的土堆。

normal.en: A tomb can be the structure outside or the chamber inside.
normal.cn: tomb 既可以指外部构筑，也可以指内部墓室。

normal.en: Scale turns a grave into a monument, and the word then carries public memory.
normal.cn: 规模把坟墓变成纪念物，这个词于是承载公共记忆。

normal.en: A saint's tomb becomes a pilgrimage destination.
normal.cn: 圣者之墓会成为朝圣地。

normal.en: In metaphor, any fatal place can be called a tomb.
normal.cn: 在比喻中，任何致命之地都能被称为 tomb。

abstract.en: Abstractly, a tomb is architecture built around a single fact: someone is not coming back.
abstract.cn: 抽象地看，tomb 是围绕一个事实建造的建筑：有人不会再回来。

abstract.en: The word holds both container and room, both body and memory.
abstract.cn: 这个词同时容纳容器与房间、身体与记忆。

abstract.en: Every monument to the dead is also a claim by the living about status.
abstract.cn: 每一座死者纪念物，也是生者关于身份的一次主张。

examples.en: The tomb was sealed with a single massive stone.
examples.cn: 这座墓被一块巨大的石头封住。

examples.en: Paintings inside the tomb show the dead man hunting.
examples.cn: 墓内壁画描绘墓主狩猎的场景。

examples.en: The valley proved a tomb for the lost expedition.
examples.cn: 这个谷地成了失踪探险队的葬身之处。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「tomb」读音近「土墓」——用土石堆起来、封住死者的地方 → 坟墓、陵墓

root: 希腊 tymbos「坟丘」（与意为「鼓起」的动词相关）→ 拉丁 tumba → 古法语 tombe → 英语 tomb。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses follow one structure: a mound becomes a stone grave, then a royal monument, an inner chamber, a container, a recorded unit, a holy site, one room underground and finally any fatal place.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项沿同一座构筑展开：土丘变成石墓，再变成王陵、内部墓室、容器、记录单位、圣地、地下单室，最后变成任何致命之处。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a stone door cut into a hillside, a name above it, darkness behind.
core.cn: 核心意象：山坡上凿出的石墓门，门楣上有名字，门后是黑暗。

branches.en: FROM HEAP TO MONUMENT: the mound hardens into architecture and then into public statement.
branches.cn: 从土堆到纪念物：坟丘硬化成建筑，再变成公共宣示。

branches.en: ROOM AND BOX: inside the tomb is a chamber, and a small enough chamber becomes a container.
branches.cn: 房间与箱子：墓内是房间，而足够小的房间就变成容器。

branches.en: THE UNIT: excavation gives the whole structure a number and a plan.
branches.cn: 单位：发掘给整座构筑一个编号与一张平面图。

branches.en: SACRED AND UNDERGROUND: pilgrimage and catacombs multiply the forms a tomb can take.
branches.cn: 神圣与地下：朝圣与地下墓穴让墓的形式倍增。

branches.en: THE FATAL PLACE: any ending can be imagined as a tomb.
branches.cn: 致命之处：任何终结都可以被想象成一座墓。

intro.en: Tomb is a borrowed word with little internal structure in English, but its Latin and Greek ancestry connects it to a few relatives.
intro.cn: tomb 是一个借词，在英语内部结构很少，但其拉丁与希腊来历把它与少数亲属词连在一起。

latinIntro.en: Greek tymbos became Latin tumba and then English tomb; the same Latin stock gives tumulus and entomb. The Greek word is also linked to a verb for swelling.
latinIntro.cn: 希腊 tymbos 变成拉丁 tumba，再进入英语 tomb；同一拉丁词干还产生 tumulus 与 entomb。这个希腊词也与一个意为「鼓起」的动词相关。

items.meaning: a mound raised over a grave
items.example: Tymbos names the heap before it names the building.
items.exampleCN: tymbos 先指土堆，后指建筑。

items.example: Latin tumba carried the word westward.
items.exampleCN: 拉丁 tumba 把这个词带向西方。

items.example: Old French tombe entered English after the Conquest.
items.exampleCN: 古法语 tombe 在征服之后进入英语。

items.structure: tomb (English noun, from Old French tombe)
items.meaning: a grave or built burial structure
items.example: The tomb was cut into the rock.
items.exampleCN: 这座墓凿入岩石。

items.meaning: the stone that marks a tomb
items.example: The tombstone carries a name and a date.
items.exampleCN: 墓碑刻着姓名与日期。

items.structure: en- (in) + tomb (to put in a tomb)
items.example: The body was entombed beneath the floor.
items.exampleCN: 遗体被葬在地面之下。

items.meaning: the act of placing in a tomb
items.example: The entombment was recorded in the parish book.
items.exampleCN: 入葬记录在教区簿册中。

items.example: The tumulus covers several graves.
items.exampleCN: 这座坟丘覆盖着数座墓。

items.example: The tombal inscription is worn away.
items.exampleCN: 墓上的铭文已磨损。

definition_zh: 墓碑；墓石；碑文；（数据库中的）删除标记
definition_en: a stone set at a grave to mark it and carry the dead person's name, or, in computing, a marker that records a deleted item
core_image: 一块半埋的灰色石板立在草丛里，上面刻着姓名、两个年份和一行小字，字口里积着尘土
scene: 草丛里立着一块半埋的灰色石板，上面刻着姓名、两个年份和一行小字，字口里积着尘土。Half sunk in grass, the tombstone still carries a name, two years and a line worn thin by weather.
sceneCN: 这里 tombstone 指「立在墓前、刻有姓名与年份以标记墓位的石板」（第 1 个义项：作为墓位标识的立石）；句意为草丛中的石板半埋，上面仍可读出姓名、两个年份与一行被风雨磨薄的字。可辨识物件：石板、刻字、草丛、土堆、苔痕。

pos.zh: 墓碑；墓石
（计算机）删除标记；墓碑记录

senses.title: A stone that marks a grave
senses.titleCN: 墓碑：标记墓位的立石
senses.definition: a stone placed at a grave to identify the person buried there
senses.definitionCN: 立在墓前以标明所葬之人的石块
senses.example: The tombstone records her name and the year of her death.
senses.exampleCN: 墓碑记着她的姓名与去世年份。
senses.why: Tombstone is a plain compound of tomb and stone: a stone whose job is to mark a tomb and keep a name visible.
senses.whyCN: tombstone 是 tomb 与 stone 的朴素复合：一块以标记墓、让名字保持可见为职责的石头。

senses.title: A flat slab over the grave
senses.titleCN: 墓石：覆盖墓穴的平石板
senses.definition: a flat stone laid horizontally over a grave rather than standing upright
senses.definitionCN: 横铺在墓穴上、而非竖立的石板
senses.example: The tombstone lies flat and has lost its edges.
senses.exampleCN: 这块墓石平铺着，边缘已经磨圆。
senses.why: Not every marker stands; a slab seals the grave as well as labels it, and the same word covers both jobs.
senses.whyCN: 并非所有标记都竖立；石板既封住墓穴又标明它，同一个词涵盖这两项功能。

senses.title: The inscription on the stone
senses.titleCN: 碑文：石上刻写的文字
senses.definition: the carved text on a grave stone, including name, dates and a short message
senses.definitionCN: 墓石上刻的文字，含姓名、年代与简短语句
senses.example: The tombstone reads simply that he loved the sea.
senses.exampleCN: 碑文只写着他爱海。
senses.why: Metonymy again: the marker and the message share one word, because the stone exists to carry the words.
senses.whyCN: 又是转喻：标记与文字共用一个词，因为石头存在的目的就是承载文字。

senses.title: A grave marker in a record
senses.titleCN: 墓位标记：登记系统中的标识
senses.definition: the marker or entry that identifies a grave in a cemetery register or on a plan
senses.definitionCN: 在墓地登记册或平面图上标识某个墓穴的标记或条目
senses.example: The plan uses a tombstone symbol for each plot.
senses.exampleCN: 平面图用墓碑符号标出每个墓位。
senses.why: Administration needs symbols, so a small drawn stone can stand for a grave in a register.
senses.whyCN: 管理需要符号，于是一个画出来的小石碑就能在登记册中代表一处墓穴。

senses.title: A mason's carved product
senses.titleCN: 石作成品：石匠制作的碑石
senses.definition: the worked stone as a product of cutting, lettering and finishing
senses.definitionCN: 作为切割、刻字与打磨之成品的加工石
senses.example: The mason delivered the tombstone in two weeks.
senses.exampleCN: 石匠两周后交付了这块墓碑。
senses.why: Looking at the craft, the word names a manufactured object with a trade behind it, not a memorial act.
senses.whyCN: 从工艺角度看，这个词指一件背后有行业支撑的制成品，而不是一次纪念行为。

senses.title: A genealogical marker
senses.titleCN: 族谱标记：家谱研究中的墓石信息
senses.definition: the stone as a source of birth, death, marriage and family data for genealogy
senses.definitionCN: 作为家谱研究中性、婚、死亡与家族数据来源的墓石
senses.example: Genealogists photographed every tombstone in the parish.
senses.exampleCN: 家谱研究者拍下了教区内的每一块墓碑。
senses.why: A stone is also a document: dates and relationships carved in it can be read as records when paper is missing.
senses.whyCN: 石头也是一份文件：纸上记录缺失时，刻在上面的日期与关系可以被当作档案来读。

senses.title: A sign that something has ended
senses.titleCN: 比喻：某事物终结的标志
senses.definition: used figuratively for a visible sign that a project, era or person is finished
senses.definitionCN: 比喻某项目、时代或人物已经结束的可见标志
senses.example: The empty factory is a tombstone for the old industry.
senses.exampleCN: 那座空工厂是旧工业的墓碑。
senses.why: A marker tells later visitors who lies here; applied to an ended enterprise, the image says the same thing about an era.
senses.whyCN: 标记告诉后来者这里躺着谁；用于终结的事业，这个意象对某个时代说了同一件事。

senses.title: A deletion marker in computing
senses.titleCN: 删除标记：数据库与分布式系统中的墓碑记录
senses.definition: a small record that marks an item as deleted so that the deletion can propagate and be respected
senses.definitionCN: 把某项标记为已删除、以便删除状态能传播并被遵守的小记录
senses.example: The tombstone prevents the deleted entry from reappearing.
senses.exampleCN: 这条删除标记防止已删条目重新出现。
senses.why: In distributed systems an absent item cannot be distinguished from an item never seen, so a tombstone is left in its place like a stone over an empty grave.
senses.whyCN: 在分布式系统中，缺失的条目与从未出现的条目无法区分，因此要在原处留一块「墓碑」，如同空墓上的石碑。

intro.en: Tombstone is a native compound of tomb, borrowed from Greek through Latin and French, and stone, from Old English stan. The computing sense is a modern metaphor. Dates are approximate.
intro.cn: tombstone 是 tomb 与 stone 构成的本族复合词；tomb 经拉丁与法语借自希腊语，stone 出自古英语 stan。计算机义是现代的比喻延伸。年代均为约数。

items.en: Stan meant stone or rock and continues Proto-Germanic *stainaz; it builds stone, stony, cornerstone and tombstone.
items.cn: stan 意为石头或岩石，延续原始日耳曼语 *stainaz；它构成 stone、stony、cornerstone、tombstone。

items.en: Tomb arrived through Latin tumba and Old French tombe from Greek tymbos, a burial mound, keeping the sense of a marked grave.
items.cn: tomb 经拉丁 tumba 与古法语 tombe 来自希腊 tymbos「坟丘」，保留「有标记的墓」这一义。

items.en: English joined the two words to name the stone that marks a grave, a plain descriptive compound rather than a borrowed phrase.
items.cn: 英语把两个词连起来，指标记墓穴的石头；这是朴素的描述性复合，而非借来的短语。

items.en: In the late twentieth century distributed databases borrowed the image: a deleted record leaves a marker that says an entry once existed here.
items.cn: 二十世纪后期，分布式数据库借用了这个意象：被删除的记录留下一个标记，说明此处曾有条目。

items.en: Source uncertain: the first written use of tombstone is not precisely dated, and the date when the computing sense entered general technical use is also approximate.
items.cn: 来源不确定：tombstone 的首次书面使用没有确切年代，计算机义进入一般技术用语的年代也只是约数。

note.en: The first group holds words for the same stone under other names; the second group holds markers and memorial objects.
note.cn: 第一组是同一块石头的其他名称；第二组是标记与纪念物类词。

entries.definition: The common synonym for the stone at a grave; tombstone is slightly older and also has the computing sense.
entries.definitionCN: 墓前石块的常用同义词；tombstone 略古，并且还有计算机义。

entries.definition: Specifically the upright stone at the head of a grave; a tombstone may also lie flat.
entries.definitionCN: 特指立在墓首的竖石；tombstone 也可以是平铺的。

entries.definition: The grave or structure; the stone is only its marker.
entries.definitionCN: 坟墓或构筑；石碑只是它的标记。

entries.definition: A plate bearing text fixed to a wall or monument; it marks rather than covers a grave.
entries.definitionCN: 固定在墙或纪念物上的文字牌；它标记，而不覆盖墓穴。

entries.definition: Anything built or kept to remember the dead; a tombstone is one small form of memorial.
entries.definitionCN: 为纪念死者而建或保存的任何东西；墓碑是纪念物的一种小形式。

entries.definition: The words inscribed on a tomb, not the stone that carries them.
entries.definitionCN: 刻在墓上的文字，而非承载文字的石块。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: the two native halves, the upright and flat forms, the inscription and the database metaphor.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：两个本族成分、竖立与平铺两种形式、铭文，以及数据库比喻。

normal.en: tomb plus stone: the word simply says what the object is.
normal.cn: tomb 加 stone：这个词直接说明物件是什么。

normal.en: A tombstone may stand at the head of a grave or lie flat over it.
normal.cn: 墓碑可以立在墓首，也可以平铺在墓上。

normal.en: The stone is also a document: names and dates can be read when paper is lost.
normal.cn: 石头也是文件：纸面记录丢失时，姓名与年代仍可读。

normal.en: Metonymy lets tombstone name the inscription as well as the slab.
normal.cn: 转喻使 tombstone 既指石板，也指碑文。

normal.en: In databases a tombstone is a marker left where a deleted record used to be.
normal.cn: 在数据库中，tombstone 是留在被删记录原处的标记。

abstract.en: Abstractly, a tombstone is information made durable in the hardest available material.
abstract.cn: 抽象地看，墓碑是把信息固定在可得的最硬材料上。

abstract.en: It answers one question for strangers: who was here.
abstract.cn: 它为陌生人回答一个问题：这里曾是谁。

abstract.en: The computing sense shows how far the image travels: a deleted record also needs a stone.
abstract.cn: 计算机义显示这个意象走得多远：被删除的记录也需要一块石碑。

examples.en: The tombstone was cleaned so the lettering could be read again.
examples.cn: 墓碑经过清理，字迹又能辨认了。

examples.en: A simple tombstone marks the grave of the unknown sailor.
examples.cn: 一块朴素的墓碑标记着那位无名水手的墓。

examples.en: The system writes a tombstone so that the deletion reaches every copy.
examples.cn: 系统写入一条删除标记，使删除状态传到每一份副本。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「tomb（墓）+ stone（石）」——墓前那块刻字的石头 → 墓碑

root: tomb（希腊 tymbos「坟丘」经拉丁 tumba、古法语 tombe）+ 古英语 stan「石头」；字面为「墓前的石头」。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses follow one slab: it marks a grave, covers it, carries words, enters registers, comes from a mason, feeds genealogy, stands for an ending and even marks a deleted record.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项沿同一块石板展开：它标记墓、覆盖墓、承载文字、进入登记册、出自石匠、供家谱研究、象征终结，甚至标记被删除的记录。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a weathered slab in grass, its cut letters filled with dust.
core.cn: 核心意象：草丛中一块风化的石板，刻字的凹槽里积着尘土。

branches.en: THE WORKED STONE: craft produces the slab, and placing it turns a product into a marker.
branches.cn: 加工之石：工艺造出石板，安放它则把产品变成标记。

branches.en: THE COVER: a flat slab seals the grave as well as naming it.
branches.cn: 覆盖：平石板既封住墓穴，也命名它。

branches.en: WORDS AND SYMBOLS: the inscription and the register entry both make the stone readable as information.
branches.cn: 文字与符号：铭文与登记条目都让石头可作为信息来读。

branches.en: THE LONG RECORD: genealogy reads dates from the stone, and metaphor reads an ending from it.
branches.cn: 长久的记录：家谱从石上读日期，比喻从石上读终结。

branches.en: THE DIGITAL STONE: a deletion marker repeats the gesture in a system where absence needs a sign.
branches.cn: 数字之石：删除标记在「缺席需要符号」的系统里重演同一动作。

intro.en: Tombstone is a plain two-word compound whose halves are both readable, which makes the word unusually transparent.
intro.cn: tombstone 是朴素的双词复合，两半都可读，因此这个词异常透明。

latinIntro.en: The stone half is native English, from Old English stan; the tomb half reached English through Latin tumba from Greek tymbos. No single Latin verb stands behind the compound.
latinIntro.cn: stone 一半是英语本族词，出自古英语 stan；tomb 一半经拉丁 tumba 来自希腊 tymbos。这个复合词背后没有单一拉丁动词。

items.example: Stan is the source of modern stone.
items.exampleCN: stan 是现代 stone 的来源。

items.structure: stone (English noun, from Old English stan)

items.exampleCN: 这块石头由手工切割并刻字。

items.structure: tomb (English noun, from Greek tymbos via Latin and French)
items.meaning: a grave or built burial structure
items.example: The tomb lies beneath the slab.
items.exampleCN: 墓就在石板之下。

items.example: The tombstone bears two dates.
items.exampleCN: 墓碑上刻着两个年份。

items.example: Gravestone is the commoner everyday word.
items.exampleCN: gravestone 是更常用的日常说法。

items.meaning: the stone standing at the head of a grave
items.example: The headstone faces east.
items.exampleCN: 这块墓碑朝东。

items.meaning: the first stone of a building
items.example: Cornerstone shows the same stone-building pattern.
items.exampleCN: cornerstone 显示同样的「石+构件」构词模式。

items.example: The stonemason carved the letters.
items.exampleCN: 石匠刻下了这些字母。
